# calendar

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/calendar/

The Jalali, Hijri and Gregorian calendars: conversion, day arithmetic, month names and time zones.

This package works with three calendars: Jalali (Solar Hijri, the official calendar of Iran and Afghanistan), Hijri (lunar) and Gregorian. A date is a plain struct of year, month and day, and each calendar has its own conversion, validation, day arithmetic and month name functions.

The Hijri calendar here is arithmetic: months alternate between 30 and 29 days and are not adjusted by sighting the moon, so a date can be one day off from the official calendar of a given country.

There are three ways to turn an instant into a date: `EpochToJalali` and its siblings use the machine local time, `WallClockJalali` takes a fixed time zone such as Tehran, and `LoadZone` covers zones that observe daylight saving.

## Types

### `Zone`

```salam
struct Zone
```

A full time zone from the zone database (tzdata), with its history of offsets and daylight saving.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = "UTC"` | The zone name. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Whether the zone loaded. |
| `type_offset` | `Vector` | The offset of each time type, in seconds. |
| `type_isdst` | `Vector` | Whether each type is daylight saving. |
| `type_abbrev` | `Vector` | The abbreviation of each type, such as EST. |
| `times` | `Vector` | The instants at which the offset changes. |
| `type_at` | `Vector` | The time type in force after each change. |
| `base_type` | `int = 0` | The type in force before the first change. |
| `rule` | `PosixTZ` | The POSIX rule for the years after the last recorded change. |

calendar-Zone.salam

```salam
import calendar

func main:
    mut z := calendar.LoadZone("America/New_York")
    println z.name, z.ok
    winter := 1704067200
    summer := 1719792000
    println calendar.ZoneOffsetMinutes(z, winter), calendar.ZoneOffsetMinutes(z, summer), calendar.ZoneOffsetSeconds(z, summer)
    println calendar.ZoneIsDST(z, winter), calendar.ZoneIsDST(z, summer)
    println calendar.ZoneAbbrevAt(z, winter), calendar.ZoneAbbrevAt(z, summer)
    tz := calendar.TimeZoneAt(z, summer)
    println tz.name, tz.offset_minutes
    println calendar.ZoneAt("Asia/Tehran", winter).offset_minutes
    e := calendar.ZonedToEpoch(calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 6, day = 30 }, calendar.ClockTime { hour = 20 }, z)
    println e == summer
    calendar.FreeZone(z)
    println calendar.LoadZone("Mars/Olympus").ok
    mut l := calendar.LocalZone()
    println l.ok or not l.ok
    calendar.FreeZone(l)
end
```

Output:

```text
America/New_York true
-300 -240 -14400
false true
EST EDT
EDT -240
210
true
false
true
```

### `GregorianDate`

```salam
struct GregorianDate
```

A Gregorian date.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `year` | `int = 1970` | The year. |
| `month` | `int = 1` | The month, from 1. |
| `day` | `int = 1` | The day of the month, from 1. |

calendar-Convert.salam

```salam
import calendar

func main:
    g := calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 3, day = 20 }
    j := calendar.GregorianToJalali(g)
    h := calendar.GregorianToHijri(g)
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(g), calendar.FormatJalali(j), calendar.FormatHijri(h)
    println calendar.FormatJalaliLongFa(j)
    println calendar.FormatHijriLongFa(h)
    println calendar.FormatHijriLongAr(h)
    println calendar.FormatGregorianLongEn(g)
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.JalaliToGregorian(calendar.JalaliDate { year = 1403, month = 1, day = 1 }))
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.HijriToGregorian(calendar.HijriDate { year = 1445, month = 9, day = 1 }))
    println calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.JalaliToHijri(j)), calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.HijriToJalali(h))
    d := calendar.GregorianToJDN(g)
    println d, calendar.JalaliToJDN(j), calendar.HijriToJDN(h)
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.JDNToGregorian(d + 1)), calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.JDNToJalali(d + 1)), calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.JDNToHijri(d + 1))
end
```

### `ClockTime`

```salam
struct ClockTime
```

A time of day.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hour` | `int = 0` | The hour, 0 to 23. |
| `minute` | `int = 0` | The minute. |
| `second` | `int = 0` | The second. |

calendar-Epoch.salam

```salam
import calendar
import time

func main:
    t := 1710943509
    zone := calendar.TZLocal(t)
    g := calendar.EpochToGregorian(t)
    println calendar.CompareGregorian(g, calendar.WallClockGregorian(t, zone)) == 0
    println calendar.CompareJalali(calendar.EpochToJalali(t), calendar.WallClockJalali(t, zone)) == 0
    println calendar.CompareHijri(calendar.EpochToHijri(t), calendar.WallClockHijri(t, zone)) == 0
    println calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.EpochToClockTime(t)) == calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.WallClockTime(t, zone))
    j := calendar.JalaliDate { year = 1403, month = 1, day = 1 }
    println calendar.JalaliToUnixUTC(j, 14, 5, 9) == t
    println calendar.GregorianToUnixUTC(calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 3, day = 20 }, 14, 5, 9)
    println calendar.HijriToUnixUTC(calendar.HijriDate { year = 1445, month = 9, day = 10 }, 0, 0, 0)
    println calendar.CompareGregorian(calendar.TodayGregorian(), calendar.EpochToGregorian(time.Now())) >= 0, calendar.TodayGregorian().year >= 2024, calendar.TodayJalali().year >= 1403, calendar.TodayHijri().year >= 1445
    c := calendar.NowClockTime()
    println c.hour < 24, c.minute < 60, c.second < 61
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true
true
true
true
1710943509
1710892800
true true true true
true true true
```

### `TimeZone`

```salam
struct TimeZone
```

A time zone with a fixed offset from UTC.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = "UTC"` | The zone name, such as `Asia/Tehran`. |
| `offset_minutes` | `int = 0` | The offset from UTC in minutes; 210 for Tehran. |

calendar-TimeZone.salam

```salam
import calendar

func main:
    t := 1710943509
    tehran := calendar.TZTehran()
    println tehran.name, tehran.offset_minutes
    println calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.WallClockJalali(t, tehran)), calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.WallClockTime(t, tehran))
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.WallClockGregorian(t, calendar.TZTokyo())), calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.WallClockTime(t, calendar.TZTokyo()))
    println calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.WallClockHijri(t, calendar.TZMecca()))
    each zone in [calendar.TZUTC(), calendar.TZKabul(), calendar.TZRiyadh(), calendar.TZDubai(), calendar.TZIstanbul(), calendar.TZLondon(), calendar.TZNewYork()]:
        println zone.name, zone.offset_minutes, calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.WallClockTime(t, zone))
    end
    g := calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 3, day = 20 }
    c := calendar.ClockTime { hour = 23, minute = 0, second = 0 }
    println calendar.ZonedGregorianToEpoch(g, c, tehran)
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.ConvertZonedGregorian(g, c, tehran, calendar.TZTokyo())), calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.ConvertZonedTime(g, c, tehran, calendar.TZTokyo()))
    fixed := calendar.FixedOffsetZone("UTC+05:30", 330)
    println fixed.name, calendar.FormatClockTime(calendar.WallClockTime(t, fixed))
    local := calendar.TZLocal(t)
    println local.name, local.offset_minutes == calendar.LocalOffsetMinutes(t)
end
```

Output:

```text
Asia/Tehran 210
1403-01-01 17:35:09
2024-03-20 23:05:09
1445-09-10
UTC 0 14:05:09
Asia/Kabul 270 18:35:09
Asia/Riyadh 180 17:05:09
Asia/Dubai 240 18:05:09
Europe/Istanbul 180 17:05:09
Europe/London 0 14:05:09
America/New_York -300 09:05:09
1710963000
2024-03-21 04:30:00
UTC+05:30 19:35:09
Local true
```

### `JalaliToJDN`


### `IsLeapJalali`

```salam
func IsLeapJalali(year: int): bool
```

True when the Jalali year is a leap year, meaning Esfand has 30 days.

calendar-Jalali.salam

```salam
import calendar

func main:
    println calendar.IsLeapJalali(1403), calendar.IsLeapJalali(1404), calendar.DaysInJalaliYear(1403)
    println calendar.DaysInJalaliMonth(1403, 1), calendar.DaysInJalaliMonth(1403, 7), calendar.DaysInJalaliMonth(1403, 12), calendar.DaysInJalaliMonth(1404, 12)
    println calendar.IsValidJalaliDate(1404, 12, 30), calendar.IsValidJalaliDate(1403, 12, 30)
    println calendar.JalaliMonthNameFa(1), calendar.JalaliMonthNameEn(1), calendar.JalaliMonthNameFa(12)
    j := calendar.JalaliDate { year = 1403, month = 6, day = 31 }
    d := calendar.JalaliToJDN(j)
    println calendar.JalaliWeekday(d), calendar.JalaliWeekdayNameFa(calendar.JalaliWeekday(d))
    println calendar.WeekdayJalali(j), calendar.WeekdayNameFa(calendar.WeekdayJalali(j))
    println calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.AddDaysJalali(j, 1)), calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.AddWeeksJalali(j, 2))
    println calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.AddMonthsJalali(j, 1)), calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.AddYearsJalali(j, -1))
    println calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.StartOfMonthJalali(j)), calendar.FormatJalali(calendar.EndOfMonthJalali(calendar.AddMonthsJalali(j, 6)))
    nowruz := calendar.JalaliDate { year = 1404, month = 1, day = 1 }
    println calendar.DaysBetweenJalali(j, nowruz), calendar.CompareJalali(j, nowruz), calendar.CompareJalali(nowruz, nowruz)
end
```

Output:

```text
true false 366
31 30 30 29
false true
فروردین Farvardin اسفند
0 شنبه
6 شنبه
1403-07-01 1403-07-14
1403-07-30 1402-06-31
1403-06-01 1403-12-30
181 -1 0
```

### `IsLeapGregorian`

```salam
func IsLeapGregorian(year: int): bool
```

True when the Gregorian year is a leap year.

calendar-Gregorian.salam

```salam
import calendar

func main:
    println calendar.IsLeapGregorian(2024), calendar.IsLeapGregorian(1900), calendar.DaysInGregorianYear(2024)
    println calendar.DaysInGregorianMonth(2024, 2), calendar.DaysInGregorianMonth(2023, 2), calendar.IsValidGregorianDate(2023, 2, 29)
    g := calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 1, day = 31 }
    w := calendar.WeekdayGregorian(g)
    println w, calendar.WeekdayNameEn(w), calendar.WeekdayNameFa(w), calendar.WeekdayNameAr(w)
    println calendar.Weekday(calendar.GregorianToJDN(g)), calendar.GregorianMonthNameEn(1)
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.AddMonthsGregorian(g, 1)), calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.AddYearsGregorian(calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 2, day = 29 }, 1))
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.AddDaysGregorian(g, 30)), calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.AddWeeksGregorian(g, -1))
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.StartOfMonthGregorian(g)), calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.EndOfMonthGregorian(calendar.AddMonthsGregorian(g, 1)))
    println calendar.FormatGregorian(calendar.NextWeekdayOnOrAfter(g, 5))
    year_end := calendar.GregorianDate { year = 2024, month = 12, day = 31 }
    println calendar.DaysBetweenGregorian(g, year_end), calendar.CompareGregorian(year_end, g)
end
```

Output:

```text

29 28 false
3 Wednesday چهارشنبه الأربعاء
3 January
2024-02-29 2025-02-28
2024-03-01 2024-01-24
2024-01-01 2024-02-29
2024-02-02
335 1
```

```salam
import calendar

func main:
    h := calendar.HijriDate { year = 1445, month = 9, day = 29 }
    println calendar.IsLeapHijri(1445), calendar.IsLeapHijri(1446)
    println calendar.DaysInHijriMonth(1445, 9), calendar.DaysInHijriMonth(1445, 12), calendar.DaysInHijriMonth(1446, 12)
    println calendar.IsValidHijriDate(1445, 9, 30), calendar.IsValidHijriDate(1445, 10, 30)
    println calendar.HijriMonthNameFa(9), calendar.HijriMonthNameAr(9), calendar.HijriMonthNameEn(9)
    println calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.AddDaysHijri(h, 1)), calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.AddWeeksHijri(h, 1))
    println calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.AddMonthsHijri(h, 3)), calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.AddYearsHijri(h, 1))
    println calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.StartOfMonthHijri(h)), calendar.FormatHijri(calendar.EndOfMonthHijri(h))
    muharram := calendar.HijriDate { year = 1446, month = 1, day = 1 }
    println calendar.DaysBetweenHijri(h, muharram), calendar.CompareHijri(h, muharram)
    println calendar.WeekdayNameFa(calendar.WeekdayHijri(h))
end
```

Output:

```text
true false
30 30 29
true false
رمضان رمضان Ramadan
1445-09-30 1445-10-06
1445-12-29 1446-09-29
1445-09-01 1445-09-30
91 -1
دوشنبه
```

# thread

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/thread/

Holding and waiting for the threads that `spawn` creates.

In Salam you start a function that should run alongside the rest of the program with `spawn`. It takes a function with no parameters and no result and gives back a number, the thread's handle. `join`, or `thread.Join`, waits for that thread to finish.

The `thread` package wraps that handle in a `Thread` so you can keep several of them in a vector and wait for all of them at once. Threads share the program's globals; for shared data use sync or atomic.

## Types

### `Thread`

```salam
struct Thread
```

A thread, running or finished.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `i64 = 0` | The handle `spawn` returned; zero means invalid. |

thread-Join.salam

```salam
import thread
import sync

mut total := 0
mut lock := sync.Mutex {}

func worker():
    repeat 1000:
        sync.Lock(lock)
        total += 1
        sync.Unlock(lock)
    end
end

func main:
    lock = sync.NewMutex()
    first := thread.New(spawn(worker))
    println thread.Valid(first), thread.Handle(first) != 0
    mut group := Vector {} as Vector<thread.Thread>
    defer group.free()
    repeat 3:
        group = thread.Collect(group, spawn(worker))
    end
    thread.Join(first)
    thread.JoinAll(group)
    println group.len(), total
    empty := thread.New(0)
    println thread.Valid(empty), empty.handle
    thread.Join(empty)
    sync.Destroy(lock)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
3 4000
false 0
```

## Functions

### `New`

```salam
func New(h: i64): Thread
```

Wraps a `spawn` handle in a `Thread`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: thread-Join.salam

### `SpawnStack`

```salam
func SpawnStack(fn: i64, arg: void*, stack: u64): Thread
```

Starts a function on a new thread with a stack of the size you give, in bytes, for work that needs more than the default, such as deep recursion. The function takes a `void*` and returns nothing. If the system cannot give that stack it returns an invalid handle, so check with `Valid`.

thread-SpawnStack.salam

```salam
import thread

mut total := 0 as i64

func count(n: i64): i64:
    if n <= 0:
        ret 0
    end
    ret 1 + count(n - 1)
end

func work(_arg: void*):
    total = count(200000)
end

func main:
    stack := (64 * 1024 * 1024) as u64
    t := thread.SpawnStack(work, null, stack)
    println thread.Valid(t)
    thread.Join(t)
    println total
end
```

Output:

```text
true
200000
```

### `Join`

```salam
func Join(t: Thread)
```

Waits for the thread to finish. It does nothing for an invalid thread.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: thread-Join.salam

### `JoinAll`

```salam
func JoinAll(threads: Vector<Thread>)
```

Waits for every thread in a vector to finish.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: thread-Join.salam

### `Valid`

```salam
func Valid(t: Thread): bool
```

True when the handle is not zero.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: thread-Join.salam

### `Handle`

```salam

```

The thread's handle.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: thread-Join.salam

### `Collect`

```salam

```

Adds a new thread with this handle to a vector and returns the vector.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: thread-Join.salam

# sync

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/sync/

Mutexes, condition variables, wait groups, read-write locks, semaphores and once, for coordinating threads.

When several threads change the same variable they have to take turns, or the result depends on the order the threads happen to run in. A mutex is the simplest answer: each thread takes the lock before touching the data and releases it afterwards.

A wait group is for waiting until several pieces of work are done: call `Add` before starting them, `Done` at the end of each, and `Wait` on the main thread. Every tool in this package is created with a `New...` function and released with a `Destroy...` one.

## Types

### `Mutex`

```salam
struct Mutex
```

A mutex; only one thread holds it at a time.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The operating system's lock. |

sync-Mutex.salam

```salam
import sync

mut balance := 0
mut lock := sync.Mutex {}
mut group := sync.WaitGroup {}

func deposit():
    repeat 500:
        sync.Lock(lock)
        balance += 1
        sync.Unlock(lock)
    end
    sync.Done(group)
end

func main:
    lock = sync.NewMutex()
    group = sync.NewWaitGroup()
    sync.Wait(group)
    sync.Add(group, 4)
    a := spawn(deposit)
    b := spawn(deposit)
    c := spawn(deposit)
    d := spawn(deposit)
    sync.Wait(group)
    join(a)
    join(b)
    join(c)
    join(d)
    println "balance:", balance
    sync.DestroyWaitGroup(group)
    sync.Destroy(lock)
end
```

Output:

```text
balance: 2000
```

### `CondVar`

```salam
struct CondVar
```

A condition variable: threads sleep on it until another thread wakes them.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The operating system's condition variable. |

sync-CondVar.salam

```salam
import sync

mut ready := false
mut lock := sync.Mutex {}
mut cond := sync.CondVar {}

func producer():
    sync.SleepMs(20)
    sync.Lock(lock)
    ready = true
    sync.Broadcast(cond)
    sync.Unlock(lock)
end

func main:
    lock = sync.NewMutex()
    cond = sync.NewCondVar()
    start := sync.NowMs()
    sync.Lock(lock)
    println sync.WaitCondTimeout(cond, lock, 10)
    t := spawn(producer)
    until not ready:
        sync.WaitCond(cond, lock)
    end
    sync.Unlock(lock)
    join(t)
    println ready, sync.NowMs() - start >= 20
    sync.Signal(cond)
    sync.DestroyCondVar(cond)
    sync.Destroy(lock)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true true
```

### `WaitGroup`

```salam
struct WaitGroup
```

A wait group: a count of unfinished work.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `counter` | `i64*` | The number of unfinished pieces of work. |
| `mu` | `void*` | The internal lock. |
| `cv` | `void*` | The internal condition variable. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: sync-Mutex.salam

### `RWMutex`

```salam
struct RWMutex
```

A read-write lock: several readers together, or one writer alone.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `i64*` | The internal state: the readers, the writer and the waiting writers. |
| `mu` | `void*` | The internal lock. |
| `cv` | `void*` | The internal condition variable. |

sync-RWMutex.salam

```salam
import sync

func main:
    rw := sync.NewRWMutex()
    sync.RLock(rw)
    sync.RLock(rw)
    println "two readers together"
    sync.RUnlock(rw)
    sync.RUnlock(rw)
    sync.WLock(rw)
    println "one writer alone"
    sync.WUnlock(rw)
    sync.DestroyRWMutex(rw)

    sem := sync.NewSemaphore(2)
    sync.Acquire(sem)
    println sync.TryAcquire(sem), sync.TryAcquire(sem)
    sync.Release(sem)
    println sync.TryAcquire(sem)
    sync.DestroySemaphore(sem)

    once := sync.NewOnce()
    repeat 3:
        sync.Do(once, (): println "only once" end)
    end
    sync.DestroyOnce(once)
end
```

Output:

```text
two readers together
one writer alone
true false
true
only once
```

### `Semaphore`

```salam
struct Semaphore
```

A semaphore: a limited number of permits that threads take and give back.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permits` | `i64*` | The number of free permits. |
| `mu` | `void*` | The internal lock. |
| `cv` | `void*` | The internal condition variable. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: sync-RWMutex.salam

### `Once`

```salam
struct Once
```

A "once": it runs a function only the first time.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `done` | `i64*` | Whether the function has run. |
| `mu` | `void*` | The internal lock. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: sync-RWMutex.salam

# atomic

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/atomic/

A counter and a flag that several threads can change safely without taking a lock by hand.

For a simple counter that several threads increment, you do not have to build a lock yourself: `I64` in this package does each operation in one indivisible step. `CompareAndSwap` is the base of most lock-free algorithms: it changes the value only if it is still the one you expected.

In the current implementation each cell is protected by a small lock, so it is correct, but no faster than the processor's atomic instructions.

## Types

### `I64`

```salam
struct I64
```

A 64-bit whole number shared between threads.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cell` | `i64*` | The address of the value. |
| `mu` | `sync.Mutex` | The internal lock. |

atomic-I64.salam

```salam
import atomic

mut counter := atomic.I64 {}

func worker():
    repeat 1000:
        atomic.Add(counter, 1)
    end
end

func main:
    counter = atomic.NewI64(0)
    a := spawn(worker)
    b := spawn(worker)
    join(a)
    join(b)
    println atomic.Load(counter)
    atomic.Store(counter, 10)
    println atomic.Swap(counter, 20), atomic.Load(counter)
    println atomic.CompareAndSwap(counter, 20, 30), atomic.CompareAndSwap(counter, 20, 40), atomic.Load(counter)
    atomic.DestroyI64(counter)
    flag := atomic.NewFlag(false)
    println atomic.TestAndSet(flag), atomic.TestAndSet(flag), atomic.Get(flag)
    atomic.Set(flag, false)
    println atomic.Get(flag)
    atomic.DestroyFlag(flag)
end
```

Output:

```text
2000
10 20
true false 30
true false true
false
```

### `Flag`

```salam
struct Flag
```

A true or false flag shared between threads.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cell` | `i64*` | The address of the value. |
| `mu` | `sync.Mutex` | The internal lock. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: atomic-I64.salam

# chan

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/chan/

A channel for passing values from one thread to another, with a buffer, timeouts and closing.

A channel is a queue that several threads send values into at one end and receive from at the other; it handles the locks and the waiting for you. You give the value type when you create it, as in `chan.Chan<i64>`, and call `init` with a capacity before using it.

When the buffer is full, `send` waits; when it is empty, `recv` does. A channel of capacity zero is "unbuffered": the sender waits until a receiver takes the value. After `close`, sending returns false but receivers still get the values that are left; once the channel is empty, `ok` turns false and a receiving loop can end.

## Types

### `Chan`

```salam
struct Chan<T>
```

A channel of values of type `T`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `buf` | `T*` | The buffer of values. |
| `ctl` | `i64*` | The internal state: the head and tail of the queue, the count and whether it is closed. |
| `cap` | `i64 = 0` | The capacity. |
| `zidx` | `i64 = 0` | The buffer slot holding the type's zero value, for when nothing was received. |
| `mu` | `sync.Mutex` | The internal lock. |
| `not_empty` | `sync.CondVar` | Waking the receivers. |
| `not_full` | `sync.CondVar` | Waking the senders. |
| `taken` | `sync.CondVar` | The signal that a value was taken, on an unbuffered channel. |

chan-Chan.salam

```salam
import chan
import sync

mut jobs := chan.Chan {} as chan.Chan<i64>
mut results := chan.Chan {} as chan.Chan<i64>
mut group := sync.WaitGroup {}

func worker():
    mut open := true
    until true:
        n := jobs.recv(open)
        if not open:
            break
        end
        results.send(n * n)
    end
    sync.Done(group)
end

func main:
    jobs.init(4)
    results.init(16)
    group = sync.NewWaitGroup()
    sync.Add(group, 2)
    a := spawn(worker)
    b := spawn(worker)
    repeat 1 to 11 in n:
        jobs.send(n)
    end
    jobs.close()
    sync.Wait(group)
    join(a)
    join(b)
    results.close()
    mut total := 0 as i64
    mut open := true
    until true:
        v := results.recv(open)
        if not open:
            break
        end
        total += v
    end
    println "sum of the squares:", total
    println jobs.is_closed(), jobs.len(), jobs.capacity(), jobs.send(1)
    sync.DestroyWaitGroup(group)
    jobs.free()
    results.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
sum of the squares: 506
true 0 4 false
```

#### `init`

```salam

```

Prepares the channel with the given capacity; zero means unbuffered.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Chan.salam

#### `send`

```salam

```

Sends a value, waiting when there is no room. If the channel is closed it returns false.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Chan.salam

#### `send_timeout`

```salam

```

Like `send`, but it waits at most `ms` milliseconds.

chan-Timeout.salam

```salam
import chan

func main:
    mut c := chan.Chan {} as chan.Chan<str>
    c.init(1)
    println c.try_send("hello"), c.try_send("again")
    println c.send_timeout("late", 20)
    mut open := true
    println c.try_recv(open), open
    _ := c.recv_timeout(open, 20)
    println "after 20 milliseconds:", open
    println c.send_deadline("a", 0, false)
    println c.recv_deadline(open, 20, true), open
    c.free()
end
```

```text

false
hello true
after 20 milliseconds: false
true

```

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Timeout.salam

#### `recv`

```salam

```

Receives a value, waiting when there is none. When the channel is closed and empty, `ok` turns false; the returned value then means nothing and must not be used.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Chan.salam

#### `recv_timeout`

Like `recv`, but it waits at most `ms` milliseconds. If nothing arrives, `ok` turns false.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Timeout.salam

#### `recv_deadline`


The base of the two above, with the same meaning for `timed`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Timeout.salam

#### `try_send`

```salam

```

Sends if there is room right now; it never waits. On an unbuffered channel it is always false.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Timeout.salam

#### `try_recv`

#### `close`

#### `is_closed`

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: chan-Chan.salam

# pool

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/pool/

Running one loop in parallel across several processor cores.

If each turn of a loop is independent of the others, such as processing each slot of an array on its own, `ParallelFor` spreads the turns across several worker threads and waits for all of them. The loop body is a function taking an `i64`, the turn's number.

The order the turns run in is not defined. If the turns change shared data, use a lock or atomic; each turn writing to its own slot is safe.

## Functions

### `CPUCount`

```salam
func CPUCount(): i64
```

The number of processor cores, at least one.

pool-ParallelFor.salam

```salam
import pool
import mem

mut squares := null as i64*

func main:
    println pool.CPUCount() >= 1
    squares = mem.AllocateZeroed(80 as u64) as i64*
    pool.ParallelFor(10, 4, (i: i64): squares[i] = i * i end)
    mut total := 0 as i64
    repeat 10 in i:
        total += squares[i]
    end
    println total
    pool.ParallelForAuto(10, (i: i64): squares[i] = -i end)
    println squares[9]
    mem.Free(squares as void*)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
285
-9
```

### `ParallelFor`

```salam
func ParallelFor(n: i64, workers: i64, body: func(i64))
```

Runs the body for the numbers zero to `n - 1` across `workers` threads and waits for all of them.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: pool-ParallelFor.salam

### `ParallelForAuto`

```salam
func ParallelForAuto(n: i64, body: func(i64))
```

Like `ParallelFor`, with one thread per core.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: pool-ParallelFor.salam

# ctx

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ctx/

A context for cancellation and deadlines, passed from the main piece of work down to the smaller ones.

A context tells long-running work when to stop: either someone called `Cancel`, or its deadline passed. Contexts form a tree: you start from `Background` and make a child each time with `WithCancel`, `WithTimeout` or `WithDeadline`.

Cancelling a context ends all its children, but not its parent. The work should check `IsDone` from time to time, or wait on it with `Wait`. Free each context with `Free` when you are done with it, children before parents.

## Types

### `Context`

```salam
struct Context
```

A context.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `i64*` | The internal state: cancelled, the deadline and whether there is one. |
| `parent` | `Context*` | The parent context, or null for the root. |
| `mu` | `sync.Mutex` | The lock every context in one tree shares. |
| `cv` | `sync.CondVar` | The condition variable that cancellation wakes. |
| `is_root` | `bool = false` | Whether this context is the root. |

ctx-Context.salam

```salam
import ctx

func main:
    root := ctx.Background()
    cancellable := ctx.WithCancel(root)
    timed := ctx.WithTimeout(cancellable, 30)
    println ctx.IsDone(timed), "[" + ctx.Err(timed) + "]", ctx.Deadline(timed) > 0, ctx.Deadline(root)
    println ctx.Wait(timed, 10)
    println ctx.Wait(timed, 1000), ctx.Err(timed)
    ctx.Cancel(cancellable)
    println ctx.IsDone(cancellable), ctx.Err(cancellable), ctx.IsDone(root)
    past := ctx.WithDeadline(root, 1)
    println ctx.IsDone(past), ctx.Err(past)
    ctx.Free(past)
    ctx.Free(timed)
    ctx.Free(cancellable)
    ctx.Free(root)
end
```

Output:

```text
false [] true 0
false
true deadline exceeded
true cancelled false
true deadline exceeded
```

## Functions

### `Background`

```salam
func Background(): Context
```

The root context, which never finishes by itself.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `WithCancel`

```salam

```

A child that ends when `Cancel` is called.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `WithTimeout`

```salam

```

A child that ends `ms` milliseconds from now.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `WithDeadline`

```salam

```

A child that ends at the instant `at_ms`, in milliseconds, as `sync.NowMs` gives it.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `Cancel`

```salam

```

Ends the context and all its children and wakes everything waiting.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `IsDone`

```salam

```

True when the context, or one of its parents, has been cancelled or has passed its deadline.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `Err`

```salam

```

Why it finished: `cancelled` or `deadline exceeded`, or an empty string while it is still running.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `Deadline`

```salam

```

The nearest deadline in the context and its parents, in milliseconds, or zero when there is none.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

### `Wait`

```salam

```

Waits at most `ms` milliseconds for the context to finish and says whether it did.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ctx-Context.salam

# encoding

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding/

Turning text and data into Base64, hexadecimal and URL encoding.

This package holds the common ways of writing bytes as plain text: Base64 for fitting binary data into JSON or email, hexadecimal for showing bytes, and URL encoding for putting text or special characters into a web address.

The larger formats, such as JSON, YAML and XML, have sub-packages of their own, listed in this same group.

## Functions

### `Base64Encode`

```salam
func Base64Encode(data: str): str
```

Turns text into standard Base64, padded with `=`.

encoding-Base64.salam

```salam
import encoding
import mem

func main:
    e := encoding.Base64Encode("hello world")
    println e
    println encoding.Base64Decode(e)
    mut ok := false
    println "[" + encoding.Base64DecodeStrict("***", ok) + "]", ok
    println encoding.Base64DecodeStrict("YWJj", ok), ok
    b := mem.Allocate(3 as u64)
    mem.Set(b, 255, 3 as u64)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(b, 3)
    out := mem.Allocate(8 as u64)
    println encoding.Base64DecodeBytes("AAEC", out, 8, ok), ok
    mem.Free(b)
    mem.Free(out)
end
```

Output:

```text
aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=
hello world
[] false
abc true
////
3 true
```

# encoding/json

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-json/

Building and reading JSON: from a plain string through automatic struct conversion to streaming.

There are three ways to work with JSON here. For simple jobs, functions such as `Member`, `Object` and `Get` work directly on JSON text. For real programs, `Marshal` and `Unmarshal` convert a Salam struct to JSON and back. For data whose shape you do not know in advance, `Decode` returns a dynamic Value.

Set the key name of a field with `@json "name"` above it; `@json "-"` leaves the field out. Without it, the field's own name becomes the key.

## Types

### `JSONOptions`

```salam
struct JSONOptions
```

The options for `Encode`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indent` | `str = ""` | The indent unit; empty means one line. |
| `sort_keys` | `bool = false` | Write the keys in alphabetical order. Without it the key order is not fixed. |
| `ignore_null` | `bool = false` | Leave out the keys whose value is null. |

encoding-json-Value.salam

```salam
import encoding.json
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr
import fs.file

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    v := json.Decode(`{"city": "Tehran", "zones": [1, 2, 22]}`, e)
    println encerr.IsError(e), value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(v, "city"))
    println json.EncodeDefault(v)
    opts := json.JSONOptions { indent = "  ", sort_keys = true }
    println json.Encode(v, opts)
    _ := json.Decode("[1, 2", e)
    println encerr.IsError(e), e.position
    mut enc := json.NewBufEncoder()
    enc.Encode(value.ValueInt(1))
    enc.Encode(value.ValueString("two"))
    println enc.String()
    enc.Close()
    mut pretty := json.NewBufEncoderIndent("  ")
    pretty.Encode(v)
    println pretty.String()
    pretty.Close()
    out := file.Open("lines.ndjson", "wb")
    mut lines := json.NewEncoder(out)
    lines.Encode(value.ValueInt(10))
    lines.Encode(value.ValueInt(20))
    lines.Close()
    mut tabbed := json.NewEncoderIndent(file.Open("pretty.json", "wb"), "\t")
    tabbed.Encode(v)
    tabbed.Close()
    mut reader := json.NewDecoder(file.Open("lines.ndjson", "rb"))
    mut total := 0 as i64
    until reader.More():
        total += value.AsInt(reader.Decode())
    end
    println total
    mut two := json.NewBufDecoder("{\"a\": 1}\n{\"a\": 2}\n")
    until two.More():
        println json.EncodeDefault(two.Decode())
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
false Tehran
{"city": "Tehran", "zones": [1, 2, 22]}
{
  "city": "Tehran",
  "zones": [
    1,
    2,
    22
  ]
}
true 5
1
"two"
{
  "city": "Tehran",
  "zones": [
    1,
    2,
    22
  ]
}
30
{"a": 1}
{"a": 2}
```

### `JSONEncoder`

```salam
struct JSONEncoder
```

A streaming writer: it writes several JSON values one after another, each on its own line.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dst` | `File*` | The destination file, when it writes to one. |
| `useFile` | `bool = false` | Whether it writes to a file or into memory. |
| `buf` | `str.StringBuilder` | The text buffer, when it writes into memory. |
| `indent` | `str = ""` | The indent unit; empty means one value per line. |
| `count` | `int = 0` | How many values have been written. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-json-Value.salam

#### `Encode`

```salam

```

Writes one value and a newline after it.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-json-Value.salam

#### `String`

```salam

```

The text written into memory.

### `JSONDecoder`

```salam
struct JSONDecoder
```

A streaming reader: it reads consecutive JSON values one at a time, as in a JSON Lines file.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `File*` | The source file. |
| `useFile` | `bool = false` | Whether it reads from a file. |
| `buf` | `str = ""` | The text that was read. |
| `pos` | `int = 0` | The current position in the text. |
| `loaded` | `bool = false` | Whether the file has been read. |
| `eof` | `bool = false` | It has reached the end of the text. |
| `bad` | `bool = false` | An error happened while reading. |

## Functions

### `Valid`

```salam
func Valid(text: str): bool
```

True when the text is valid JSON.

encoding-json-Build.salam

```salam
import encoding.json

func main:
    mut tags := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    tags.push(json.Str("hello"))
    tags.push(json.Str(`a "quoted" line`))
    mut members := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    members.push(json.Member("name", "Ali"))
    members.push(json.MemberInt("age", 30))
    members.push(json.MemberBool("admin", false))
    members.push(json.MemberFloat("score", 18.5))
    members.push(json.MemberRaw("tags", json.Array(tags)))
    text := json.Object(members)
    println text
    println json.Valid(text), json.Valid("{broken")
    println json.Get(text, "name"), json.GetInt(text, "age"), json.GetFloat(text, "score")
    println json.Has(text, "admin"), json.Has(text, "email"), json.Keys(text)
    println json.Escape("one\ttwo")
    pretty := json.Indent(text)
    println pretty
    println json.Minify(pretty) == json.Minify(text)
    println json.Indent4(`{"a":1}`)
    println json.IndentTabs(`{"a":1}`) == "{\n\t\"a\": 1\n}", json.IndentWith(`[1]`, "--")
    nested := `{"user":{"tags":["a","b"],"name":"Ali"}}`
    println json.GetPath(nested, "user.name"), json.GetPath(nested, "user.tags.1"), json.Items(json.GetPath(nested, "user.tags")).len()
    println json.Unquote(`"\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645"`)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"name": "Ali", "age": 30, "admin": false, "score": 18.5, "tags": ["hello", "a \"quoted\" line"]}
true false
Ali 30 18.5
true false ["name", "age", "admin", "score", "tags"]
one\ttwo
{
  "name": "Ali",
  "age": 30,
  "admin": false,
  "score": 18.5,
  "tags": [
    "hello",
    "a \"quoted\" line"
  ]
}
true
{
    "a": 1
}
true [
--1
]
Ali b 2
سلام
```

### `SchemaEnvelope`

```salam
func SchemaEnvelope<T>(v: T): str
```

Builds the JSON Schema of a value's type, along with the definitions of the nested types, inside an envelope to be combined later with `SchemaMerge`.

encoding-json-Marshal.salam

```salam
import encoding.json
import encoding.encerr

struct User:
    @json "name"
    pub name: str = ""
    @json "age"
    pub age: int = 0
    @json "tags"
    pub tags: Vector<str> = Vector {}
    @json "-"
    pub password: str = ""
end

func main:
    mut u := User { name = "Maryam", age = 28, password = "secret" }
    u.tags.push("admin")
    println json.Marshal(u)
    println json.MarshalIndent(u, "  ")
    mut loaded := User {}
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    println json.Unmarshal(`{"name": "Reza", "age": 41, "tags": ["a", "b"]}`, loaded, e)
    println loaded.name, loaded.age, loaded.tags.len()
    println json.Unmarshal(`{"name": "Reza", "age": "forty"}`, loaded, e), e.message
    mut lenient := User {}
    println json.UnmarshalLenient(`{"name": "Sara", "extra": 1}`, lenient, e), lenient.name
    println json.Schema(u)
    envelope := json.SchemaEnvelope(u)
    println json.SchemaMerge(envelope) == json.Schema(u)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"name":"Maryam","age":28,"tags":["admin"]}
{
  "name": "Maryam",
  "age": 28,
  "tags": [
    "admin"
  ]
}
true
Reza 41 2
false value does not match the expected type
true Sara
{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","$defs":{"User":{"title":"User","type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer","format":"int32"},"tags":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["name","age","tags"],"additionalProperties":false}},"$ref":"#/$defs/User"}
true
```

# encoding/yaml

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-yaml/

Reading YAML by path, building and writing it, and converting it to JSON.

YAML is the usual format for configuration files. This package converts YAML to JSON internally, which is what makes its reading functions simple and what lets it work alongside the json package.

The reading functions take a path: keys separated by dots, with a list index in square brackets, as in `app.hosts[1]`. A path that is not there gives an empty string or zero; to tell that apart from a real value, use `Has`.

## Functions

### `Decode`

```salam
func Decode(text: str, err &: encerr.EncodingError): value.Value
```

Turns YAML into a dynamic `Value`.

encoding-yaml-Build.salam

```salam
import encoding.yaml
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr
import str

func main:
    mut members := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    members.push(yaml.Member("name", "salam"))
    members.push(yaml.MemberInt("port", 8080))
    members.push(yaml.MemberBool("debug", false))
    members.push(yaml.MemberFloat("ratio", 0.25))
    mut hosts := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    hosts.push(yaml.Str("a: b"))
    members.push(yaml.MemberRaw("hosts", yaml.Array(hosts)))
    object := yaml.Object(members)
    println object
    println yaml.Dump(object)
    println str.Contains(yaml.DumpTabs(`{"a": {"b": 1}}`), "\tb: 1"), yaml.DumpWith(`{"a": [1]}`, "    ")
    println yaml.Escape("one: two")
    println yaml.Parse("x: 1")
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    v := yaml.Decode("city: Tehran\npopulation: 9000000\n", e)
    println value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(v, "population"))
    println yaml.Encode(v)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"name": "salam", "port": 8080, "debug": false, "ratio": 0.25, "hosts": ["a: b"]}
name: salam
port: 8080
debug: false
ratio: 0.25
hosts:
  - "a: b"
true a:
    - 1
one: two
{"x": 1}
9000000
city: Tehran
population: 9000000
```

```salam
import encoding.yaml

func main:
    text := "app:\n  name: salam\n  port: 8080\n  debug: true\n  ratio: 0.5\n  hosts:\n    - a.example\n    - b.example\n"
    println yaml.Valid(text), yaml.Has(text, "app.name"), yaml.Has(text, "app.user")
    println yaml.Get(text, "app.name"), yaml.GetInt(text, "app.port"), yaml.GetBool(text, "app.debug"), yaml.GetFloat(text, "app.ratio")
    println yaml.TypeOf(text, "app.hosts"), yaml.Len(text, "app.hosts"), yaml.Get(text, "app.hosts[1]")
    println yaml.Keys(text, "app")
    mut required := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    required.push("app")
    println yaml.HasKeys(text, required)
    required.push("db")
    println yaml.HasKeys(text, required)
    println yaml.ToJSON(text)
    println yaml.SplitDocuments("a: 1\n---\nb: 2\n").len()
end
```

Output:

```text
true true false
salam 8080 true 0.5
list 2 b.example
["name", "port", "debug", "ratio", "hosts"]
true
false
{"app": {"name": "salam", "port": 8080, "debug": true, "ratio": 0.5, "hosts": ["a.example", "b.example"]}}
2
```

# encoding/csv

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-csv/

Reading and writing CSV files, with correct quoting and conversion to a dynamic value.

CSV is the simplest table format: one row per line, fields separated by commas. A field containing a comma, a quote or a newline is wrapped in quotes, and a quote inside it is doubled. This package follows those rules both ways.

Every field is a string. When the first row is a header, `ToValue` turns each row into an object with those keys.

## Types

### `CSVRow`

```salam
struct CSVRow
```

One row.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | `Vector` | The row's fields. |

encoding-csv-Table.salam

```salam
import encoding.csv
import encoding.value

func main:
    text := "name,city\nAli,Tehran\n\"Sara, engineer\",\"Shiraz\"\n"
    mut table := csv.ReadAll(text)
    println table.rows.len()
    each row in table.rows:
        println row.fields.len(), row.fields[0]
    end
    println csv.WriteAll(table)
    csv.FreeTable(table)
    println csv.ReadLine(`a,"b,c",d`)
    mut fields := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    fields.push("plain")
    fields.push(`with "quotes"`)
    println csv.WriteLine(fields)
    v := csv.ToValue("name,age\nAli,30\n")
    println value.ArrayLen(v), value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(value.ArrayGet(v, 0), "name"))
    println csv.FromValue(v)
    opts := csv.CSVOptions { header = false }
    rows := csv.ToValueWith("1,2\n3,4\n", opts)
    println value.ArrayLen(rows), csv.FromValueWith(rows, opts)
end
```

Output:

```text
3
2 name
2 Ali
2 Sara, engineer
name,city
Ali,Tehran
"Sara, engineer",Shiraz
["a", "b,c", "d"]
plain,"with ""quotes"""
1 Ali
age,name
30,Ali
2 1,2
3,4
```

### `CSVTable`

```salam

```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `Vector` | The rows, including the header row. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-csv-Table.salam


| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-csv-Table.salam

# encoding/toml

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-toml/

Reading and writing TOML configuration files.

TOML is a straightforward configuration format of `[section]` tables and `key = value` pairs. This package turns it into a dynamic Value and back.

## Functions

### `DecodeStrict`

```salam
func DecodeStrict(text: str, ok &: bool): value.Value
```

Reads TOML, setting `ok` false when the text is not valid.

encoding-toml-Decode.salam

```salam
import encoding.toml
import encoding.value

func main:
    text := "title = \"salam\"\n\n[server]\nhost = \"localhost\"\nport = 8080\ntags = [\"a\", \"b\"]\n"
    println toml.Valid(text), toml.Valid("= no key")
    v := toml.Decode(text)
    server := value.ObjectGet(v, "server")
    println value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(v, "title")), value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(server, "port"))
    println toml.Encode(v)
    mut read := false
    _ := toml.DecodeStrict("a = \n", read)
    println read
    mut wrote := false
    println toml.EncodeStrict(value.ValueInt(1), wrote), wrote
end
```

Output:

```text
true false
salam 8080
title = "salam"
[server]
host = "localhost"
tags = ["a", "b"]
port = 8080

false
 false
```

# encoding/url

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-url/

Taking a web address apart, building and editing its parameters, and resolving relative addresses.

`Parse` takes a full address such as `https://user@shop.example.co.uk:8443/path?page=2#top` apart. The parts are kept exactly as they appeared in the text; for the decoded form use functions such as `DecodedPath`.

The parameter functions edit the address's query through the query package, and `String` builds the finished address.

## Types

### `URL`

```salam
struct URL
```

A parsed web address.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scheme` | `str = ""` | The scheme, such as `https`. |
| `userinfo` | `str = ""` | The user name and password before the `@`, still encoded. |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host name or numeric address. |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port, or zero when none was given. |
| `path` | `str = ""` | The path, still encoded. |
| `raw_query` | `str = ""` | The query after the `?`, still encoded. |
| `fragment` | `str = ""` | The part after the `#`. |

encoding-url-Parse.salam

```salam
import encoding.url
import encoding.query

func main:
    mut u := url.Parse("https://user%20a:pw@shop.example.co.uk:8443/books/%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85?page=2&sort=new#top")
    println u.scheme, u.host, u.port, u.path, u.raw_query, u.fragment
    println url.Hostname(u), url.HostPort(u), url.IsIP(u)
    println url.Labels(u), url.PublicSuffix(u), url.Domain(u), url.Subdomain(u)
    println url.DecodedPath(u), url.DecodedUserinfo(u)
    println url.ParamNames(u), query.Size(url.Query(u))
    url.SetParam(u, "page", "3")
    println url.RemoveParam(u, "sort"), url.String(u)
    mut keep := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    keep.push("page")
    url.KeepParams(u, keep)
    mut q := query.NewQueryMap()
    query.Add(q, "q", "hello world")
    url.SetQuery(u, q)
    println url.String(u)
    url.ClearQuery(u)
    println url.String(u)
    println url.String(url.Join(u, "../img/a.png")), url.EncodePathSegment("a b/c")
    println url.IsIP(url.Parse("http://127.0.0.1/"))
end
```

Output:

```text
https shop.example.co.uk 8443 /books/%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85 page=2&sort=new top
shop.example.co.uk shop.example.co.uk:8443 false
["shop", "example", "co", "uk"] co.uk example.co.uk shop
/books/سلام user a:pw
["page", "sort"] 2
true https://user%20a:pw@shop.example.co.uk:8443/books/%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85?page=3#top
https://user%20a:pw@shop.example.co.uk:8443/books/%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85?q=hello+world#top
https://user%20a:pw@shop.example.co.uk:8443/books/%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85#top
https://user%20a:pw@shop.example.co.uk:8443/img/a.png a%20b%2Fc
true
```

# encoding/query

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-query/

Reading and building the query string of a web address, such as `q=hello&page=2`.

The query string is the part after the `?` in a web address. One key may appear several times, as in `tag=a&tag=b`, so a `QueryMap` keeps a list of values for each key, and keeps the keys in order.

Functions such as `Get` and `Has` work on the string directly, which suits reading something once.

## Types

### `QueryOptions`

```salam
struct QueryOptions
```

The encoding options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `space_as_plus` | `bool = true` | Write a space as `+`; true by default. When false, `%20` is written. |

encoding-query-Query.salam

```salam
import encoding.query

func main:
    text := "q=hello&page=2&tag=a&tag=b&empty="
    println query.Get(text, "q"), query.Get(text, "page"), query.Has(text, "empty"), query.Has(text, "x")
    println query.GetAll(text, "tag")
    mut m := query.Decode(text)
    println query.Size(m), query.Keys(m)
    query.Add(m, "tag", "c")
    query.Set(m, "page", "3")
    println query.Remove(m, "empty")
    println query.Encode(m)
    mut keep := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    keep.push("q")
    query.Retain(m, keep)
    println query.Encode(m)
    opts := query.QueryOptions {}
    println query.EncodeWith(query.DecodeWith("b=2&a=1", opts), opts)
    empty := query.NewQueryMap()
    println query.Size(empty)
end
```

Output:

```text
hello 2 true false
["a", "b"]
4 ["q", "page", "tag", "empty"]
true
q=hello&page=3&tag=a&tag=b&tag=c
q=hello
b=2&a=1
0
```

### `QueryValues`

```salam
struct QueryValues
```

The values of one key.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The values, in order. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-query-Query.salam

### `QueryMap`

```salam
struct QueryMap
```

A map from key to values that keeps the key order.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `HashMap` | The values of each key. |
| `order` | `Vector` | The keys in the order they first appeared. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-query-Query.salam

# encoding/envfile

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-envfile/

Reading and writing `.env` files, with variable substitution.

A `.env` file holds a program's environment variables, one `KEY=value` per line. This package skips blank lines and `#` comments, accepts `export` before a key, strips the quotes, and keeps the keys in order.

`Parse` substitutes references such as `${HOST}` from the same file; `ParseRaw` leaves them alone. The operating system's own environment variables are not read; for those see the env package.

## Types

### `Doc`

```salam
struct Doc
```

The contents of an env file.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `m` | `collections.OrderedMap` | The keys and values, in order. |
| `flags` | `Vector` | For each key, whether its value takes substitution; single quotes turn it off. |

encoding-envfile-Parse.salam

```salam
import encoding.envfile
import encoding.encerr

func main:
    text := "# settings\nHOST=localhost\nPORT=8080\nexport NAME=\"hello world\"\nURL=http://${HOST}:${PORT}/\n"
    mut doc := envfile.Parse(text)
    println envfile.Len(doc), envfile.Keys(doc)
    println envfile.Get(doc, "NAME"), envfile.Has(doc, "DEBUG"), envfile.GetOr(doc, "DEBUG", "false")
    println envfile.KeyAt(doc, 0), envfile.ValueAt(doc, 1)
    println envfile.Get(doc, "URL")
    raw := envfile.ParseRaw(text)
    println envfile.Get(raw, "URL"), envfile.RefNames(raw)
    mut base := envfile.New()
    expanded := envfile.ExpandDoc(raw, base)
    println envfile.Get(expanded, "URL")
    println envfile.Expand("${HOST}/api", doc, base), envfile.RefNamesIn("$A and ${B}")
    envfile.Set(doc, "DEBUG", "true")
    println envfile.Remove(doc, "URL")
    println envfile.Format(doc)
    println envfile.FormatExport(base) == "", envfile.Quote("a b")
    mut other := envfile.Parse("PORT=9090\nMODE=prod\n")
    envfile.MergeInto(doc, other)
    println envfile.Get(doc, "PORT"), envfile.Get(doc, "MODE")
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    _ := envfile.ParseStrict("=no key\n", e)
    println encerr.IsError(e), envfile.Valid("A=1\n")
    println envfile.ParseScalar(`"a\tb"`), envfile.ParseScalarEx("x ; comment", true)
    envfile.Free(doc)
    envfile.Free(raw)
    envfile.Free(base)
    envfile.Free(expanded)
    envfile.Free(other)
end
```

Output:

```text
4 ["HOST", "PORT", "NAME", "URL"]
hello world false false
HOST 8080
http://localhost:8080/
http://${HOST}:${PORT}/ ["HOST", "PORT"]
http://localhost:8080/
localhost/api ["A", "B"]
true
HOST=localhost
PORT=8080
NAME="hello world"
DEBUG=true

true "a b"
9090 prod
true true
a	b x
```

# encoding/value

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-value/

A dynamic value for data whose shape you do not know in advance; the shared language of every format in this group.

When you read JSON whose shape you do not know in advance, it cannot be poured into a fixed struct. That is what `Value` is for: every value carries its own kind, and it may be an array or an object of further values.

JSON, YAML, TOML, MessagePack, CSV and XML can all be turned into a `Value` and built from one; the encoding.serde package uses exactly this to convert between formats.

## Types

### `Value`

```salam
struct Value
```

A dynamic value: null, boolean, whole number, decimal, string, array or object.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int` | The kind of the value; one of the Kind constants. |
| `b` | `bool = false` | The boolean value. |
| `i` | `i64 = 0` | The whole number value. |
| `n` | `f64 = 0` | The decimal value. |
| `s` | `str = ""` | The string value. |
| `arr` | `Vector` | The elements of an array. |
| `obj` | `HashMap` | The keys and values of an object. |

encoding-value-Value.salam

```salam
import encoding.value

func main:
    mut user := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(user, "name", value.ValueString("Narges"))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "age", value.ValueInt(34))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "height", value.ValueFloat(1.68))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "admin", value.ValueBool(false))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "phone", value.ValueNull())
    mut languages := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(languages, value.ValueString("fa"))
    value.ArrayPush(languages, value.ValueString("en"))
    value.ArraySet(languages, 1, value.ValueString("ar"))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "langs", languages)
    println value.ToDebugString(user)
    println value.ObjectLen(user), value.ObjectHas(user, "age"), value.ObjectKeys(user)
    println value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(user, "name")), value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(user, "age")), value.AsFloat(value.ObjectGet(user, "height")), value.AsBool(value.ObjectGet(user, "admin"))
    langs := value.ObjectGet(user, "langs")
    println value.IsArray(langs), value.ArrayLen(langs), value.AsString(value.ArrayGet(langs, 1))
    mut present := false
    _ := value.ObjectGetOk(user, "email", present)
    println present
    phone := value.ObjectGet(user, "phone")
    println value.IsNull(phone), value.IsBool(phone), value.IsInt(value.ValueInt(1)), value.IsFloat(value.ValueFloat(1.0)), value.IsNumber(value.ValueInt(1))
    println value.IsString(value.ValueString("")), value.IsObject(user), phone.kind == value.KindNull, value.KindObject
    mut copy := value.ValueClone(user)
    println value.Equal(copy, user)
    removed := value.ObjectDelete(copy, "phone")
    println removed, value.Equal(copy, user)
    mut numbers := Vector {} as Vector<value.Value>
    numbers.push(value.ValueInt(1))
    mut fields := HashMap {} as HashMap<str, value.Value>
    fields.put("x", value.ValueArray(numbers))
    println value.ToDebugString(value.ValueObject(fields))
    value.ValueFree(copy)
end
```

Output:

```text
object{name: string(Narges), height: float(1.68), age: int(34), admin: bool(false), langs: array[string(fa), string(ar)], phone: null}
6 true ["name", "height", "age", "admin", "langs", "phone"]
Narges 34 1.68 false
true 2 ar
false
true false true true true
true true true 6
true
true false
object{x: array[int(1)]}
```

# encoding/serde

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-serde/

Detecting the format of a piece of text and converting JSON, YAML, TOML, XML and CSV into one another.

This package reads text in one format, turns it into a Value and writes it out in another. The format names are the short strings `json`, `yaml`, `toml`, `xml` and `csv`.

## Constants and variables

### `FormatUnknown`

```salam
const FormatUnknown: i32 = 0
```

An unknown format.

encoding-serde-Transcode.salam

```salam
import encoding.serde

func main:
    data := `{"name": "salam", "port": 8080, "tags": ["a", "b"]}`
    println serde.Detect(data), serde.Detect("a: 1\nb: 2\n"), serde.Detect("<a/>"), serde.Detect("[x]\ny = 1\n"), serde.Detect("a,b\n1,2\n")
    println serde.DetectFormat(data) == serde.FormatJSON, serde.FormatUnknown, serde.FormatYAML, serde.FormatTOML, serde.FormatXML, serde.FormatCSV
    println serde.Transcode(data, "json", "yaml")
    println serde.Transcode(data, "json", "toml")
    println serde.Transcode("name,age\nAli,30\n", "csv", "json")
    mut ok := false
    _ := serde.TranscodeStrict(data, "json", "pdf", ok)
    println ok
end
```

Output:

```text
json yaml xml toml csv
true 0 2 3 4 5
tags:
  - a
  - b
name: salam
port: 8080
tags = ["a", "b"]
name = "salam"
port = 8080

[{"age": "30", "name": "Ali"}]
false
```

# encoding/encerr

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-encerr/

The shared error of the format readers: a kind, a message and a position in the text.

The functions that read JSON, YAML, env files and MessagePack report their errors in an `EncodingError`. Build one with `NoError`, pass it to the function, and then check `IsError`.

## Types

### `EncodingError`

```salam
struct EncodingError
```

An error from reading or writing a format.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int` | The kind of error; one of the Kind constants. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The error message, in English. |
| `position` | `int = -1` | Where the error is in the text, in bytes, or -1 when it is not known. |

encoding-encerr-Error.salam

```salam
import encoding.encerr
import encoding.json

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    println encerr.IsError(e), e.kind == encerr.KindNone
    _ := json.Decode(`{"a": }`, e)
    println encerr.IsError(e), e.kind, e.position, e.message
    custom := encerr.NewError(encerr.KindCustom, "a negative value is not allowed", 12)
    println custom.kind, custom.message, custom.position
    println encerr.ErrUnexpectedEOF(40).kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedEOF
    println encerr.ErrUnexpectedToken("expected ':'", 3).kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedToken
    println encerr.ErrTypeMismatch("a number", 5).message
    println encerr.KindInvalidUTF8, encerr.KindInvalidNumber, encerr.KindDepthExceeded, encerr.KindTypeMismatch, encerr.KindKeyNotFound, encerr.KindTrailingData
end
```

Output:

```text
false true
true 2 6 invalid value
99 a negative value is not allowed 12
true
true
expected a number
3 4 5 6 7 8
```

# encoding/msgpack

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-msgpack/

The compact binary MessagePack format for dynamic values.

MessagePack holds the same data as JSON in a shorter binary form that is quicker to read; it suits sending data between services or putting it in a cache. This package turns a value into a byte buffer and back.

## Types

### `MsgpackOptions`

```salam
struct MsgpackOptions
```

The serialising options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `use_str8` | `bool = true` | Use the str8 format for short strings; true by default. Very old implementations do not know that format. |

encoding-msgpack-Marshal.salam

```salam
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr
import encoding
import compress

func main:
    mut v := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(v, "id", value.ValueInt(7))
    value.ObjectSet(v, "ok", value.ValueBool(true))
    b := msgpack.Marshal(v)
    println compress.BufLen(b), compress.BufToBase64(b)
    mut err := encerr.NoError()
    back := msgpack.Unmarshal(b, err)
    println encerr.IsError(err), value.Equal(v, back), value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(back, "id"))
    back2 := msgpack.UnmarshalBytes(b.data, b.len, err)
    println value.Equal(v, back2)
    o := msgpack.MsgpackOptions {}
    println compress.BufLen(msgpack.MarshalWith(v, o))
    println encoding.HexEncode(compress.BufToStrUnsafe(msgpack.Marshal(value.ValueInt(5))))
end
```

Output:

```text
9 gqJpZAeib2vD
false true 7
true
9
05
```

## Functions

### `MarshalWith`

```salam
func MarshalWith(v: value.Value, opts: MsgpackOptions): compress.ByteBuf
```

Turns a value into MessagePack bytes with the given options.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-msgpack-Marshal.salam

### `Marshal`

```salam

```

Turns a value into MessagePack bytes.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-msgpack-Marshal.salam

### `UnmarshalBytes`

```salam
func UnmarshalBytes(p: void*, n: int, err &: encerr.EncodingError): value.Value
```

Reads `n` bytes of MessagePack from memory.

# encoding/binary

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-binary/

Writing and reading numbers as bytes, big-endian or little-endian.

Binary file formats and network protocols store a number as several bytes in a row. Big-endian writes the most significant byte first and is the usual order in network protocols; little-endian is the other way round and is what most processors use, and formats such as ZIP.

The writing functions take a `ByteBuf` and the reading functions take a `ByteReader`, both from the compress package.

## Types

### `BinaryOptions`

```salam
struct BinaryOptions
```

The options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `big_endian` | `bool = false` | Use big-endian byte order; false by default. |

encoding-binary-ReadWrite.salam

```salam
import encoding.binary
import compress

func main:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    binary.WriteU8(b, 255)
    binary.WriteU16BE(b, 4660)
    binary.WriteU16LE(b, 4660)
    binary.WriteU32BE(b, 1)
    binary.WriteI16LE(b, -2)
    println compress.BufToBase64(b)
    binary.WriteU32LE(b, 7)
    binary.WriteU64BE(b, 8)
    binary.WriteU64LE(b, 9)
    binary.WriteI16BE(b, -3)
    binary.WriteI32BE(b, -4)
    binary.WriteI32LE(b, -5)
    binary.WriteI64BE(b, -6)
    binary.WriteI64LE(b, -7)
    binary.WriteF64(b, 1.5, true)
    binary.WriteF32(b, 0.25, false)
    println compress.BufLen(b)
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(b)
    println binary.ReadU8(r), binary.ReadU16BE(r), binary.ReadU16LE(r), binary.ReadU32BE(r), binary.ReadI16LE(r)
    println binary.ReadU32LE(r), binary.ReadU64BE(r), binary.ReadU64LE(r)
    println binary.ReadI16BE(r), binary.ReadI32BE(r), binary.ReadI32LE(r), binary.ReadI64BE(r), binary.ReadI64LE(r)
    println binary.ReadF64(r, true), binary.ReadF32(r, false)
    o := binary.BinaryOptions {}
    println o.big_endian
    compress.BufFree(b)
end
```

Output:

```text
/xI0NBIAAAAB/v8=
69
255 4660 4660 1 -2
7 8 9
-3 -4 -5 -6 -7
1.5 0.25
false
```

---

# encoding/xml

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-xml/

Reading, building and writing XML, with XPath, DTD validation, namespaces and a light simple interface.

This package has two interfaces. The document interface is the complete one: `Parse` reads the text into a document, and every node has a numeric id you use to get its name, attributes, children and text. XPath, DTD validation, namespaces, entities and the canonical form all work on that document.

The simple node interface (`Decode`, `Child`, `Attr`) is for small jobs, such as reading a small configuration file, and keeps the tree directly in plain structs. The `XMLTokenizer` reads the text without building a tree at all.

## Types

### `WriteOptions`

```salam
struct WriteOptions
```

The write options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indent` | `str = ""` | The indent unit; empty means no indenting. |
| `newline` | `str = "
"` | The newline between elements when there is indenting. |

| `declaration` | `bool = false` | Write the `<?xml ...?>` declaration. |
| `doctype` | `bool = false` | Write the DOCTYPE. |
| `empty_as_pair` | `bool = false` | Write an empty element as `<a></a>`. |
| `sort_attributes` | `bool = false` | Put the attributes in alphabetical order. |
| `escape_newlines_in_attributes` | `bool = false` | Write a newline in an attribute value as `&#10;`. |

encoding-xml-Build.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    mut d := xml.NewDocument()
    root := xml.CreateElement(d, "note")
    xml.Append(d, xml.DocumentNode(d), root)
    xml.SetAttribute(d, root, "id", "7")
    xml.SetAttribute(d, root, "draft", "yes")
    recipient := xml.CreateElement(d, "to")
    xml.Append(d, root, recipient)
    xml.Append(d, recipient, xml.CreateText(d, "Maryam & Reza"))
    body := xml.CreateElement(d, "body")
    xml.Append(d, root, body)
    xml.Append(d, body, xml.CreateCData(d, "<b>bold</b>"))
    xml.InsertBefore(d, root, xml.CreateComment(d, "recipient"), recipient)
    xml.Append(d, xml.DocumentNode(d), xml.CreateProcessingInstruction(d, "app", "v=1"))
    println xml.Write(d)
    println xml.RemoveAttribute(d, root, "draft"), xml.RemoveChild(d, root, body)
    xml.SetText(d, recipient, "everyone")
    println xml.WriteIndent(d, "  ")
    println xml.WriteNode(d, recipient), xml.WriteNodeIndent(d, recipient, "\t")
    mut o := xml.DefaultWriteOptions()
    o.declaration = true
    o.empty_as_pair = true
    println xml.WriteWith(d, o)
    println xml.WriteDocument(d)
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d2 := xml.Parse("<r b=\"2\"   a=\"1\"><x/></r>", err)
    println xml.Canonical(d2), xml.CanonicalNode(d2, xml.ChildAt(d2, xml.Root(d2), 0))
    xml.Free(d2)
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
<note id="7" draft="yes"><!--recipient--><to>Maryam &amp; Reza</to><body><![CDATA[<b>bold</b>]]></body></note><?app v=1?>
true true
<note id="7">
  <!--recipient-->
  <to>everyone</to>
</note>
<?app v=1?>

<to>everyone</to> <to>everyone</to>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<note id="7"><!--recipient--><to>everyone</to></note><?app v=1?>
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<note id="7"><!--recipient--><to>everyone</to></note><?app v=1?>

<r a="1" b="2"><x></x></r> <x></x>
```

### `ElementDecl`

```salam
struct ElementDecl
```

The declaration of one element in the DTD.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The element name. |
| `content` | `int = 1` | The content kind; one of the `Content` constants. |
| `model` | `str = ""` | The content model as text, such as `(to, body)`. |
| `root` | `int = -1` | The root of the model tree. |
| `mixed` | `Vector` | The names of the elements allowed in mixed content. |

encoding-xml-DTD.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    dtd := xml.ParseDTD("<!ELEMENT note (to, body)>\n<!ELEMENT to (#PCDATA)>\n<!ELEMENT body (#PCDATA)>\n<!ATTLIST note id ID #REQUIRED kind (a|b) \"a\">")
    println dtd.ok, xml.DeclaredElementCount(dtd), xml.DeclaredAttributeCount(dtd)
    el := dtd.elements[0]
    println el.name, el.content == xml.ContentChildren, el.model
    at := dtd.attributes[1]
    println at.name, at.kind == xml.AttrEnumeration, at.mode == xml.DefaultValue, at.value, at.values
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut good := xml.Parse("<note id=\"n1\"><to>me</to><body>hello</body></note>", err)
    mut report := xml.Validate(good, dtd)
    println report.ok
    xml.FreeReport(report)
    println xml.ApplyDefaults(good, dtd), xml.AttributeValue(good, xml.Root(good), "kind")
    mut bad := xml.Parse("<note><body>no recipient</body></note>", err)
    mut r2 := xml.Validate(bad, dtd)
    println r2.ok, r2.items.len()
    println xml.ReportText(r2)
    xml.FreeReport(r2)
    mut inner := xml.Parse("<!DOCTYPE a [<!ELEMENT a EMPTY>]><a>text</a>", err)
    mut r3 := xml.ValidateInternalSubset(inner)
    println r3.ok, inner.doctype
    xml.FreeReport(r3)
    mut ns := xml.Parse("<a xmlns:x=\"urn:x\"><x:b/></a>", err)
    mut r4 := xml.CheckNamespaces(ns)
    println r4.ok
    xml.FreeReport(r4)
    mut dtd2 := dtd
    xml.FreeDTD(dtd2)
    xml.Free(good)
    xml.Free(bad)
    xml.Free(inner)
    xml.Free(ns)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 3 2
note true (to, body)
kind true true a ["a", "b"]
true
1 a
false 2
line 1, column 1: the children of <note> do not match (to, body)
line 1, column 1: <note> is missing the required attribute "id"
false a
true
```

encoding-xml-Parse.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    src := "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<library xmlns:b=\"urn:books\">\n  <!-- the list -->\n  <b:book id=\"1\" lang=\"en\"><title>Dune</title><year>1965</year></b:book>\n  <b:book id=\"2\"><title>Solaris</title></b:book>\n</library>"
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse(src, err)
    println err.ok, d.version, xml.NodeCount(d) > 0
    r := xml.Root(d)
    println xml.Name(d, r), xml.Kind(d, r) == xml.KindElement, xml.Parent(d, r) == xml.DocumentNode(d)
    mut books := xml.Elements(d, r)
    println books.items.len()
    b := books.items[0]
    println xml.Name(d, b), xml.LocalName(d, b), xml.Prefix(d, b), xml.NamespaceURI(d, b)
    println xml.Line(d, b), xml.Column(d, b), xml.Depth(d, b), xml.Path(d, b)
    println xml.AttributeCount(d, b), xml.HasAttribute(d, b, "lang"), xml.AttributeValue(d, b, "id")
    a := xml.AttributeAt(d, b, 1)
    println a.name, a.value
    t := xml.FirstElementNamed(d, b, "title")
    println xml.Text(d, t), xml.Text(d, b), xml.IsElement(d, t)
    println xml.ChildCount(d, b), xml.Name(d, xml.ChildAt(d, b, 1))
    println xml.Name(d, xml.NextSibling(d, t)), xml.PreviousSibling(d, t)
    mut all := xml.Descendants(d, r)
    mut named := xml.ElementsNamed(d, r, "b:book")
    mut up := xml.Ancestors(d, t)
    mut kids := xml.ChildNodes(d, r)
    println all.items.len(), named.items.len(), up.items.len(), kids.items.len()
    println xml.Exists(d, 9999), xml.Value(d, xml.ChildAt(d, t, 0))
    xml.FreeList(all)
    xml.FreeList(named)
    xml.FreeList(up)
    xml.FreeList(kids)
    xml.FreeList(books)
    _ := xml.Parse("<a><b></a>", err)
    println err.ok, err.line, xml.ErrorText(err)
    println xml.WellFormed("<x/>", err)
    xml.Free(d)
    mut o := xml.DefaultOptions()
    o.keep_comments = false
    mut d2 := xml.ParseWith("<!DOCTYPE p [<!ENTITY site \"hello\">]><p xmlns:x=\"urn:x\" x:id=\"7\">&site; <b>b</b> end</p>", o, err)
    p := xml.Root(d2)
    println err.ok, xml.EntityCount(d2), xml.EntityValue(d2, "site")
    println "[" + xml.DirectText(d2, p) + "]", xml.AttributeValueNS(d2, p, "urn:x", "id")
    println xml.EntityDepthLimit, xml.EntityExpansionLimit, o.max_depth
    xml.Free(d2)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 1.0 true
library true true
2
b:book book b urn:books
4 3 2 /library[1]/b:book[1]
2 true 1
lang en
Dune Dune1965 true
2 year
year -1
9 2 3 3
false Dune
false 1 line 1, column 7: </a> closes <b>
true
true 1 hello
[hello  end] 7
32 262144 1024
```

### `ParseOptions`

```salam
struct ParseOptions
```

The parse options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `preserve_whitespace` | `bool = false` | Keep text nodes that are only whitespace. |
| `keep_comments` | `bool = true` | Keep the comments. |
| `keep_instructions` | `bool = true` | Keep the processing instructions. |
| `namespaces` | `bool = true` | Resolve the namespaces. |
| `expand_entities` | `bool = true` | Replace entities with their values. |
| `max_depth` | `int = 1024` | The greatest element depth. |
| `max_entity_depth` | `int` | The greatest depth of nested entities. |
| `max_entity_expansion` | `int` | The greatest text length after entities are expanded; a guard against the "entity bomb" attack. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-xml-Parse.salam

### `XMLNode`

```salam
struct XMLNode
```

A simple node: one element with its attributes, children and text; for small jobs without a document.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tag` | `str = ""` | The element name. |
| `attrs` | `HashMap` | The attributes. |
| `children` | `Vector` | The child elements. |
| `text` | `str = ""` | The text of the element. |

encoding-xml-Simple.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml
import encoding.value

func main:
    n := xml.Decode("<config env=\"prod\"><db host=\"localhost\" port=\"5432\"/><feature>search</feature><feature>chat</feature></config>")
    println n.tag, xml.HasAttr(n, "env"), xml.Attr(n, "env")
    db := xml.Child(n, "db")
    println xml.Found(db), xml.Attr(db, "port"), xml.Found(xml.Child(n, "cache"))
    feats := xml.Children(n, "feature")
    println feats.items.len(), feats.items[1].text
    mut item := xml.NewXMLNode("item")
    xml.SetAttr(item, "id", "3")
    mut name := xml.NewXMLNode("name")
    name.text = "book"
    xml.AppendChild(item, name)
    println xml.Encode(item)
    println xml.EncodeIndent(item, "  ")
    println xml.EncodeDeclaration(item)
    println xml.Valid("<a><b/></a>"), xml.Valid("<a><b></a>")
    mut ok := false
    _ := xml.DecodeStrict("<a>", ok)
    println ok
    v := xml.ToValue(n)
    println value.ToDebugString(v)
    println xml.Encode(xml.FromValue(v, "root"))
    println xml.EscapeText("a < b & c"), xml.EscapeAttr(`"x"`), xml.UnescapeEntities("&lt;p&gt; &amp; &#115;")
    mut tz := xml.NewXMLTokenizer("<a x=\"1\">hello<!--c--></a>")
    until true:
        t := xml.NextToken(tz)
        if t.kind == xml.XMLTokEOF or t.kind == xml.XMLTokError:
            break
        end
        println t.kind, t.tag, t.text
    end
    println xml.XMLTokStartElement, xml.XMLTokEndElement, xml.XMLTokText, xml.XMLTokComment, xml.XMLTokCData
end
```

Output:

```text
config true prod
true 5432 false
2 chat
<item id="3"><name>book</name></item>
<item id="3">
  <name>book</name>
</item>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<item id="3"><name>book</name></item>
true false
false
object{feature: array[string(search), string(chat)], @env: string(prod), db: object{@port: string(5432), @host: string(localhost)}}
<root env="prod"><feature>search</feature><feature>chat</feature><db host="localhost" port="5432"/></root>
a &lt; b &amp; c &quot;x&quot; <p> & s
1 a
3  hello
4  c
2 a
1 2 3 4 5
```

### `XPathValue`

```salam
struct XPathValue
```

The result of an XPath evaluation: a node set, a string, a number or a boolean.

| Name | Type | Description |

encoding-xml-XPath.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse("<shop><item price=\"120\">tea</item><item price=\"80\">sugar</item><item price=\"45\">bread</item></shop>", err)
    r := xml.DocumentNode(d)
    mut cheap := xml.Select(d, r, "//item[@price < 100]", err)
    println cheap.items.len()
    each n in cheap.items:
        println xml.Text(d, n)
    end
    xml.FreeList(cheap)
    println xml.SelectString(d, r, "/shop/item[1]", err), xml.SelectNumber(d, r, "sum(//item/@price)", err), xml.SelectBoolean(d, r, "count(//item) = 3", err)
    last := xml.SelectFirst(d, r, "//item[last()]", err)
    println xml.NodeName(d, last), xml.StringValue(d, last)
    mut v := xml.Evaluate(d, r, "//item/@price", err)
    println v.kind == xml.ValueNodeSet, v.nodes.items.len()
    first := v.nodes.items[0]
    println xml.IsAttributeRef(first), xml.ReferencedAttribute(d, first).value, xml.IsAttributeRef(xml.AttributeRef(0))
    xml.FreeValue(v)
    num := xml.Evaluate(d, r, "string-length('hello')", err)
    println num.kind == xml.ValueNumber, num.number, xml.ValueString, xml.ValueBoolean
    _ := xml.Select(d, r, "//item[@", err)
    println err.ok
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
2
sugar
bread
tea 245 true
item bread
true 3
true 120 true
true 5 1 3
false
```

### `Node`

```salam
struct Node
```

One node: an element, text, a comment and so on.

| Name | Type | Description |

| `uri` | `str = ""` | The namespace URI. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The text of text nodes, comments and the like. |
| `parent` | `int = -1` | The id of the parent; -1 for the document node. |
| `children` | `Vector` | The ids of the children. |
| `attrs` | `Vector` | The indices of the attributes. |
| `line` | `int = 0` | The line number in the text. |
| `col` | `int = 0` | The column number in the text. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-xml-Parse.salam

### `Document`

```salam
struct Document
```

One XML document, parsed or built. Nodes are taken out of it by number, their id.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `Vector` | Every node; the id of a node is its index in this vector. |
| `attributes` | `Vector` | Every attribute. |
| `version` | `str = ""` | The version in the `<?xml ...?>` declaration. |
| `encoding` | `str = ""` | The encoding in the declaration. |
| `standalone` | `str = ""` | The `standalone` value in the declaration. |
| `doctype` | `str = ""` | The name of the root element in `<!DOCTYPE>`. |
| `doctype_public` | `str = ""` | The public identifier of the DOCTYPE. |
| `doctype_system` | `str = ""` | The system identifier of the DOCTYPE. |
| `internal_subset` | `str = ""` | The text of the internal subset of the DOCTYPE, between `[` and `]`. |
| `entity_names` | `Vector` | The names of the defined entities. |
| `entity_values` | `Vector` | The values of the entities. |
| `owned` | `Vector` | The strings the document holds. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-xml-Parse.salam

### `NodeList`

```salam
struct NodeList
```

A list of node ids.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The ids. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: encoding-xml-Parse.salam
