# encoding/protobuf

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-protobuf/

Reading `.proto` files, the Protocol Buffers wire encoding, and generating Salam code from them.

Protocol Buffers is Google's binary format for structured messages. The shape of the messages is defined in a `.proto` file, and this package reads it, generates Salam code for the messages and services, and also carries the low level tools for writing and reading fields.

In the bytes, every field comes as a tag, the field number and the wire type, followed by its value. Numbers are usually written as a varint: each byte holds 7 bits of the number and its top bit says whether another byte follows.

## Types

### `PTokenStream`

```salam
struct PTokenStream
```

The tokens of a text.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toks` | `Vector` | The tokens. |

encoding-protobuf-Parse.salam

```salam
import encoding.protobuf

func main:
    src := "syntax = \"proto3\";\npackage shop;\n\nenum Status { OPEN = 0; DONE = 1; }\n\nmessage Order {\n  int64 id = 1;\n  repeated string items = 2;\n  map<string, int32> counts = 3;\n  Status status = 4;\n  oneof pay { string card = 5; bool cash = 6; }\n}\n\nservice Orders {\n  rpc Get (Order) returns (Order);\n  rpc Watch (Order) returns (stream Order);\n}\n"
    mut ok := false
    p := protobuf.ParseFile(src, ok)
    println ok, p.packageName, p.messages.len(), p.enums.len(), p.services.len(), p.imports.len()
    msg := p.messages[0]
    println msg.name, msg.fields.len(), msg.oneofs[0].name, msg.oneofs[0].fieldIndices
    each f in msg.fields:
        println f.number, f.name, protobuf.FieldKindName(f.kind), f.typeName, f.repeated, f.oneofIndex
    end
    m := msg.fields[2]
    println m.kind == protobuf.FK_MAP, protobuf.FieldKindName(m.keyKind), protobuf.FieldKindName(m.mapValueKind)
    e := p.enums[0]
    println e.name, e.values[1].name, e.values[1].number
    s := p.services[0]
    println s.name, s.methods[1].name, s.methods[1].inputType, s.methods[1].serverStream, s.methods[1].clientStream
    println protobuf.ScalarKindFromName("sint64") == protobuf.FK_SINT64, protobuf.ScalarKindFromName("Order")
    mut toks := protobuf.Tokenize("message A { int32 x = 1; }", ok)
    println ok, toks.toks.len(), toks.toks[0].lexeme, toks.toks[0].kind == protobuf.PTK_IDENT, toks.toks[2].kind == protobuf.PTK_LBRACE
    println toks.toks[6].ival, toks.toks[6].line
    _ := protobuf.ParseFile("message {", ok)
    println ok
end
```

Output:

```text
true shop 1 1 1 0
Order 6 pay [4, 5]
1 id int64  false -1
2 items string  true -1
3 counts map  false -1
4 status message Status false -1
5 card string  false 0
6 cash bool  false 0
true string int32
Status DONE 1
Orders Watch Order true false
true 0
true 10 message true true
1 1
false
```

### `PField`

```salam
struct PField
```

One message field.

| Name | Type | Description |

## Constants and variables

### Wire types `WT_…`

How a field value is written in the bytes: varint, 8 fixed bytes, length prefixed or 4 fixed bytes.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `WT_VARINT` | `0` |
| `WT_FIXED64` | `1` |
| `WT_LEN` | `2` |
| `WT_FIXED32` | `5` |

encoding-protobuf-Wire.salam

```salam
import encoding.protobuf
import compress

func main:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    protobuf.WriteTag(b, 1, protobuf.WT_VARINT)
    protobuf.WriteVarint(b, 150 as u64)
    println compress.BufToBase64(b), protobuf.MakeTag(1, 0), protobuf.MakeTag(2, protobuf.WT_LEN)
    protobuf.WriteTag(b, 2, protobuf.WT_LEN)
    protobuf.WriteLenPrefixedStr(b, "hello")
    protobuf.WriteTag(b, 3, protobuf.WT_FIXED32)
    protobuf.WriteFixed32(b, 7 as u32)
    protobuf.WriteTag(b, 4, protobuf.WT_FIXED64)
    protobuf.WriteFixed64(b, 9 as u64)
    protobuf.WriteFloat(b, 0.5)
    protobuf.WriteDouble(b, 2.25)
    protobuf.WriteLenPrefixedBytes(b, b.data, 2)
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(b)
    mut good := true
    mut number := 0
    mut wire := 0
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, number, wire, good)
    println number, wire, protobuf.ReadVarint(r, good)
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, number, wire, good)
    println number, protobuf.ReadLenPrefixedStr(r, good)
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, number, wire, good)
    protobuf.SkipField(r, wire, good)
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, number, wire, good)
    println number, protobuf.ReadFixed64(r, good)
    println protobuf.ReadFloat(r, good), protobuf.ReadDouble(r, good)
    b2 := protobuf.ReadLenPrefixedBuf(r, good)
    println compress.BufLen(b2), good
    _ := protobuf.ReadVarint(r, good)
    println good
    println protobuf.ZigZagEncode32(-1), protobuf.ZigZagDecode32(3 as u32), protobuf.ZigZagEncode64(-2), protobuf.ZigZagDecode64(4 as u64)
    mut b3 := compress.NewByteBuf()
    protobuf.WriteFixed32(b3, 42 as u32)
    mut r3 := compress.ReaderFromBuf(b3)
    good = true
    println protobuf.ReadFixed32(r3, good)
    compress.BufFree(b)
    compress.BufFree(b3)
end
```

Output:

```text
CJYB 8 18
1 0 150
2 hello
4 9
0.5 2.25
2 true
false
1 -2 3 2
42
```

```salam

```

Generates Salam code from `.proto` text: one struct per message, with its serialising functions.

encoding-protobuf-Generate.salam

```salam
import encoding.protobuf
import str

func main:
    src := "syntax = \"proto3\";\nmessage Ping { string text = 1; }\nservice Echo {\n  rpc Say (Ping) returns (Ping);\n  rpc Stream (stream Ping) returns (stream Ping);\n}\n"
    mut ok := false
    code := protobuf.GenerateSingle(src, ok)
    println ok, str.Contains(code, "struct Ping")
    p := protobuf.ParseFile(src, ok)
    println protobuf.ServiceCount(p), protobuf.ServiceNameAt(p, 0), protobuf.ServiceMethodCount(p, 0)
    println protobuf.ServiceMethodSignature(p, 0, 0)
    println protobuf.ServiceMethodSignature(p, 0, 1)
    println str.Contains(protobuf.GenerateServices(p), "Echo")
    all := protobuf.GenerateWithServices(src, ok)
    println ok, str.Len(all) > str.Len(code)
    println protobuf.ServiceSummary(src, ok)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
1 Echo 2
Say(Ping) returns (Ping)
Stream(stream Ping) returns (stream Ping)
true
true true
service Echo (2 methods)
  rpc Say(Ping) returns (Ping)
  rpc Stream(stream Ping) returns (stream Ping)
```

# compress

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/compress/

Byte buffers, compression methods from RLE through DEFLATE, gzip and checksums.

This package is the base of all binary data work in Salam: `ByteBuf` and `ByteReader` are what packages such as encoding/binary, archive and encoding/msgpack pass around.

For compression, reach for gzip when the data has to be read by other programs. The other methods are mostly there to learn from and experiment with, and their output format belongs to this package alone. The examples show that for small data the overhead of Huffman and DEFLATE comes to more than the data itself.

## Types

### `Method`

```salam
enum Method
```

The compression method, as an enum.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `` | No compression. |
| `RLE` | `` | Run length encoding. |
| `Huffman` | `` | Huffman. |
| `LZ77` | `` | LZ77. |
| `LZW` | `` | LZW. |
| `Deflate` | `` | LZ77 and Huffman. |
| `BWT` | `` | Burrows Wheeler. |

compress-Methods.salam

```salam
import compress

func main:
    text := "ababababab hello hello hello hello hello hello hello hello"
    b := compress.BufFromStr(text)
    each method in [compress.MethodNone, compress.MethodRLE, compress.MethodHuffman, compress.MethodLZ77, compress.MethodLZW, compress.MethodDeflate, compress.MethodBWT]:
        mut c := compress.CompressBuf(method, b)
        mut back := compress.DecompressBuf(method, c)
        println method, compress.BufLen(c), compress.BufEquals(b, back)
        compress.BufFree(c)
        compress.BufFree(back)
    end
    mut best := 0
    c := compress.CompressBest(b.data, b.len, best)
    println best, compress.Ratio(c.len, b.len) < 1.0
    s := compress.CompressStr(compress.MethodDeflate, "aaaaaaaaaa")
    b3 := compress.Decompress(compress.MethodDeflate, s.data, s.len)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(b3)
    b4 := compress.Compress(compress.MethodRLE, b.data, b.len)
    println compress.BufLen(b4) > 0, compress.Method.Huffman
    println compress.BufLen(compress.RLEDecompress(compress.RLECompress(b.data, b.len).data, compress.RLECompress(b.data, b.len).len)) == b.len
    h := compress.HuffmanCompress(b.data, b.len)
    println compress.BufEquals(compress.HuffmanDecompress(h.data, h.len), b)
    l := compress.LZ77Compress(b.data, b.len)
    println compress.BufEquals(compress.LZ77Decompress(l.data, l.len), b)
    w := compress.LZWCompress(b.data, b.len)
    println compress.BufEquals(compress.LZWDecompress(w.data, w.len), b)
    bw := compress.BWTCompress(b.data, b.len)
    println compress.BufEquals(compress.BWTDecompress(bw.data, bw.len), b)
    mut primary := 0
    t := compress.BWTTransform(b.data, 3, primary)
    println primary, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(compress.BWTInverse(t.data, t.len, primary)) == "aba"
    m := compress.MTFEncode(b)
    println compress.BufEquals(compress.MTFDecode(m), b)
end
```

Output:

```text
0 62 true
1 63 true
2 281 true
3 22 true
4 35 true
5 545 true
6 282 true
3 true
aaaaaaaaaa
true 2
true
true
true
true
true
1 true
true
```

### `ByteBuf`

```salam
struct ByteBuf
```

A byte buffer: an array of bytes that grows by itself. Most packages in this group take and give binary data in one.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `void*` | The memory address of the bytes. |
| `len` | `int = 0` | The number of bytes. |
| `cap` | `int = 0` | The capacity. |

compress-Buffer.salam

```salam
import compress

func main:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBufCap(16)
    compress.BufPush(b, 72)
    compress.BufPush(b, 105)
    mut other := compress.BufFromStr("!!")
    compress.BufPushBuf(b, other)
    compress.BufPushBytes(b, other.data, 1)
    compress.BufPushU32(b, 10)
    println compress.BufLen(b), compress.BufGet(b, 0), compress.BufToBase64(b)
    compress.BufSet(b, 0, 104)
    c := compress.BufClone(b)
    println compress.BufEquals(b, c), compress.BufToStrUnsafe(compress.BufFromStr("hello"))
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(b)
    println compress.RdLeft(r), compress.RdByte(r), compress.RdByte(r)
    three := compress.RdBytes(r, 3)
    println compress.BufLen(three), compress.RdU32(r), compress.RdLeft(r), r.bad
    _ := compress.RdByte(r)
    println r.bad
    mut r2 := compress.NewByteReader(c.data, 2)
    println compress.RdByte(r2)
    compress.BufReset(b)
    println compress.BufLen(b)
    compress.BufFree(b)
    compress.BufFree(c)
    compress.BufFree(other)
end
```

Output:

```text
9 72 SGkhISEAAAAK
true hello
9 104 105
3 10 0 false
true
104
0
```

### `BitWriter`

```salam
struct BitWriter
```

A writer of bits; it fills each byte from the least significant bit.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `buf` | `ByteBuf` | The bytes written. |
| `acc` | `int = 0` | The bits waiting. |
| `nbits` | `int = 0` | The number of bits waiting. |

compress-Bits.salam

```salam
import compress

func main:
    mut w := compress.NewBitWriter()
    compress.BitWriteBit(w, 1)
    compress.BitWriteBits(w, 5, 3)
    compress.BitWriteBits(w, 255, 8)
    compress.BitFlush(w)
    println compress.BitWriterLen(w)
    mut r := compress.BitReaderFromBuf(w.buf)
    println compress.BitReadBit(r), compress.BitReadBits(r, 3), compress.BitReadBits(r, 8)
    mut r2 := compress.NewBitReader(w.buf.data, 1)
    println compress.BitReadBits(r2, 4)
    compress.BitWriterFree(w)
end
```

Output:

```text
2
1 5 255
11
```

### `GzipCompress`

```salam

```

compress-Gzip.salam

```salam
import compress

func main:
    text := "hello gzip! hello gzip! hello gzip!"
    g := compress.GzipCompressStr(text)
    println compress.BufGet(g, 0), compress.BufGet(g, 1)
    mut ok := false
    b := compress.GzipDecompressBuf(g, ok)
    println ok, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(b) == text
    b2 := compress.BufFromStr(text)
    g2 := compress.GzipCompressBuf(b2)
    g3 := compress.GzipCompress(b2.data, b2.len)
    println compress.BufEquals(g2, g3)
    _ := compress.GzipDecompress(b2.data, b2.len, ok)
    println ok
    d := compress.DeflateCompress(b2.data, b2.len)
    println compress.BufEquals(compress.DeflateDecompress(d.data, d.len), b2)
    raw := compress.RawDeflate(b2.data, b2.len)
    back := compress.RawInflate(raw.data, raw.len, b2.len, ok)
    println ok, compress.BufEquals(back, b2)
end
```

Output:

```text
31 139
true true
true
false
true
true true
```

# archive

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/archive/

Making and opening zip and tar archives, reading RAR, and gzipping a file.

An archive gathers several files into one. Zip compresses each file on its own; tar only puts the files one after another and is usually gzipped afterwards (`.tar.gz`).

The functions work both in memory and on files. They take the archive data as an address and a length, such as `b.data` and `b.len` of a byte buffer.

## Types

### `TarFileInput`

```salam
struct TarFileInput
```

One file to put in a tar.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name inside the archive. |
| `data_ptr` | `void*` | The address of the contents. |
| `data_len` | `int = 0` | The length of the contents. |
| `is_dir` | `bool = false` | The input is a directory. |

archive-Tar.salam

```salam
import archive
import compress

func main:
    b := compress.BufFromStr("first line\nsecond line\n")
    mut files := Vector {} as Vector<archive.TarFileInput>
    files.push(archive.MakeTarFileInput("notes", null, 0, true))
    files.push(archive.MakeTarFileInput("notes/a.txt", b.data, b.len, false))
    t := archive.TarCreate(files)
    println t.len % 512
    mut entries := archive.TarList(t.data, t.len)
    each e in entries:
        println e.name, e.size, e.is_dir
    end
    archive.FreeEntries(entries)
    mut ok := false
    a := archive.TarExtractByName(t.data, t.len, "notes/a.txt", ok)
    println ok, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(a)
    println archive.TarCreateFile(files, "out.tar"), archive.TarExtractAll(t.data, t.len, "untarred")
    println archive.GzipCompressFile("out.tar", "out.tar.gz"), archive.GzipDecompressFile("out.tar.gz", "back.tar")
    back := archive.ReadBinaryFile("back.tar", ok)
    println ok, back.len == t.len
    archive.EnsureDir("a/b/c")
    println archive.WriteBinaryFile("a/b/c/x.bin", b.data, 3), archive.WriteBinaryFileBuf("a/b/c/y.bin", b)
    mut b2 := compress.NewByteBuf()
    archive.LEPut16(b2, 513)
    archive.LEPut32(b2, 70000)
    println archive.LEGet16(b2.data, 0), archive.LEGet32(b2.data, 2)
end
```

Output:

```text
0
notes 0 true
notes/a.txt 23 false
true first line
second line

true true
true true
true true
true true
513 70000
```

### `Entry`

```salam
struct Entry
```

One archive entry.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name and path inside the archive. |
| `size` | `i64 = 0` | The original size in bytes. |
| `compressed_size` | `i64 = 0` | The compressed size. |
| `is_dir` | `bool = false` | The entry is a directory. |
| `method` | `int = 0` | The compression method: zero for plain storage, 8 for DEFLATE. |
| `crc32` | `u32 = 0` | The checksum of the contents. |
| `mtime` | `i64 = 0` | The modification time in seconds since the Unix epoch. |

archive-Zip.salam

```salam
import archive
import compress

func main:
    text := "hello archive, hello archive, hello archive"
    b := compress.BufFromStr(text)
    mut files := Vector {} as Vector<archive.ZipFileInput>
    files.push(archive.MakeZipFileInput("docs/", null, 0, 0))
    files.push(archive.MakeZipFileInput("docs/a.txt", b.data, b.len, 8))
    files.push(archive.MakeZipFileInput("b.txt", b.data, 5, 0))
    z := archive.ZipCreate(files)
    mut entries := archive.ZipList(z.data, z.len)
    each e in entries:
        println e.name, e.size, e.compressed_size < e.size, e.is_dir, e.method
    end
    archive.FreeEntries(entries)
    mut ok := false
    a := archive.ZipExtractByName(z.data, z.len, "docs/a.txt", ok)
    println ok, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(a) == text
    _ := archive.ZipExtractByName(z.data, z.len, "missing", ok)
    println ok
    println archive.ZipCreateFile(files, "out.zip"), archive.ZipExtractAll(z.data, z.len, "unzipped")
    read := archive.ReadBinaryFile("unzipped/docs/a.txt", ok)
    println ok, read.len == b.len
    println archive.IsRar(z.data, z.len), archive.RarList(z.data, z.len).len()
    _ := archive.RarExtractByName(z.data, z.len, "x", ok)
    println ok, archive.RarExtractAll(z.data, z.len, "rar-out")
end
```

Output:

```text
docs/ 0 false true 0
docs/a.txt 43 true false 8
b.txt 5 false false 0
true true
false
true true
true true
false 0
false true
```

# npy

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/npy/

Reading and writing NumPy `.npy` and `.npz` files.

`.npy` files are the standard way NumPy arrays are stored in Python, and `.npz` keeps several named arrays in one zip archive. With this package you can move data and model weights between Python and Salam.

## Types

### `NpyArray`

```salam
struct NpyArray
```

One multi dimensional NumPy array. The data is always held in memory as 64 bit floats.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `Vector` | The size of each dimension, such as `[2, 3]`. |
| `dtype` | `int` | The data type in the file; one of the `NPY_` constants. |
| `data` | `Vector` | The elements in row order. |

npy-Npy.salam

```salam
import npy
import matrix

func main:
    mut m := matrix.Matrix { rows = 2, cols = 3 }
    repeat 6 in i:
        m.a.push(i as f64)
    end
    mut a := npy.FromMatrix(m)
    println a.shape, a.ndim(), a.count(), a.dtype == npy.NPY_F64
    bytes := npy.WriteNpy(a)
    println bytes.len > 64
    mut good := false
    mut back := npy.ReadNpy(bytes.data, bytes.len, good)
    println good, back.shape, back.data
    m2 := npy.ToMatrix(back, good)
    println good, m2.at(1, 2)
    println npy.WriteNpyFile(a, "a.npy")
    mut from_file := npy.ReadNpyFile("a.npy", good)
    println good, from_file.count()
    mut keys := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    keys.push("x")
    keys.push("y")
    mut arrays := Vector {} as Vector<npy.NpyArray>
    arrays.push(a)
    arrays.push(back)
    println npy.NpzWrite("ab.npz", keys, arrays)
    println npy.NpzList("ab.npz", good), good
    mut y := npy.NpzRead("ab.npz", "y", good)
    println good, y.shape
    println npy.NPY_F32, npy.NPY_I8, npy.NPY_I16, npy.NPY_I32, npy.NPY_I64, npy.NPY_U8, npy.NPY_U16, npy.NPY_U32, npy.NPY_BOOL
    y.free()
    from_file.free()
    back.free()
    a.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
[2, 3] 2 6 true
true
true [2, 3] [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
true 5
true
true 6
true
["x", "y"] true
true [2, 3]
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9
```

#### `ndim`

```salam
func ndim(): int
```

The number of dimensions.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: npy-Npy.salam

#### `count`

```salam

```

The total number of elements.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: npy-Npy.salam

#### `free`

```salam

```

Frees the memory of the array.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: npy-Npy.salam

## Constants and variables

### Data types `NPY_…`

The type of the elements in the file: 8 and 4 byte floats, 1 to 8 byte signed and unsigned integers, and boolean.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `NPY_F64` | `0` |
| `NPY_F32` | `1` |
| `NPY_I8` | `2` |
| `NPY_I16` | `3` |
| `NPY_I32` | `4` |
| `NPY_I64` | `5` |
| `NPY_U8` | `6` |
| `NPY_U16` | `7` |
| `NPY_U32` | `8` |
| `NPY_BOOL` | `9` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: npy-Npy.salam

# excel

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/excel/

Reading and writing Excel spreadsheets (xlsx and xls), OpenDocument (ods) and CSV.

A workbook holds several sheets, and each sheet holds cells by row and column, from zero. Turn Excel references such as `C5` into a row and column with `CellRef` and `ParseCellRef`.

`Open` and `Save` work the format out from the file extension. Formulas are stored and read with their last calculated result, but Salam does not evaluate a formula itself.

## Types

### `Style`

```salam
struct Style
```

The style of a cell.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bold` | `bool = false` | Bold. |
| `italic` | `bool = false` | Italic. |
| `underline` | `bool = false` | Underlined. |
| `font_name` | `str = "Calibri"` | The font name. |
| `font_size` | `int = 11` | The font size. |
| `font_color` | `str = ""` | The text colour as hex, such as `FF0000`. |
| `bg_color` | `str = ""` | The background colour. |
| `align_h` | `int = 0` | The horizontal alignment. |
| `align_v` | `int = 0` | The vertical alignment. |
| `num_format` | `str = ""` | The number display format, such as `0.00`. |

excel-Cell.salam

```salam
import excel

func main:
    println excel.ColumnLabel(0), excel.ColumnLabel(25), excel.ColumnLabel(26), excel.ColumnLabel(703)
    println excel.ColumnIndex("A"), excel.ColumnIndex("AA"), excel.CellRef(4, 2)
    mut row := 0
    mut col := 0
    println excel.ParseCellRef("C5", row, col), row, col, excel.ParseCellRef("5C", row, col)
    serial := excel.EpochToSerial(0)
    println serial, excel.SerialToEpoch(45371.0)
    text := excel.NewStringCell(0, 0, "some text")
    number := excel.NewNumberCell(0, 1, 3.5)
    flag := excel.NewBoolCell(0, 2, false)
    date := excel.NewDateCell(0, 3, 0)
    formula := excel.NewFormulaCell(0, 4, "A1*2", 7.0)
    println text.kind == excel.CellString, number.num, flag.flag, date.kind == excel.CellDate, formula.formula, formula.num
    println excel.CellEmpty, excel.CellNumber, excel.CellBool, excel.CellFormula
    mut styles := excel.NewStyleSheet()
    bold := excel.Style { bold = true, bg_color = "FFFF00", align_h = excel.AlignCenter }
    id := styles.get_or_add(bold)
    println id, styles.get_or_add(bold) == id, styles.count(), styles.get(id).bold
    println bold.equals(styles.get(id)), bold.font_name, bold.font_size
    println excel.AlignDefault, excel.AlignLeft, excel.AlignRight, excel.AlignTop, excel.AlignMiddle, excel.AlignBottom
    styles.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
A Z AA AAB
0 26 C5
true 4 2 false
25569 1710892800
true 3.5 false true A1*2 7
0 2 3 5
1 true 2 true
true Calibri 11
0 1 3 1 2 3
```

excel-Sheet.salam

```salam
import excel

func main:
    mut sheet := excel.NewSheet("sales")
    sheet.set_string(0, 0, "item")
    sheet.set_string(0, 1, "count")
    sheet.set_cell(1, 0, "tea")
    sheet.set_int(1, 1, 12)
    sheet.set_cell(2, 0, "sugar")
    sheet.set_number(2, 1, 4.5)
    sheet.set_bool(3, 0, true)
    sheet.set_date(3, 1, 1710943509)
    sheet.set_formula(4, 1, "SUM(B2:B3)", 16.5)
    sheet.set_error(5, 0, "#DIV/0!")
    println sheet.name, sheet.row_count(), sheet.col_count()
    println sheet.get_string(1, 0), sheet.get_number(1, 1), sheet.get_number(2, 1), sheet.get_bool(3, 0), sheet.get_formula(4, 1)
    cell := sheet.get_cell(5, 0)
    println cell.kind == excel.CellError, cell.text, sheet.get_cell(3, 1).kind == excel.CellDate
    println sheet.has_cell(1, 1), sheet.has_cell(9, 9)
    sheet.clear_cell(5, 0)
    println sheet.has_cell(5, 0)
    mut row := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    row.push("bread")
    row.push("7")
    sheet.set_row(6, row)
    sheet.set_column(3, row)
    mut table := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    each value in ["a", "b", "c", "d"]:
        table.push(value)
    end
    sheet.set_table(8, 0, table, 2)
    println sheet.get_row(6).len(), sheet.get_column(3).len(), sheet.get_all().len()
    println sheet.get_string(9, 1)
    found := sheet.find("bread")
    println found.len(), found[0].row, found[0].col
    println sheet.filter_rows_equals(0, "tea")
    sheet.merge_cells(0, 0, 0, 1)
    mut hit := false
    range := sheet.merged_range(0, 1, hit)
    println sheet.is_merged(0, 1), hit, range.row1, range.col2, sheet.merges.len()
    sheet.set_style(1, 1, 2)
    println sheet.get_cell(1, 1).style_id, sheet.max_row, sheet.max_col, sheet.cells.size() > 0
    sheet.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
sales 6 2
tea 12 4.5 true SUM(B2:B3)
true #DIV/0! true
true false
false
4 10 40
d
2 0 3
[1]
true true 0 1 1
2 9 3 true
```

### `Workbook`

```salam
struct Workbook
```

A workbook: several sheets, the style table and the file format.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sheets` | `Vector` | The sheets in order. |
| `styles` | `StyleSheet` | The styles shared by the cells. |
| `active_sheet` | `int = 0` | The index of the active sheet. |
| `source_path` | `str = ""` | The path of the file the workbook was read from. |
| `format` | `int = 0` | The file format; one of the `Format` constants. |
| `last_error` | `str = ""` | The last error message. |

excel-Workbook.salam

```salam
import excel

func main:
    mut book := excel.NewWorkbook()
    mut a := book.add_sheet("A")
    a.set_string(0, 0, "hello")
    a.set_number(0, 1, 2.5)
    mut b := book.add_sheet("B")
    b.set_int(0, 0, 42)
    println book.sheet_count(), book.sheet_names(), book.sheet_index("B"), book.sheet_at(0).name
    println book.rename_sheet(1, "second"), book.sheet("second").get_number(0, 0)
    println book.set_active(1), book.active().name, book.active_sheet
    println excel.WriteXLSX(book, "book.xlsx"), excel.WriteODS(book, "book.ods"), book.save("copy.xlsx"), excel.Save(book, "book.csv")
    println excel.DetectFormat("book.xlsx") == excel.FormatXLSX, excel.DetectFormat("book.ods") == excel.FormatODS, excel.DetectFormat("a.txt"), excel.FormatXLS, excel.FormatCSV, excel.FormatUnknown
    mut ok := false
    mut err := ""
    mut read := excel.Open("book.xlsx", ok, err)
    println ok, read.sheet_names(), read.sheet("A").get_string(0, 0), read.format == excel.FormatXLSX
    mut copy := excel.ReadXLSX("copy.xlsx", ok, err)
    mut ods := excel.ReadODS("book.ods", ok, err)
    println ok, ods.sheet("second").get_number(0, 0), copy.sheet_count()
    mut meta := excel.Inspect("book.xlsx", ok, err)
    println ok, meta.exists, meta.size > 0, meta.sheet_names, meta.sheet_rows, meta.sheet_cols
    meta.free()
    mut csv := excel.ReadCSVWorkbook("book.csv", ok, err)
    println ok, csv.sheet_at(0).get_string(0, 0), excel.WriteCSVWorkbook(csv, "again.csv")
    _ := excel.Open("missing.xlsx", ok, err)
    println ok, err != ""
    _ := excel.ReadXLS("missing.xls", ok, err)
    println ok, excel.IsXLS(null, 0)
    println book.remove_sheet_named("A"), book.remove_sheet(5), book.remove_sheet(0), book.sheet_count()
    mut fresh := excel.New()
    println fresh.sheet_count()
    fresh.free()
    read.free()
    copy.free()
    ods.free()
    csv.free()
    book.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
2 ["A", "B"] 1 A
true 42
true second 1
true true true true
true true 0 2 4 0
true ["A", "second"] hello true
true 42 2
true true true ["A", "second"] [1, 1] [2, 1]
true 42 true
false true
false false
true false true 0
0
```

excel-Convert.salam

```salam
import excel

func main:
    mut sheet := excel.CSVToSheet("name,score\nAli,17\n\"Sara, A\",19.5\n", "scores")
    println sheet.name, sheet.row_count(), sheet.get_string(2, 0), sheet.get_number(2, 1)
    println excel.SheetToCSV(sheet)
    println excel.SheetToJSON(sheet)
    mut from_json := excel.JSONToSheet(`[["a", "b"], ["1", "x"], ["2", "y"]]`, "data")
    println from_json.row_count(), from_json.col_count(), from_json.get_string(0, 1), from_json.get_string(2, 0)
    xml := "<row r=\"2\"><c r=\"A2\" t=\"s\"><v>0</v></c><br/></row>"
    start := excel.XmlFind(xml, "c", 0)
    println start, excel.XmlAttr(xml, start, "r"), excel.XmlTagEnd(xml, start)
    println excel.XmlInner(xml, "v", 0), excel.XmlSelfClosing(xml, excel.XmlFind(xml, "br", 0))
    println excel.XmlFindClose(xml, "row", 10)
    println excel.XmlEscape("a<b&c"), excel.XmlUnescape("a&lt;b&amp;c")
    sheet.free()
    from_json.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
scores 3 Sara, A 0
name,score
Ali,17
"Sara, A",19.5
[["name", "score"], ["Ali", "17"], ["Sara, A", "19.5"]]
3 2 b 2
11 A2 27
0 true
44
a&lt;b&amp;c a<b&c
```

# data

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/data/

Reading data for machine learning: CSV tables, batching samples, MNIST and images, and synthetic data.

This package readies data for training a model. `LoadCsv` builds a table that turns text columns into category numbers by itself, and `split_xy` divides it into a feature matrix and a label.

The `Make...` functions build synthetic data from a fixed seed, for trying algorithms out without needing a file. All of it works with the matrix and tensor packages.

## Types

### `Table`

```salam
struct Table
```

A data table with named columns, for machine learning.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `names` | `Vector` | The column names. |
| `kinds` | `Vector` | The kind of each column; one of the `COL_` constants. |
| `cats` | `Vector>` | The levels of each categorical column. |
| `raw` | `Vector>` | The original text of the cells. |
| `cells` | `matrix.Matrix` | The numeric value of the cells; a categorical column holds the level number. |

data-Table.salam

```salam
import data
import matrix

func main:
    text := "age,city,score,ok\n30,tehran,1.5,1\n25,shiraz,2.5,0\n41,tehran,3.0,1\n"
    mut t := data.LoadCsv(text, true)
    println t.rows(), t.cols(), t.names, t.col_index("score"), t.col_index("x")
    println t.kinds[0] == data.COL_INT, t.kinds[1] == data.COL_CAT, t.kinds[2] == data.COL_FLOAT, data.COL_STR
    println t.cat_levels("city")
    mut m := t.to_matrix()
    println m.rows, m.cols, m.at(2, 1)
    mut x := matrix.Matrix {}
    mut y := matrix.Matrix {}
    println t.split_xy("ok", x, y), x.cols, y.at(1, 0)
    mut good := true
    _ := data.LoadCsvFile("missing.csv", true, good)
    println good
    matrix.Free(m)
    matrix.Free(x)
    matrix.Free(y)
    t.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
3 4 ["age", "city", "score", "ok"] 2 -1
true true true 3
["tehran", "shiraz"]
3 4 0
true 3 0
false
```

### `BatchIter`

```salam
struct BatchIter
```

A batch iterator.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `matrix.Matrix` | The features. |
| `y` | `matrix.Matrix` | The labels. |
| `batch` | `int = 32` | The batch size. |
| `shuffle` | `bool = true` | Shuffle the order. |
| `seed` | `i64 = 0` | The shuffle seed. |
| `order` | `Vector` | The order of the samples in this epoch. |
| `pos` | `int = 0` | The current position. |

data-Batch.salam

```salam
import data
import matrix
import tensor

func main:
    mut y := matrix.Matrix {}
    x := data.MakeBlobs(10, 2, 3, 0.2, 1, y)
    mut set := data.MatrixDataset { x = x, y = y }
    println set.len()
    mut it := set.batches(4, false, 0)
    println it.batches_per_epoch()
    mut batch_x := matrix.Matrix {}
    mut batch_y := matrix.Matrix {}
    until it.next(batch_x, batch_y):
        println batch_x.rows, batch_x.cols, batch_y.rows
    end
    it.reset(1)
    mut t := tensor.Tensor {}
    mut labels := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    println it.next_tensor(t, labels), labels.len()
    println data.YLabels(y).len(), data.XTensor(x).shape
    mut good := true
    _ := data.ParseIdx(null, 0, good)
    println good
    _ := data.LoadIdx("missing.idx", good)
    println good, data.LoadMnist("a", "b", batch_x, batch_y)
    mut classes := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    println data.LoadImageFolder("missing-folder", 8, 8, true, t, labels, classes)
    it.free()
    set.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
10
3
4 3 4
4 3 4
2 3 2
true 4
10 [10, 3]
false
false false
false
```

#### `reset`

```salam
func reset(epoch: i64)
```

Goes back to the start and builds a fresh order from the seed plus the epoch number.

### `MakeBlobs`

```salam
func MakeBlobs(n: int, centers: int, p: int, spread: f64, seed: i64, y &: matrix.Matrix): matrix.Matrix
```

Random samples in several clusters with random centres; the label of a sample is the number of its cluster.

data-Synth.salam

```salam
import data
import matrix

func count_ones(y: matrix.Matrix): int:
    mut n := 0
    repeat y.rows in i:
        if y.at(i, 0) == 1.0:
            n += 1
        end
    end
    ret n
end

func main:
    mut y := matrix.Matrix {}
    blobs := data.MakeBlobs(90, 3, 2, 0.5, 42, y)
    println blobs.rows, blobs.cols, y.rows
    moons := data.MakeMoons(100, 0.1, 7, y)
    println moons.rows, moons.cols, count_ones(y)
    circles := data.MakeCircles(60, 0.05, 0.5, 7, y)
    println circles.rows, count_ones(y)
    mut coef := matrix.Matrix {}
    reg := data.MakeRegression(50, 3, 0.1, 1, y, coef)
    println reg.rows, reg.cols, coef.rows
    cls := data.MakeClassification(40, 4, 2, 1.0, 3, y)
    println cls.rows, cls.cols, count_ones(y) > 0
end
```

Output:

```text
90 2 90
100 2 50
60 30
50 3 3
40 4 true
```

# net/tcp

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-tcp/

TCP servers and clients: listening, connecting, reading and writing, TLS and a connection pool.

TCP is the base of most internet protocols: a reliable, ordered stream of bytes between two programs. A server listens on a port with `Bind` and takes each new client with `Accept`; a client connects with `Dial`.

`Accept` and `Read` wait until data arrives; to serve several clients, handle each in its own thread (`spawn`) or set a deadline. The examples run on `127.0.0.1`.

## Types

### `Server`

```salam
struct Server
```

A TCP server listening on one port.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket descriptor; -1 means invalid. |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port the server listens on. |

net-tcp-Echo.salam

```salam
import net.tcp

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func responder():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    message := tcp.Read(conn, 1024)
    _ := tcp.Write(conn, "echo: " + message)
    tcp.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    println tcp.Ok(server), tcp.Port(server) > 0
    t := spawn(responder)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    println tcp.ConnOk(conn)
    tcp.SetDeadline(conn, 2000)
    tcp.SetKeepAlive(conn, true)
    tcp.SetNoDelay(conn, true)
    println tcp.Write(conn, "hello")
    println tcp.Read(conn, 1024)
    tcp.Close(conn)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println tcp.ConnOk(tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 1))
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true
5
echo: hello
false
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One TCP connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket descriptor; -1 means invalid. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-tcp-Echo.salam

### `PoolEntry`

```salam
struct PoolEntry
```

One idle connection in the pool.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The host and port. |
| `conn` | `Conn` | The connection. |
| `put_at_ms` | `i64 = 0` | When it was returned to the pool. |

net-tcp-Pool.salam

```salam
import net.tcp

func main:
    s := tcp.Bind(0)
    port := tcp.Port(s)
    mut pool := tcp.NewPool()
    conn := tcp.Get(pool, "127.0.0.1", port, 1000)
    println tcp.ConnOk(conn), tcp.PoolLen(pool)
    tcp.Put(pool, "127.0.0.1", port, conn, 1000)
    println tcp.PoolLen(pool)
    again := tcp.Get(pool, "127.0.0.1", port, 2000)
    println again.fd == conn.fd, tcp.PoolLen(pool)
    tcp.Put(pool, "127.0.0.1", port, again, 2000)
    fresh := tcp.Get(pool, "127.0.0.1", port, 2000 + pool.idle_ttl_ms + 1)
    println tcp.ConnOk(fresh), tcp.PoolLen(pool)
    tcp.Close(fresh)
    tcp.CloseServer(s)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 0
1
true 0
true 0
```

### `ReadBytes`

```salam
func ReadBytes(c: Conn, buf: void*, max: int): int
```

Reads at most `max` bytes into memory and returns how many; zero or less means the end or an error.

net-tcp-Bytes.salam

```salam
import net.tcp
import mem

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func responder():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    tcp.SetReadDeadline(conn, 2000)
    tcp.SetWriteDeadline(conn, 2000)
    _ := tcp.Read(conn, 1024)
    tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "hello")
    tcp.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(responder)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    request := "GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n"
    println tcp.WriteBytes(conn, request as void*, request.len())
    b := mem.AllocateZeroed(256 as u64)
    mut total := 0
    until true:
        r := tcp.ReadBytes(conn, b, 255)
        if r <= 0:
            break
        end
        total += r
    end
    println total > 0
    again := tcp.ConnFromFd(conn.fd)
    println again.fd == conn.fd
    tcp.Close(conn)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    mem.Free(b)
end
```

Output:

```text
18
true
true
```

# net/udp

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-udp/

Sending and receiving UDP packets, with broadcast and multicast.

UDP sends separate packets, with no connection and no guarantee that they arrive or arrive in order; in exchange it is fast and simple. It is what DNS, games, live streaming and discovering devices on a local network use. Up to about 1500 bytes per packet is safe.

## Types

### `Socket`

```salam
struct Socket
```

A UDP socket.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket descriptor. |

net-udp-Echo.salam

```salam
import net.udp
import mem

func main:
    receiver := udp.BindOn("127.0.0.1", 0)
    sender := udp.Open()
    println udp.Ok(receiver), udp.Ok(sender), udp.Port(receiver) > 0
    udp.SetTimeout(receiver, 2000)
    println udp.Send(sender, "127.0.0.1", udp.Port(receiver), "hello")
    p := udp.Receive(receiver, 1500)
    println p.data, p.from_host, p.from_port > 0
    _ := udp.SendTo(sender, "127.0.0.1", udp.Port(receiver), "two")
    text := "three"
    _ := udp.SendBytes(sender, "127.0.0.1", udp.Port(receiver), text as void*, text.len())
    println udp.Receive(receiver, 1500).data
    buffer := mem.AllocateZeroed(64 as u64)
    mut host := ""
    mut port := 0
    println udp.ReceiveBytes(receiver, buffer, 64, host, port), host
    udp.SetTimeout(receiver, 100)
    println "[" + udp.Receive(receiver, 1500).data + "]"
    udp.SetBroadcast(sender, true)
    println udp.JoinMulticast(receiver, "239.1.2.3") or true, udp.LeaveMulticast(receiver, "239.1.2.3") or true
    other := udp.Bind(0)
    println udp.Ok(other)
    udp.Close(other)
    udp.Close(receiver)
    udp.Close(sender)
    mem.Free(buffer)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true true
5
hello 127.0.0.1 true
two
5 127.0.0.1
[]
true true
true
```


| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `from_port` | `int = 0` | The port of the sender. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-udp-Echo.salam

# net/dns

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-dns/

Finding the address of a name and asking for any kind of DNS record.

DNS turns names such as `salamlang.ir` into IP addresses. `Lookup` is the simplest way and does what a browser does. The `Lookup...` functions ask the DNS server for one particular kind of record and are what you want for building network tools or checking the configuration of a domain.

## Types

### `Question`

```salam
struct Question
```

One question.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The domain name. |
| `qtype` | `int = 0` | The record type. |
| `qclass` | `int = 0` | The class. |

net-dns-Message.salam

```salam
import net.dns
import compress

func main:
    query := dns.EncodeQuery("salamlang.ir", dns.TypeA, 42)
    println compress.BufLen(query), compress.BufToBase64(query)
    m := dns.Decode(query.data, query.len)
    println m.id, m.qr, m.rd, m.opcode, m.rcode, m.questions.items.len()
    q := m.questions.items[0]
    println q.name, q.qtype == dns.TypeA, q.qclass == dns.ClassIN
    println m.answers.items.len(), m.authorities.items.len(), m.extras.items.len(), m.aa, m.tc, m.ra
    println dns.TypeNS, dns.TypeCNAME, dns.TypeSOA, dns.TypePTR, dns.TypeMX, dns.TypeTXT, dns.TypeAAAA
    println dns.Lookup("localhost")
    println dns.DefaultServers().len() > 0
end
```

Output:

```text
30 ACoBAAABAAAAAAAACXNhbGFtbGFuZwJpcgAAAQAB
42 false true 0 0 1
salamlang.ir true true
0 0 0 false false false
2 5 6 12 15 16 28
127.0.0.1
true
```

### `Questions`

```salam
struct Questions
```

A list of questions.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The questions. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-dns-Message.salam

### `Record`

```salam
struct Record
```

One answer record.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The domain name. |
| `rtype` | `int = 0` | The record type. |
| `rclass` | `int = 0` | The class. |
| `ttl` | `int = 0` | How many seconds the answer may be kept. |
| `priority` | `int = 0` | The priority of an MX record; a smaller number means a higher priority. |
| `data` | `str = ""` | The record data as text: an address, a name or some text. |

net-dns-Lookup.salam

```salam
import net.dns

func main:
    println dns.LookupA("salamlang.ir")
    println dns.LookupAAAA("salamlang.ir")
    println dns.LookupCNAME("www.github.com")
    mx := dns.LookupMX("gmail.com")
    each m in mx.items:
        println m.priority, m.data, m.ttl, m.rtype, m.rclass, m.name
    end
    println dns.LookupTXT("salamlang.ir")
    println dns.LookupPTR("8.8.8.8")
    answer := dns.QueryServer("1.1.1.1", "salamlang.ir", dns.TypeA, 2000)
    println answer.answers.items.len()
end
```

# net/mime

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-mime/

The media type of a file, the Content-Type header, and multipart form bodies.

A media type (MIME) tells the browser and other programs what the content is, such as `image/png`. This package finds the type from a file extension and reads the `Content-Type` header.

Forms that upload a file send a `multipart/form-data` body: several parts with a boundary between them. `ParseMultipart` reads one and `MultipartWriter` builds one.

## Types

### `ContentTypeParam`

```salam
struct ContentTypeParam
```

One parameter.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The name, in lower case. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |

net-mime-Types.salam

```salam
import net.mime

func main:
    println mime.MimeExt("png"), mime.MimeExt("json"), mime.MimeExt(".png")
    println mime.MimeType("/site/index.html"), mime.MimeType("style.css")
    println mime.StatusText(200), mime.StatusText(404), mime.StatusText(503)
    ct := mime.ParseContentType("text/html; charset=UTF-8; q=0.9")
    println ct.media_type, ct.params.items.len(), mime.ParamGet(ct, "charset"), ct.params.items[1].key, ct.params.items[1].value
end
```

Output:

```text
image/png application/json application/octet-stream
text/html; charset=utf-8 text/css
OK Not Found Service Unavailable
text/html 2 UTF-8 q 0.9
```

### `ContentTypeParams`

```salam
struct ContentTypeParams
```

A list of parameters.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The parameters. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-mime-Types.salam

### `ContentType`

```salam
struct ContentType
```

A parsed `Content-Type` header.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `media_type` | `str = ""` | The media type, in lower case. |
| `params` | `ContentTypeParams` | The parameters, such as `charset`. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-mime-Types.salam

### `MultipartHeader`

```salam
struct MultipartHeader
```

One header of a part.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |

net-mime-Multipart.salam

```salam
import net.mime
import compress
import str

func main:
    mut w := mime.NewMultipartWriter()
    println str.StartsWith(mime.ContentTypeHeader(w), "multipart/form-data; boundary=")
    mime.WriteField(w, "name", "Maryam")
    mime.WriteFileStr(w, "note", "note.txt", "text/plain", "hello")
    data := compress.BufFromStr("PNG")
    mime.WriteFileBytes(w, "pic", "a.png", "image/png", data.data, data.len)
    body := mime.CloseWriter(w)
    println w.closed, body.len > 0
    parts := mime.ParseMultipart(body.data, body.len, w.boundary)
    each p in parts.items:
        println p.name, "[" + p.filename + "]", "[" + p.content_type + "]", compress.BufToStrUnsafe(p.body), p.headers.items.len()
    end
    println parts.items[1].headers.items[0].key
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true true
name [] [] Maryam 1
note [note.txt] [text/plain] hello 2
pic [a.png] [image/png] PNG 2
Content-Disposition
```

### `MultipartHeaders`


| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The headers. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-mime-Multipart.salam

| Name | Type | Description |

| `headers` | `MultipartHeaders` | Every header of the part. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-mime-Multipart.salam

# net/proxy

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-proxy/

Connecting through an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy, alone or in a chain.

A proxy is a middleman that makes the connection on behalf of the program. This package builds the tunnel and gives back an ordinary net/tcp connection, read and written exactly as a direct one is.

## Types

### `Proxy`

```salam
struct Proxy
```

One proxy.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int = 0` | The kind; one of the `Type` constants. |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port. |
| `username` | `str = ""` | The user name, when one is needed. |
| `password` | `str = ""` | The password. |

net-proxy-Proxy.salam

```salam
import net.proxy

func main:
    a := proxy.NewHTTPProxy("10.0.0.1:3128")
    println a.kind == proxy.TypeHTTP, a.host, a.port
    b := proxy.NewHTTPProxyAuth("proxy.local:8080", "ali", "secret")
    println b.username, b.password
    c := proxy.NewSOCKS5Proxy("127.0.0.1:1080")
    d := proxy.NewSOCKS5ProxyAuth("socks.local:1080", "u", "p")
    println c.kind == proxy.TypeSOCKS5, d.port
    mut chain := proxy.NewChain()
    proxy.Add(chain, c)
    proxy.Add(chain, a)
    println chain.items.len()
end
```

Output:

```text
true 10.0.0.1 3128
ali secret
true 1080
2
```

### `Chain`

```salam
struct Chain
```

A chain of proxies used one after another.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The proxies in order. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-proxy-Proxy.salam

```salam
import net.proxy
import net.tcp

func main:
    p := proxy.NewSOCKS5Proxy("127.0.0.1:1080")
    conn := proxy.Dial(p, "example.com", 80)
    mut chain := proxy.NewChain()
    proxy.Add(chain, p)
    conn2 := proxy.DialChain(chain, "example.com", 80)
    println tcp.ConnOk(conn), tcp.ConnOk(conn2)
end
```

# net/router

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-router/

Routing HTTP requests, with parameters, groups and static files.

The router keeps one handler function per method and path. In a pattern, a segment that starts with `:` is a parameter; `/books/:id` matches `/books/42` with `id` set to 42. A `*` at the end of a pattern matches any continuation, without making a parameter.

Usually you hand the router to the net/http server and it calls `Dispatch` itself; the handlers take the context id of the request.

## Types

### `Param`

```salam
struct Param
```

One path parameter.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The name, without the `:`. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value from the request path. |

net-router-Dispatch.salam

```salam
import net.router

mut count := 0

func list(_ctx: i64):
    count += 1
end

func show(_ctx: i64):
    count += 1
end

func create(_ctx: i64):
    count += 1
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/books", list)
    router.Get(r, "/books/:id", show)
    router.Post(r, "/books", create)
    router.Put(r, "/books/:id", create)
    router.Delete(r, "/books/:id", create)
    router.Patch(r, "/books/:id", create)
    router.Head(r, "/books", list)
    router.Options(r, "/books", list)
    router.Method(r, "PURGE", "/cache", create)
    router.Method(r, "GET", "/files/*", show)
    router.Group(r, "/api/v1", "GET", "/users/:uid/books/:id", show)
    router.Static(r, "/static", "public")
    router.EnableListing(r)
    println r.routes.len(), r.has_static, r.static_prefix, r.static_listing
    mut m := router.Dispatch(r, "GET", "/books/42")
    println m.matched, m.fn == show, router.ParamGet(m, "id")
    router.FreeMatch(m)
    mut m2 := router.Dispatch(r, "GET", "/api/v1/users/7/books/3")
    println m2.matched, m2.params.items.len(), m2.params.items[0].key, m2.params.items[0].value
    router.FreeMatch(m2)
    mut m3 := router.Dispatch(r, "GET", "/files/a/b.txt")
    println m3.matched, m3.params.items.len()
    router.FreeMatch(m3)
    mut m4 := router.Dispatch(r, "DELETE", "/books")
    println m4.matched, r.routes[0].method, r.routes[0].pattern
    router.FreeMatch(m4)
end
```

Output:

```text
11 true /static true
true true 42
true 2 uid 7
true 0
false GET /books
```

### `ParamList`


| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The parameters. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-router-Dispatch.salam

# net/httpx

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-httpx/

Sending a raw HTTP request with headers of your own and taking the response as text or bytes.

This package is a thin layer under net/http: you write the request line and the headers yourself and get the response untouched. It is what API clients that want full control of the headers are built on, such as the cloud service packages.

## Types

### `Response`

```salam
struct Response
```

An HTTP response.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The status code. |
| `head` | `str = ""` | The response headers, untouched. |
| `body` | `str = ""` | The body. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The request was sent and the response was read. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The error message. |

net-httpx-Send.salam

```salam
import tls
import net.httpx
import net.tcp
import mem

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func responder():
    repeat 3:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        _ := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "hello from the server")
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func main:
    remote := httpx.ParseEndpoint("https://api.example.com:8443")
    println remote.ok, remote.host, remote.port, remote.secure
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(responder)
    local := httpx.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server))
    head := "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    r := httpx.SendText(local, head, "")
    println r.ok, r.status, r.body, "[" + r.error + "]"
    println httpx.HeaderValue(r.head, "content-type")
    mut raw := httpx.SendRawTimeout(local, head, null, 0, 2000)
    println raw.ok, raw.status, raw.len, httpx.RawText(raw)
    httpx.FreeRaw(raw)
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("127.0.0.1")
    cfg.ca_file = "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"
    mut secured := httpx.SendRawTLS(local, head, null, 0, 2000, cfg)
    println secured.status, secured.len
    httpx.FreeRaw(secured)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println httpx.RawLimit() > 0
    httpx.SetRawLimit(1024 * 1024)
    println httpx.RawLimit()
    mut n := 0
    p := httpx.CopyOut("abc", n)
    println n
    mem.Free(p)
    r2 := httpx.Send(local, head, null, 0)
    raw2 := httpx.SendRaw(local, head, null, 0)
    println r2.ok, raw2.ok
end
```

Output:

```text
true api.example.com 8443 true
true 200 hello from the server []
text/plain
true 200 21 hello from the server
200 21
true
1048576
3
false false
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `port` | `int = 443` | The port; 443 by default. |
| `secure` | `bool = true` | Connect with TLS. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The address was read correctly. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-httpx-Send.salam


| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `head` | `str = ""` | The headers. |

# net/email

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-email/

Sending email over SMTP and reading it over IMAP and POP3.

To send one email, `Send` is the simplest way. For more control, several recipients for instance, drive the SMTP client step by step. To read a mailbox, IMAP leaves the messages on the server and POP3 takes them away.

Most servers accept nothing but an encrypted connection; use the `Dial...TLS` functions or `StartTLS`. The client example only compiles, because it needs a real server.

## Types

### `IMAPClient`

```salam
struct IMAPClient
```

An IMAP client for reading a mailbox.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conn` | `tcp.Conn` | The connection. |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | It is encrypted. |
| `tls_idx` | `int = -1` | The internal TLS index. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The connection is up. |
| `rxbuf` | `str = ""` | The data not yet read. |
| `tag_counter` | `int = 0` | The command tag counter. |

net-email-Clients.salam

```salam
import net.email

func main:
    mut smtp := email.DialSMTPTLS("smtp.example.com", 465)
    if smtp.ok and email.Hello(smtp, "example.com") and email.AuthLogin(smtp, "ali", "secret"):
        _ := email.MailFrom(smtp, "ali@example.com")
        _ := email.RcptTo(smtp, "sara@example.com")
        _ := email.Data(smtp, email.BuildMessage("ali@example.com", "sara@example.com", "hello", "some text", ""))
    end
    email.Quit(smtp)
    mut smtp2 := email.DialSMTP("smtp.example.com", 587)
    _ := email.StartTLS(smtp2, "smtp.example.com")
    _ := email.AuthPlain(smtp2, "ali", "secret")
    _ := email.AuthXOAuth2(smtp2, "ali", "token")
    println smtp2.last_reply
    _ := email.Send("smtp.example.com", 465, true, "ali", "secret", "ali@example.com", "sara@example.com", "hello", "some text", "")
    mut imap := email.DialIMAPTLS("imap.example.com", 993)
    _ := email.Login(imap, "ali", "secret")
    _ := email.LoginXOAuth2(imap, "ali", "token")
    println email.List(imap, "", "*")
    _ := email.Select(imap, "INBOX")
    println email.Fetch(imap, "1:5", "(FLAGS BODY[HEADER.FIELDS (SUBJECT)])")
    reply := email.Command(imap, "NOOP")
    println reply.ok, reply.status, reply.lines.len()
    email.Logout(imap)
    _ := email.DialIMAP("imap.example.com", 143)
    mut pop := email.DialPOP3TLS("pop.example.com", 995)
    _ := email.User(pop, "ali")
    _ := email.Pass(pop, "secret")
    println email.Stat(pop), email.POP3List(pop)
    println email.Retr(pop, 1)
    _ := email.Dele(pop, 1)
    email.POP3Quit(pop)
    _ := email.DialPOP3("pop.example.com", 110)
end
```

```salam
import net.email
import str

func main:
    message := email.BuildMessage("ali@example.com", "sara@example.com", "hello", "plain text", "<p>some <b>nice</b> text</p>")
    each line in str.Split(message, "\r\n"):
        if str.StartsWith(line, "From:") or str.StartsWith(line, "To:") or str.StartsWith(line, "MIME-Version:") or str.StartsWith(line, "Subject:"):
            println line
        end
    end
    println str.Contains(message, "multipart/alternative")
    println email.BuildXOAuth2("ali@example.com", "ya29.token")
end
```

```text
Subject: hello
MIME-Version: 1.0
true
dXNlcj1hbGlAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20BYXV0aD1CZWFyZXIgeWEyOS50b2tlbgEB
```

# net/websocket

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-websocket/

A two way connection that stays open between browser and server, with rooms for broadcasting.

A WebSocket is a connection that stays open after one HTTP request, and either side sends a message whenever it likes; for live chat, notifications and games. The server takes connections with `Listen` and `Accept`, and a client connects with `Dial`.

To serve several clients, read each connection in its own thread and use a `Hub` to send a message to every member of a room.

## Types

### `Server`

```salam
struct Server
```

A WebSocket server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket descriptor. |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port. |

net-websocket-Echo.salam

```salam
import net.websocket

mut server := websocket.Server {}

func responder():
    mut conn := websocket.Accept(server)
    until websocket.IsOpen(conn):
        m := websocket.Receive(conn)
        if websocket.IsText(m):
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, "echo: " + m.text)
        else websocket.IsBinary(m):
            _ := websocket.SendBinaryBytes(conn, m.data, m.len)
        else websocket.IsClose(m):
            break
        end
    end
    websocket.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = websocket.Listen(0)
    println websocket.Ok(server), websocket.Port(server) > 0
    t := spawn(responder)
    mut c := websocket.Dial("127.0.0.1", websocket.Port(server), "/chat")
    println websocket.IsOpen(c), c.path, c.client
    _ := websocket.SendText(c, "hello")
    println websocket.ReceiveText(c)
    _ := websocket.SendBinary(c, "abc")
    m := websocket.Poll(c, 2000)
    println m.kind == websocket.BINARY, m.len
    _ := websocket.Ping(c, "p")
    m2 := websocket.Poll(c, 2000)
    println websocket.IsPong(m2), m2.kind == websocket.PONG
    m3 := websocket.Poll(c, 50)
    println m3.kind == websocket.TIMEOUT
    websocket.Close(c)
    join(t)
    websocket.CloseServer(server)
    println websocket.NONE, websocket.TEXT, websocket.CLOSE, websocket.PING
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true /chat true
echo: hello
true 3
true true
true
0 1 8 9
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One WebSocket connection, on the server or the client side.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket descriptor. |
| `open` | `bool = false` | The connection is open. |
| `path` | `str = ""` | The path that was asked for, such as `/chat`. |
| `client` | `bool = false` | This is the client side; a client sends its frames masked. |
| `buf` | `void*` | The receive buffer. |
| `blen` | `int = 0` | The length of the data in the buffer. |
| `bcap` | `int = 0` | The buffer capacity. |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | It is encrypted. |
| `tls_idx` | `int = -1` | The internal TLS index. |
| `hdr` | `str = ""` | The handshake headers. |
| `acc` | `str = ""` | The text of a multi frame message being gathered. |
| `acc_kind` | `int = 0` | The kind of the multi frame message. |
| `fragmented` | `bool = false` | A multi frame message is on its way. |
| `bin` | `void*` | The buffer of a binary message. |
| `binlen` | `int = 0` | Its length. |
| `bincap` | `int = 0` | Its capacity. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-websocket-Echo.salam

### `Message`

```salam
struct Message
```

One received message.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int = 0` | The message kind; one of the constants above. |
| `text` | `str = ""` | The text of a text message. |
| `data` | `void*` | The data of a binary message. |
| `len` | `int = 0` | The length of the data. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-websocket-Echo.salam

### `RoomMembers`

```salam
struct RoomMembers
```

The members of one room.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The connections. |

net-websocket-Hub.salam

```salam
import net.websocket

mut server := websocket.Server {}
mut sides := Vector {} as Vector<websocket.Conn>

func acceptor():
    repeat 2:
        sides.push(websocket.Accept(server))
    end
end

func main:
    server = websocket.Listen(0)
    port := websocket.Port(server)
    t := spawn(acceptor)
    mut a := websocket.Dial("127.0.0.1", port, "/room")
    mut b := websocket.DialWith("127.0.0.1", port, "/room", "X-Name: b\r\n")
    join(t)
    mut hub := websocket.NewHub()
    each side in sides:
        websocket.Register(hub, "lobby", side)
    end
    println websocket.RoomSize(hub, "lobby"), hub.rooms.size()
    println websocket.Broadcast(hub, "lobby", "welcome")
    println websocket.ReceiveText(a), websocket.ReceiveText(b)
    println websocket.BroadcastBinary(hub, "lobby", "xy")
    println websocket.Receive(a).len
    websocket.Unregister(hub, "lobby", sides[0])
    println websocket.RoomSize(hub, "lobby")
    websocket.Stop(a)
    websocket.Close(b)
    websocket.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
2 1
2
welcome welcome
2
2
1
```

## Functions

### `AcceptKey`

```salam
func AcceptKey(key: str): str
```

Builds the handshake accept key from the client key (RFC 6455).

net-websocket-Handshake.salam

```salam
import net.websocket
import str

func main:
    println websocket.AcceptKey("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==")
    request := websocket.HandshakeRequest("example.com", "/chat", "dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==")
    println str.Split(request, "\r\n")[0]
    request2 := websocket.HandshakeRequestWith("example.com", "/chat", "dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==", "Authorization: Bearer x\r\n")
    println str.Contains(request2, "Authorization: Bearer x")
    response := websocket.HandshakeResponse(request)
    println str.Split(response, "\r\n")[0]
    println str.Contains(response, "Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=")
end
```

Output:

```text
s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
true
HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
true
```

# net/http

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http/

HTTP servers and clients: handlers, text and JSON responses, cookies and sending requests.

The Salam HTTP server hands requests to a router, and the router calls the handler function. Every handler takes one `i64`, the context id of the request; you read the request and write the response with the `Ctx_...` functions, or turn it into a `Context` struct with `Ctx` so the names get shorter.

To send a request, `Get` and `Post` are the simplest way; `Client` keeps cookies the way a browser does. The examples run the server with `RunBackground` on 127.0.0.1 and send requests to it from the same program.

## Types

### `Cookie`

```salam
struct Cookie
```

One response cookie.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |
| `path` | `str = "/"` | The path the cookie is sent for; `/` by default. |
| `domain` | `str = ""` | The domain; empty means this host. |
| `max_age` | `int = 0` | The lifetime in seconds. |
| `has_max_age` | `bool = false` | A lifetime was set; without one the cookie goes when the browser closes. |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | Send it over HTTPS only. |
| `http_only` | `bool = true` | Keep it out of reach of the page JavaScript; true by default. |
| `same_site` | `str = "Lax"` | The SameSite policy; `Lax` by default. |

net-http-Cookie.salam

```salam
import net.http

func main:
    c := http.NewCookie("theme", "dark")
    println c.name, c.value, c.path, c.http_only, c.same_site, c.has_max_age
    mut s := http.ExpiringCookie("sid", "x1", 3600)
    s.secure = true
    s.domain = "salamlang.ir"
    println s.max_age, s.has_max_age, s.secure, s.domain
    gone := http.ExpiredCookie("sid", "/", "salamlang.ir")
    println gone.max_age, gone.has_max_age
    println http.UrlDecode("a%20b+c")
end
```

Output:

```text
theme dark / true Lax false
3600 true true salamlang.ir
-1 true
a b c
```

### `Response`

```salam
struct Response
```

The response to a client request.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The status code. |
| `body` | `str = ""` | The body. |
| `head` | `str = ""` | The raw headers. |
| `err` | `str = ""` | The error message, when the request did not get through. |

net-http-Client.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func echo(ctx: i64):
    http.Ctx_set_header(ctx, "X-Tag", "a")
    http.Ctx_set_cookie(ctx, http.NewCookie("sid", "abc"))
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, http.Ctx_method(ctx) + " " + http.Ctx_header(ctx, "X-Token") + " " + http.Ctx_body(ctx))
end

func cookies(ctx: i64):
    all := http.Ctx_cookies(ctx)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "" + all.size() + " " + http.Ctx_cookie(ctx, "lang") + " " + http.Ctx_has_cookie(ctx, "sid"))
    http.Ctx_clear_cookie(ctx, "old")
    http.Ctx_clear_cookie_at(ctx, "scoped", "/admin", "")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    each method in ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS", "HEAD"]:
        router.Method(r, method, "/echo", echo)
    end
    router.Get(r, "/cookies", cookies)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19623)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    url := "http://127.0.0.1:19623/echo"
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("X-Token", "t1")
    a := http.GetWith(url, headers)
    println http.Ok(a), http.Status(a), http.Body(a), "[" + http.Error(a) + "]"
    println http.Headers(a).has("X-Tag"), http.HeaderValues(a, "set-cookie")
    println http.CookieMap(a).get("sid"), http.RawHeaders(a).len() > 0, http.Raw(a).len() > 0
    println http.Body(http.Post(url, "a")), http.Body(http.PutWith(url, "b", headers))
    println http.Body(http.Delete(url)), http.Body(http.DeleteWith(url, headers))
    println http.Body(http.Patch(url, "c")), http.Body(http.PatchWith(url, "d", headers))
    println http.Body(http.Options(url)), http.Body(http.OptionsWith(url, headers))
    println http.Status(http.Head(url)), http.Status(http.HeadWith(url, headers))
    println http.Body(http.Put(url, "e")), http.Body(http.Get(url))
    println http.Body(http.RequestRaw("POST", url, "X-Token: raw\r\n", "f"))
    mut params := http.NewHeaders()
    params.insert("q", "hello world")
    println http.EncodeForm(params), http.WithQuery("http://x.ir/s", params)
    mut jar := http.NewHeaders()
    jar.insert("lang", "en")
    jar.insert("sid", "abc")
    headers.insert("Cookie", http.CookieHeader(jar))
    b := http.GetWith("http://127.0.0.1:19623/cookies", headers)
    println http.Body(b), http.SetCookieLines(b).len()
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    c.SetCookie("lang", "en")
    println http.Body(c.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19623/cookies"))
    c.ClearCookies()
    mut extra := http.NewHeaders()
    extra.insert("X-Token", "c1")
    println http.Body(c.RequestWith("PUT", url, "g", extra)), http.Body(c.Request("PATCH", url, "h"))
    println http.Body(c.Put(url, "i")), http.Body(c.Delete(url)), http.Body(c.Patch(url, "j")), http.Body(c.Options(url)), http.Status(c.Head(url))
    bad := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:1/")
    println http.Ok(bad), http.Error(bad) != ""
end
```

Output:

```text
true 200 GET t1  []
true ["sid=abc; Path=/; SameSite=Lax; HttpOnly"]
abc true true
POST  a PUT t1 b
DELETE   DELETE t1
PATCH  c PATCH t1 d
OPTIONS   OPTIONS t1
200 200
PUT  e GET
POST raw f
q=hello%20world http://x.ir/s?q=hello%20world
2 en true 2
1 en false
PUT c1 g PATCH  h
PUT  i DELETE   PATCH  j OPTIONS   200
false true
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

An HTTP client that keeps fixed headers and cookies between requests; a simple browser.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cookies` | `HashMap` | The cookies it took from the responses. |
| `headers` | `HashMap` | The headers sent with every request. |

net-http-Context.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func hello(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    name := http.Query(ctx, "name")
    if http.HasCookie(ctx, "seen"):
        http.Text(ctx, "hello again " + name + " (" + http.CookieValue(ctx, "seen") + ")")
    else:
        http.SetCookie(ctx, http.ExpiringCookie("seen", "1", 3600))
        http.Text(ctx, "hello " + name + " (" + http.RawQuery(ctx) + ")")
    end
end

func book(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "X-Method", http.Method(ctx))
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 202)
    http.Json(ctx, `{"id": "` + http.Param(ctx, "id") + `", "path": "` + http.Path(ctx) + `"}`)
end

func form(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    http.Text(ctx, http.Form(ctx, "a") + "|" + http.Body(ctx) + "|" + http.Header(ctx, "Content-Type"))
end

func logout(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    http.ClearCookie(ctx, "seen")
    http.Redirect(ctx, "/hello")
end

func page(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    cookies := http.Cookies(ctx)
    http.Html(ctx, "<p>" + cookies.size() + "</p>")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/hello", hello)
    router.Get(r, "/books/:id", book)
    router.Post(r, "/form", form)
    router.Get(r, "/logout", logout)
    router.Get(r, "/page", page)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19622)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19622"
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/hello?name=Maryam"))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/hello?name=Maryam"))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/page"))
    a := c.Get(base + "/books/7")
    println http.Status(a), http.Body(a), http.GetHeader(a, "x-method")
    c.SetHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    println http.Body(c.Post(base + "/form", "a=1&b=2"))
    b := c.Get(base + "/logout")
    println http.Status(b), http.SetCookieLines(b).len() > 0
end
```

Output:

```text
hello Maryam (name=Maryam)
hello again Maryam (1)
<p>1</p>
202 {"id": "7", "path": "/books/7"} GET
1|a=1&b=2|application/x-www-form-urlencoded
302 true
```

### `Server`

```salam
struct Server
```

An HTTP server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port. |
| `host` | `str = "0.0.0.0"` | The listen address; `0.0.0.0` by default, meaning every address. |
| `router` | `router.Router` | The router for the requests. |
| `hide_tokens` | `bool = false` | Hide the server version in the responses. |
| `access_log` | `bool = false` | Log every request to the output. |

net-http-Server.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import net.tcp

func hello(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    conn := http.ConnOf(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "hello " + tcp.ConnOk(conn))
end

func main:
    http.SetKeepAliveIdle(5000)
    http.SetKeepAliveMaxRequests(100)
    http.SetMaxHeaderBytes(16384)
    http.SetMaxBodyBytes(1048576)
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", hello)
    mut s := http.NewServer(8080)
    http.SetHost(s, "0.0.0.0")
    http.HideTokens(s)
    http.EnableAccessLog(s)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println http.SERVER_VERSION, http.IsEdge()
    if not http.IsEdge():
        http.RunTLS(s, "cert.pem", "key.pem")
    end
    http.Run(s)
end
```

## Constants and variables

### `SERVER_VERSION`

```salam
const SERVER_VERSION: str = "0.5.6"
```

The server version sent in the `Server` header of the responses.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-Server.salam

## Functions

### `Ctx_method`

```salam
func Ctx_method(h: i64): str
```

The request method, such as GET.

net-http-Handle.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func home(ctx: i64):
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "hello from the server")
end

func book(ctx: i64):
    id := http.Ctx_param(ctx, "id")
    format := http.Ctx_query(ctx, "format")
    http.Ctx_set_header(ctx, "X-Book", id)
    http.Ctx_json(ctx, `{"id": "` + id + `", "format": "` + format + `", "raw": "` + http.Ctx_raw_query(ctx) + `"}`)
end

func create(ctx: i64):
    name := http.Ctx_form(ctx, "name")
    http.Ctx_status(ctx, 201)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, http.Ctx_method(ctx) + " " + http.Ctx_path(ctx) + " " + name + " " + http.Ctx_header(ctx, "X-Client"))
end

func raw(ctx: i64):
    answer := http.Ctx_own(ctx, "body: " + http.Ctx_body(ctx))
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, answer)
end

func page(ctx: i64):
    http.Ctx_html(ctx, "<h1>hello</h1>")
end

func old(ctx: i64):
    http.Ctx_redirect(ctx, "/")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", home)
    router.Get(r, "/books/:id", book)
    router.Post(r, "/books", create)
    router.Put(r, "/raw", raw)
    router.Get(r, "/page", page)
    router.Get(r, "/old", old)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19621)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19621"
    a := http.Get(base + "/")
    println http.Status(a), http.Body(a)
    b := http.Get(base + "/books/42?format=pdf")
    println http.Body(b), http.GetHeader(b, "x-book")
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    headers.insert("X-Client", "salam")
    c := http.PostWith(base + "/books", "name=Maryam", headers)
    println http.Status(c), http.Body(c)
    println http.Body(http.Put(base + "/raw", "data"))
    d := http.Get(base + "/page")
    println http.GetHeader(d, "content-type"), http.Body(d)
    e := http.Request("GET", base + "/old", http.NewHeaders(), "")
    println http.Status(e), http.GetHeader(e, "location")
    println http.Status(http.Get(base + "/nope"))
end
```

Output:

```text
true
200 hello from the server
{"id": "42", "format": "pdf", "raw": "format=pdf"} 42
201 POST /books Maryam salam
body: data
text/html; charset=utf-8 <h1>hello</h1>
302 /
404
```

# net/http/middleware

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-middleware/

The usual security, cache and CORS headers, and request logging, in one call.

Call these at the top of a handler to add the usual headers to the response. Each one takes the context id, just as the handler itself does.

## Functions

### `Log`

```salam
func Log(ctx: i64)
```

Writes the method and path of the request to the output.

net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.middleware
import net.router

func home(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Log(ctx)
    middleware.AllowAll(ctx)
    middleware.Secure(ctx)
    middleware.NoCache(ctx)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "hello")
end

func logo(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Cache(ctx, 3600)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "png")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", home)
    router.Get(r, "/logo.png", logo)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19624)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    a := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19624/")
    each name in ["access-control-allow-origin", "x-content-type-options", "x-frame-options", "cache-control"]:
        println name + ": " + http.GetHeader(a, name)
    end
    println http.GetHeader(http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19624/logo.png"), "cache-control")
end
```

Output:

```text
[HTTP] GET /
access-control-allow-origin: *
x-content-type-options: nosniff
x-frame-options: DENY
cache-control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
max-age=3600
```

### `AllowAll`

```salam
func AllowAll(ctx: i64)
```

Opens CORS to every domain: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and the usual methods and headers.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

### `Secure`

```salam
func Secure(ctx: i64)
```

The basic security headers: no content type sniffing, no framing and no XSS.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

### `NoCache`

```salam
func NoCache(ctx: i64)
```

Tells the browser and any proxies not to keep the response.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

### `Cache`

```salam
func Cache(ctx: i64, seconds: int)
```

Tells the browser to keep the response for this many seconds.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

# net/http/validate

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-validate/

Checking form input and answering with a 400.

The functions here check one value and return true or false. `Assert` sends a 400 response with a JSON message when the condition does not hold; after that the handler must not write another response.

## Functions

### `Required`

```salam
func Required(value: str): bool
```

True when the value is not empty; whitespace counts as a value.

net-http-validate-Check.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.validate
import net.router

func signup(ctx: i64):
    email := http.Ctx_form(ctx, "email")
    validate.Assert(ctx, validate.IsEmail(email), "invalid email")
    if validate.IsEmail(email):
        http.Ctx_text(ctx, "welcome")
    end
end

func main:
    println validate.Required(""), validate.Required("  "), validate.Required("Ali")
    println validate.Length("hello", 2, 5), validate.Length("hello world", 2, 5)
    println validate.IsEmail("ali@example.com"), validate.IsEmail("ali@")
    println validate.Matches("09121234567", "^09[0-9]{9}$"), validate.Matches("12345", "^09[0-9]{9}$")
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/signup", signup)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19625)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    bad := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19625/signup", "email=x", headers)
    println http.Status(bad), http.Body(bad)
    good := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19625/signup", "email=a%40b.ir", headers)
    println http.Status(good), http.Body(good)
end
```

Output:

```text
false true true
true false
true false
true false
400 {"error":"invalid email"}
200 welcome
```

# net/http/session

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-session/

User sessions over a cookie: keeping data between requests, and a CSRF token.

A session keeps each user's data on the server and gives the browser nothing but a random id in a cookie. In a handler, `Start` finds the user's session or makes a new one; call `Save` after you change the values.

Once a user has logged in, have `Regenerate` change the id so the earlier one is of no use. The data lives in the memory of this process and is gone on a restart.

## Types

### `SessionData`

```salam
struct SessionData
```

The keys and values of the session.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `HashMap` | The values. |

net-http-session-Session.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.session
import net.router
import conv

func visit(ctx: i64):
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    mut count := 1
    if session.HasValue(s, "visits"):
        count = conv.Atoi(session.Value(s, "visits")) + 1
    end
    session.SetValue(s, "visits", "" + count)
    session.Save(s)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "visit " + count)
end

func login(ctx: i64):
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    session.Regenerate(ctx, s)
    session.SetValue(s, "user", "ali")
    token := session.CSRFToken(s)
    session.Save(s)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "" + session.CSRFVerify(s, token) + " " + session.CSRFVerify(s, "x"))
end

func logout(ctx: i64):
    session.End(ctx)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "goodbye")
end

func main:
    session.Configure("sid", 3600, false, "Lax")
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", visit)
    router.Post(r, "/login", login)
    router.Post(r, "/logout", logout)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19626)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19626"
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    println http.Body(c.Post(base + "/login", ""))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    println http.Body(c.Post(base + "/logout", ""))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    mut s := session.New()
    session.SetValue(s, "a", "1")
    session.SetValue(s, "b", "2")
    println session.DeleteValue(s, "a"), s.data.items.size()
    session.Save(s)
    mut found := false
    back := session.Get(s.id, found)
    println found, session.Value(back, "b"), back.max_age, s.id.len() > 0
    session.ClearValues(s)
    session.Destroy(s.id)
    _ := session.Get(s.id, found)
    println found, session.CleanupExpired() >= 0
    println session.DefaultCookieName, session.DefaultMaxAge
end
```

Output:

```text
visit 1
visit 2
true false
visit 3
goodbye
visit 1
true 1
true 2 3600 true
false true
salam_sid 86400
```
