# net/http/swagger

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-swagger/

Writing OpenAPI documentation for an API and serving the documentation page.

Swagger builds the documentation of an API in the standard OpenAPI form and serves a page for looking at it and trying it out. `Route` picks one operation, and the functions after it, such as `Summary` and `Returns`, describe that one.

The schema of a body or a response is built from a sample value; pass an empty struct and its fields, under their `@json` names, appear in the documentation. `Missing` shows the routes that are not documented yet.

## Types

### `Param`

```salam
struct Param
```

One parameter.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `loc` | `str = "query"` | Where it sits: query, header, cookie or path. |
| `required` | `bool = false` | It is required. |
| `description` | `str = ""` | The description. |
| `schema` | `str = "{"type":"string"}"` | The schema. |

net-http-swagger-Build.salam

```salam
import net.http.swagger
import encoding.json

struct Book:
    @json "id"
    pub id: int = 0
    @json "title"
    pub title: str = ""
end

func main:
    mut doc := swagger.New("library", "1.2.0")
    swagger.Describe(doc, "a sample API for books")
    swagger.Server(doc, "https://api.example.com", "the main one")
    swagger.Contact(doc, "the Salam team", "https://salamlang.ir", "team@salamlang.ir")
    swagger.License(doc, "MIT", "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT")
    swagger.BearerAuth(doc, "token", "JWT")
    swagger.ApiKeyAuth(doc, "key", "header", "X-API-Key")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "GET", "/books/:id")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "one book")
    swagger.Details(doc, "Returns the book with this id.")
    swagger.Tag(doc, "books")
    swagger.OperationId(doc, "getBook")
    swagger.PathParam(doc, "id", "the id of the book")
    swagger.Query(doc, "fields", "the fields asked for", false)
    swagger.QueryTyped(doc, "limit", "the greatest number", false, 10)
    mut orders := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    orders.push("title")
    orders.push("id")
    swagger.QueryEnum(doc, "sort", "the order", false, orders)
    swagger.Header(doc, "X-Trace", "the trace id", false)
    swagger.Cookie(doc, "sid", "the session", false)
    swagger.Secure(doc, "token")
    swagger.Returns(doc, 200, "the book", Book {})
    swagger.ReturnsHeader(doc, 200, "ETag", "the version")
    swagger.ReturnsNothing(doc, 404, "not found")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "POST", "/books")
    swagger.Accepts(doc, "the new book", Book {})
    swagger.Returns(doc, 201, "created", Book {})
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "PUT", "/books/:id/cover")
    swagger.AcceptsRaw(doc, "the cover image", "image/png", "{\"type\":\"string\",\"format\":\"binary\"}", true)
    swagger.ReturnsText(doc, 200, "done")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "POST", "/books/:id/notes")
    swagger.AcceptsOptional(doc, "the note", Book {})
    swagger.AcceptsForm(doc, "the form", Book {})
    swagger.ReturnsRaw(doc, 200, "the export", "text/csv", "{\"type\":\"string\"}")
    swagger.ReturnsHtml(doc, 200, "the page")
    swagger.ReturnsFile(doc, 200, "the file", "application/pdf")
    swagger.Deprecated(doc)
    println swagger.At(doc, "get", "/books/:id"), swagger.At(doc, "GET", "/nope")
    println doc.ops.len(), doc.ops[0].params.len(), doc.ops[0].replies.len(), doc.ops[3].is_deprecated, doc.schemes.len()
    text := swagger.Spec(doc)
    println json.Valid(text), json.Get(text, "openapi")
    println swagger.SpecIndent(doc).len() > text.len()
    println swagger.Problems(doc).len(), swagger.Undocumented(doc)
    println swagger.WriteSpec(doc, "openapi.json"), swagger.SpecFromFile("openapi.json").len() > 0, swagger.SpecFromFile("missing.json")
    println swagger.TEXT_SCHEMA, swagger.JSON_TYPE
    swagger.Free(doc)
end
```

Output:

```text
true false
4 6 2 true 2
true 3.1.0
true
0 []
true true
{"type":"string"} application/json
```

net-http-swagger-Serve.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.swagger
import net.router
import str

func list(ctx: i64):
    http.Ctx_json(ctx, "[]")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/books", list)
    router.Post(r, "/books", list)
    router.Get(r, "/admin/stats", list)
    mut doc := swagger.New("library", "1.0.0")
    println swagger.Missing(doc, r)
    swagger.ScanPrefix(doc, r, "/books")
    println doc.ops.len(), swagger.Missing(doc, r)
    swagger.Scan(doc, r)
    println doc.ops.len(), swagger.Missing(doc, r).len()
    swagger.Mount(doc, r, "/docs")
    mut server := http.NewServer(19627)
    http.Use(server, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(server)
    spec := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19627/docs/openapi.json")
    println http.Status(spec), str.Contains(http.Body(spec), "/admin/stats")
    page := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19627/docs")
    println str.Contains(http.Body(page), "<html")
    mut r2 := router.NewRouter()
    swagger.MountSpec("{\"openapi\":\"3.1.0\"}", "ready made", r2, "/spec")
    println r2.routes.len()
    println swagger.Serve(doc, 19628), http.Status(http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19628/openapi.json"))
    println swagger.ServeSpec("{\"openapi\":\"3.1.0\"}", "another", 19629)
    println str.Contains(swagger.Page("API", "/openapi.json"), "/openapi.json")
end
```

Output:

```text
["GET /books", "POST /books", "GET /admin/stats"]
2 ["GET /admin/stats"]
3 0
200 true
true
3
true 200
true
true
```

# net/http2

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http2/

The HTTP/2 protocol from the ground up: frames, HPACK header compression and streams.

This package implements HTTP/2 at the protocol level: it builds and reads frames, compresses the headers with HPACK and carries several requests at once over one connection as "streams". For building an ordinary web server net/http is simpler; this package is for when you need the protocol itself.

How it goes: build a `Transport` over a TCP or TLS socket, take a connection with `NewConn` and do the handshake. Then the client sends a request with `SendHeaders` and reads the answer in `StreamAt` after `AwaitStreamEnd`. Over TLS, the client and the server must have agreed on `h2` through ALPN.

## Types

### `Stream`

```salam
struct Stream
```

One stream: one request and its answer.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int = 0` | The id; odd for the streams a client opens. |
| `state` | `int = 0` | The state, one of the stream state constants. |
| `send_window` | `int = 65535` | The sending window. |
| `recv_window` | `int = 65535` | The receiving window. |
| `headers` | `HeaderList` | The headers received. |
| `trailers` | `HeaderList` | The trailing headers received. |
| `data` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The body received. |
| `got_headers` | `bool = false` | The headers have arrived. |
| `got_trailers` | `bool = false` | The trailing headers have arrived. |
| `end_stream` | `bool = false` | The other side has ended the stream. |
| `reset` | `bool = false` | The stream was closed with a reset frame. |
| `error_code` | `int = 0` | The reset's error code. |
| `live` | `bool = false` | This slot of the table is in use. |

net-http2-Conn.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import net.tcp
import compress

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func answer():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    mut c := http2.NewConn(http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd), true)
    if not http2.ServerHandshake(c):
        ret
    end
    id := http2.AwaitAnyHeaders(c, 20)
    stream := http2.StreamAt(c, id)
    mut headers := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":status", "200")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, "content-type", "text/plain")
    _ := http2.SendHeaders(c, id, headers, false)
    _ := http2.SendData(c, id, compress.BufFromStr("hello " + http2.HeadersGet(stream.headers, ":path")), false)
    mut trailers := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(trailers, "x-done", "1")
    _ := http2.SendTrailers(c, id, trailers)
    _ := http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, 0, 5)
    http2.CloseConn(c)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(answer)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    tx := http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd)
    println tx.ok, tx.kind == http2.H2_TRANSPORT_PLAIN
    mut c := http2.NewConn(tx, false)
    println http2.ClientHandshake(c), http2.ConnOk(c)
    id := http2.NextStreamId(c)
    mut headers := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":method", "GET")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":scheme", "http")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":path", "/books")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":authority", "127.0.0.1")
    println id, http2.SendHeaders(c, id, headers, true)
    println http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, id, 20)
    stream := http2.StreamAt(c, id)
    println http2.HeadersGet(stream.headers, ":status"), compress.BufToStrUnsafe(stream.data), stream.got_trailers, http2.HeadersGet(stream.trailers, "x-done"), stream.end_stream
    println http2.StreamCount(c) >= 1, c.remote.max_frame_size
    _ := http2.SendPing(c, compress.BufFromStr("abcdefgh"))
    println http2.Poll(c) >= http2.H2_POLL_CONNECTION
    _ := http2.SendRstStream(c, http2.NextStreamId(c), http2.H2_CANCEL)
    println http2.SendGoAway(c, http2.H2_NO_ERROR, "")
    http2.CloseConn(c)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true true
1 true
true
200 hello /books true 1 true
true 16384
true
true
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One HTTP/2 connection with its tables, settings and streams.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | `Transport` | The transport underneath. |
| `is_server` | `bool = false` | This side is the server. |
| `enc` | `DynTable` | The HPACK table for sending. |
| `dec` | `DynTable` | The HPACK table for receiving. |
| `local` | `Settings` | This side's settings. |
| `remote` | `Settings` | The other side's settings, after the handshake. |
| `next_id` | `int = 1` | The next stream id. |
| `streams` | `StreamTable` | The streams. |
| `send_window` | `int = 65535` | The connection's sending window. |
| `recv_window` | `int = 65535` | The connection's receiving window. |
| `goaway` | `bool = false` | A goaway frame arrived or was sent. |
| `last_error` | `int = 0` | The last error code. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The connection is healthy. |
| `pending_stream` | `int = 0` | The stream whose headers block is not finished yet by a continuation frame. |
| `pending_block` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The parts of that block that arrived. |
| `pending_end_stream` | `bool = false` | Those headers end the stream. |
| `pending_trailers` | `bool = false` | Those headers are trailing ones. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Conn.salam

### `Frame`

```salam
struct Frame
```

One HTTP/2 frame.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int = 0` | The frame type, one of the frame type constants. |
| `flags` | `int = 0` | The flags. |
| `stream_id` | `int = 0` | The stream id; zero means the whole connection. |
| `payload` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The frame payload. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The frame was read correctly. |

net-http2-Frame.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import compress

func main:
    mut settings := http2.DefaultSettings()
    println settings.header_table_size, settings.initial_window_size, settings.max_frame_size, settings.enable_push
    frame := http2.MakeSettingsFrame(settings)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(frame.kind), frame.stream_id, frame.payload.len
    settings.max_frame_size = 32768
    println http2.ApplySettings(settings, http2.MakeSettingsFrame(http2.DefaultSettings())), settings.max_frame_size
    ack := http2.MakeSettingsAck()
    println http2.FrameHasFlag(ack, http2.H2_FLAG_ACK)
    win := http2.MakeWindowUpdate(3, 1024)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(win.kind), http2.WindowIncrementOf(win)
    rst := http2.MakeRstStream(5, http2.H2_CANCEL)
    println http2.ErrorCodeOf(rst), http2.ErrorName(http2.ErrorCodeOf(rst))
    away := http2.MakeGoAway(7, http2.H2_NO_ERROR, "bye")
    println http2.FrameTypeName(away.kind), http2.ErrorCodeOf(away)
    ping := http2.MakePing(compress.BufFromStr("12345678"), false)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(ping.kind), ping.payload.len
    mut data := http2.NewFrame(http2.H2_DATA, http2.H2_FLAG_END_STREAM, 1)
    compress.BufPushBytes(data.payload, "hello" as void*, 5)
    mut ok := true
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(http2.DataOf(data, ok)), ok
    bytes := http2.FrameEncode(data)
    println bytes.len, compress.BufGet(bytes, 3)
    mut head := http2.NewFrame(http2.H2_HEADERS, http2.H2_FLAG_END_HEADERS, 1)
    compress.BufPush(head.payload, 130)
    println http2.HeaderBlockOf(head, ok).len, ok
    mut one := compress.NewByteBuf()
    http2.PutSetting(one, http2.H2_SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE, 16384)
    println one.len
    http2.FreeFrame(data)
    println http2.H2_DATA, http2.H2_PING, http2.H2_PROTOCOL_ERROR, http2.H2_DEFAULT_FRAME_SIZE, http2.H2_DEFAULT_WINDOW, http2.H2_MAX_FRAME_LIMIT
    println http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_PRIORITY), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_RST_STREAM), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_PUSH_PROMISE)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_GOAWAY), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_WINDOW_UPDATE), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_CONTINUATION)
    println http2.H2_SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE, http2.H2_SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH, http2.H2_SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS, http2.H2_SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, http2.H2_SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE
    println http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_INTERNAL_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_SETTINGS_TIMEOUT), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_STREAM_CLOSED)
    println http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_FRAME_SIZE_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_REFUSED_STREAM), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_COMPRESSION_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_CONNECT_ERROR)
    println http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_INADEQUATE_SECURITY), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED)
    println http2.H2_STREAM_IDLE, http2.H2_STREAM_OPEN, http2.H2_STREAM_HALF_CLOSED_LOCAL, http2.H2_STREAM_HALF_CLOSED_REMOTE, http2.H2_STREAM_CLOSED_STATE
    println http2.H2_DEFAULT_TABLE_SIZE, http2.H2_POLL_ERROR
end
```

Output:

```text
4096 65535 16384 1
SETTINGS 0 24
true 16384
true
WINDOW_UPDATE 1024
8 CANCEL
GOAWAY 0
PING 8
hello true
14 0
1 true
6
0 6 1 16384 65535 16777215
PRIORITY RST_STREAM PUSH_PROMISE
GOAWAY WINDOW_UPDATE CONTINUATION
1 2 3 4 6
INTERNAL_ERROR FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR SETTINGS_TIMEOUT STREAM_CLOSED
FRAME_SIZE_ERROR REFUSED_STREAM COMPRESSION_ERROR CONNECT_ERROR
ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM INADEQUATE_SECURITY HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED
0 1 2 3 4
4096 -1
```

### `Header`

```salam
struct Header
```

One header.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name; in HTTP/2 always in lower case. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |
| `sensitive` | `bool = false` | It is sensitive and never goes into the HPACK table; for tokens and cookies. |

net-http2-Hpack.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import compress

func main:
    mut list := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(list, ":method", "GET")
    http2.HeadersAdd(list, ":path", "/")
    http2.HeadersAdd(list, "user-agent", "salam")
    http2.HeadersAddSensitive(list, "authorization", "Bearer x")
    println http2.HeadersCount(list), http2.HeadersGet(list, ":path"), http2.HeadersHas(list, "cookie")
    mut sender := http2.NewDynTable(4096)
    mut receiver := http2.NewDynTable(4096)
    block := http2.EncodeHeaderList(sender, list, true)
    println block.len, http2.DynCount(sender), http2.DynSize(sender)
    mut ok := true
    read := http2.DecodeHeaderList(receiver, block, ok)
    println ok, read.items.len(), read.items[2].name, read.items[2].value, read.items[3].sensitive
    block2 := http2.EncodeHeaderList(sender, list, true)
    println block2.len < block.len
    fixed := http2.StaticGet(2)
    println fixed.name, fixed.value, http2.HPACK_STATIC_COUNT, http2.HPACK_ENTRY_OVERHEAD
    dyn := http2.DynGet(receiver, 1)
    println dyn.name
    mut exact := false
    println http2.TableFind(receiver, ":method", "GET", exact), exact
    println http2.TableGet(receiver, 62, ok).name, ok
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    http2.EncodeTableSizeUpdate(b, sender, 256)
    http2.DynSetMaxSize(receiver, 256)
    println b.len, sender.max_size, receiver.max_size
    mut b2 := compress.NewByteBuf()
    http2.EncodeHeader(b2, sender, http2.NewHeader("x-id", "7"), false)
    http2.DynInsert(receiver, http2.NewSensitiveHeader("k", "v"))
    println b2.len, http2.DynCount(receiver)
end
```

Output:

```text
4 / false
17 1 47
true 4 user-agent salam true
true
:method GET 61 32
user-agent
2 true
user-agent true
3 256 256
8 2
```

### `HeaderList`

```salam
struct HeaderList
```

A list of headers, in their order.

| Name | Type | Description |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Hpack.salam

### `DynTable`

```salam
struct DynTable
```

The HPACK dynamic table, which keeps the headers sent or received so that next time only their number is sent. Each side has its own table and the two must stay in step.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The entries. |
| `head` | `int = 0` | The position of the newest entry in the ring. |
| `size` | `int = 0` | The current size in bytes, with the overhead. |
| `max_size` | `int = 4096` | The largest size; older entries are pushed out. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Hpack.salam

### `HufTables`

```salam
struct HufTables
```

The internal tables of the Huffman decoder; they are built once and then used again.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `counts` | `Vector` | The number of codes of each length. |
| `first` | `Vector` | The first code of each length. |
| `syms` | `Vector` | The symbols in code order. |
| `ready` | `bool = false` | The tables are built. |

net-http2-Huffman.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import encoding
import compress

func main:
    b := http2.HuffmanEncodeStr("www.example.com")
    println encoding.HexEncode(compress.BufToStrUnsafe(b))
    println http2.HuffmanEncodedLenStr("www.example.com"), "www.example.com".len()
    mut ok := true
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(http2.HuffmanDecodeBuf(b, ok)), ok
    text := compress.BufFromStr("no-cache")
    println http2.HuffmanEncodedLen(text.data, text.len)
    mut out := compress.NewByteBuf()
    compress.BufPush(out, 0)
    http2.HuffmanEncode(out, text.data, text.len)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(http2.HuffmanDecode(out, 1, out.len - 1, ok)), ok
end
```

Output:

```text
f1e3c2e5f23a6ba0ab90f4ff
12 15
www.example.com true
6
no-cache true
```

## Constants and variables

### `H2_POLL_ERROR`


### `H2_POLL_CONNECTION`

```salam

```

A result of `Poll`: a frame for the whole connection arrived. A positive number is the id of the stream whose frame arrived.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Conn.salam

### `H2_PREFACE`

```salam
const H2_PREFACE: str = "PRI * HTTP/2.0

SM

"
```

The string an HTTP/2 client sends before anything else; 24 bytes.

net-http2-Transport.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import net.tcp
import compress

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func answer():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    mut tx := http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd)
    println "server preface:", http2.ReadPreface(tx)
    frame := http2.ReadFrame(tx, http2.H2_DEFAULT_FRAME_SIZE)
    println "server frame:", frame.ok, http2.FrameTypeName(frame.kind), frame.stream_id, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(frame.payload)
    http2.CloseTransport(tx)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(answer)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    mut tx := http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd)
    _ := http2.WritePreface(tx)
    mut data := http2.NewFrame(http2.H2_DATA, 0, 3)
    compress.BufPushBuf(data.payload, compress.BufFromStr("hi"))
    _ := http2.WriteFrame(tx, data)
    join(t)
    http2.CloseTransport(tx)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println http2.H2_PREFACE.len()
end
```

Output:

```text
server preface: true
server frame: true DATA 3 hi
24
```

### The frame flags `H2_FLAG_…`

The flags in the fifth byte of a frame. What each flag means depends on the frame type; that is why `H2_FLAG_END_STREAM` and `H2_FLAG_ACK` are both 1, one for a data or headers frame and the other for settings and ping. Check them with `FrameHasFlag`.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `H2_FLAG_END_STREAM` | `1` |
| `H2_FLAG_ACK` | `1` |
| `H2_FLAG_END_HEADERS` | `4` |
| `H2_FLAG_PADDED` | `8` |
| `H2_FLAG_PRIORITY` | `32` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Frame.salam

### `H2_SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE`

```salam
func DecodeHeaderList(t &: DynTable, block: compress.ByteBuf, ok &: bool): HeaderList
```

Turns an HPACK block back into a header list and brings the receiving table up to date.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Hpack.salam


---

# net/socketio

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-socketio/

A Socket.IO client: events, acknowledgements, namespaces and automatic reconnection.

Socket.IO is the usual live messaging library in the Node.js world. This package is a client that connects to any Socket.IO version 4 server; it has no server of its own. `Dial` connects, `On` sets a listener for an event and the `Emit...` functions send events. Listeners are called while the program processes messages with `Run`, `RunFor`, `Pump` or `Next`.

The arguments of every event are a JSON array, read with `ArgStr`, `ArgInt` and the like. If the sender wants an answer, the event's `ack_id` is not negative and you answer it with `Reply`. For several namespaces on one connection, create a `Manager`.

## Types

### `Endpoint`

```salam
struct Endpoint
```

A parsed server URL.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | HTTPS or WSS. |
| `host` | `str = "localhost"` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 80` | The port; 80 or 443 if it is not given. |
| `path` | `str = "/socket.io"` | The Socket.IO path. |
| `namespace` | `str = "/"` | The namespace, from the URL path. |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The URL is valid. |

net-socketio-URL.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func show(url: str):
    e := socketio.ParseURL(url)
    if not e.ok:
        println url, "invalid"
        ret
    end
    println e.host, e.port, e.secure, e.namespace, "query=" + e.query
    println socketio.Origin(e)
end

func main:
    show("http://localhost:3000")
    show("https://example.com/admin/?token=abc")
    show("ws://[::1]:8080/chat")
    show("ftp://example.com")
end
```

Output:

```text
localhost 3000 false / query=
http://localhost:3000
example.com 443 true /admin query=token=abc
https://example.com
::1 8080 false /chat query=
http://[::1]:8080
ftp://example.com invalid
```

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

Connection options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `str = "/socket.io"` | The path of the Socket.IO server. |
| `query` | `str = ""` | An extra query for the URL. |
| `auth` | `str = ""` | Authentication data as JSON, sent when connecting to the namespace. |
| `headers` | `str = ""` | Extra HTTP headers, one per line. |
| `transports` | `int` | The transport, one of the `TRANSPORT_...` constants. |
| `reconnection` | `bool = true` | Reconnect automatically after a disconnect. |
| `reconnection_attempts` | `int = 0` | The most attempts; zero means no limit. |
| `reconnection_delay` | `int = 1000` | The delay before the first attempt in milliseconds; it doubles every time. |
| `reconnection_delay_max` | `int = 5000` | The longest delay. |
| `randomization_factor` | `int = 50` | A random percentage added to or taken from the delay so that all clients do not come back at the same moment. |
| `timeout` | `int = 20000` | The connect timeout in milliseconds. |
| `insecure` | `bool = false` | Do not check the TLS certificate; for testing only. |
| `auto_connect` | `bool = true` | The client connects right away. |
| `event_queue` | `int = 256` | The most events in the queue. |
| `ack_timeout` | `int = 0` | The default acknowledgement timeout. |
| `retries` | `int = 0` | How many times to resend messages that got no acknowledgement. |
| `trailing_slash` | `bool = true` | Add a slash to the end of the path, like the JavaScript client. |
| `remember_upgrade` | `bool = false` | If the upgrade to WebSocket worked once, use WebSocket directly next time. |

net-socketio-Options.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    println o.path, o.reconnection, o.reconnection_delay, o.timeout
    println o.transports == socketio.TRANSPORT_AUTO
    o.transports = socketio.TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET
    o.auth = `{"token":"abc"}`
    o.auto_connect = false
    println o.transports, o.auth, o.auto_connect
    println socketio.TRANSPORT_POLLING, socketio.REASON_SERVER_DISCONNECT, socketio.REASON_PING_TIMEOUT
    println socketio.PUMP_OK, socketio.PUMP_TIMEOUT, socketio.PUMP_CLOSED
end
```

Output:

```text
/socket.io true 1000 20000
true
1 {"token":"abc"} false
2 io server disconnect ping timeout
0 1 2
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

One socket on one namespace.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p` | `void*` | The internal pointer. |

net-socketio-Client.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import net.websocket
import str

mut server := websocket.Server {}
mut report := ""

func test_server():
    mut conn := websocket.Accept(server)
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `0{"sid":"s1","upgrades":[],"pingInterval":20000,"pingTimeout":5000}`)
    mut going := true
    until going:
        m := websocket.Poll(conn, 3000)
        if m.kind != websocket.TEXT:
            break
        end
        packet := m.text.substr(1, m.text.len() - 1)
        if packet == "0":
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `40{"sid":"a1"}`)
        else str.StartsWith(packet, `2["chat"`):
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `42["chat","welcome"]`)
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `429["question","2+2"]`)
        else str.Contains(packet, `"add"`):
            id := packet.substr(1, str.Find(packet, "[") - 1)
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, "43" + id + "[5]")
        else str.StartsWith(packet, "39"):
            report += "reply: " + packet.substr(2, packet.len() - 2)
        else packet == "1":
            going = false
        end
    end
    websocket.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = websocket.Listen(0)
    t := spawn(test_server)
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.transports = socketio.TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET
    o.reconnection = false
    c := socketio.DialWith("http://127.0.0.1:" + websocket.Port(server), o)
    println socketio.IsConnected(c), socketio.Sid(c), socketio.Id(c), socketio.Namespace(c), socketio.TransportName(c)

    socketio.On(c, "chat", (e: socketio.Event):
        println "message:", socketio.ArgStr(e, 0)
    end)
    socketio.On(c, "question", (e: socketio.Event):
        println "question:", socketio.ArgStr(e, 0), e.ack_id >= 0
        _ := socketio.ReplyStr(e, "four")
    end)
    println socketio.ListenerCount(c, "chat"), socketio.HasListeners(c, "news")
    _ := socketio.EmitStr(c, "chat", "hello")
    socketio.RunFor(c, 500)

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddInt(a, 2)
    socketio.AddInt(a, 3)
    mut k := socketio.EmitAck(c, "add", a, 2000)
    println k.ok, socketio.AckInt(k, 0)
    socketio.AckFree(k)
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)

    socketio.Close(c)
    join(t)
    websocket.CloseServer(server)
    println report
end
```

Output:

```text
true s1 a1 / websocket
1 false
message: welcome
question: 2+2 true
true 5
reply: ["four"]
```

### `Manager`

```salam
struct Manager
```

A connection that several namespaces work on.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p` | `void*` | The internal pointer. |

net-socketio-Manager.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.auth = `{"token":"abc"}`
    o.auto_connect = false
    m := socketio.NewManager("https://example.com", o)
    socketio.SetReconnection(m, true)
    socketio.SetReconnectionAttempts(m, 5)
    socketio.SetReconnectionDelay(m, 500)
    socketio.SetReconnectionDelayMax(m, 10000)
    socketio.SetRandomizationFactor(m, 20)
    socketio.SetTimeout(m, 5000)
    println socketio.OptionsOf(m).reconnection_attempts

    public := socketio.Of(m, "/")
    admin := socketio.Of(m, "/admin")
    socketio.SetAuth(admin, `{"role":"admin"}`)
    println socketio.AuthOf(admin), socketio.Sockets(m).len()
    if not socketio.Open(m):
        println "error:", socketio.ManagerError(m)
        ret
    end
    println socketio.IsOpen(m)
    _ := socketio.Connect(public)
    _ := socketio.Connect(admin)
    if socketio.Refused(admin):
        println "refused:", socketio.RefusalReason(admin)
    end
    println socketio.Active(public), socketio.Disconnected(public), socketio.Recovered(public)
    println socketio.Transport(public), socketio.PingInterval(public), socketio.PingTimeout(public), socketio.MaxPayload(public)
    println socketio.Buffered(public), socketio.Pending(public), socketio.Queued(public), socketio.Attempts(public)
    println socketio.EndpointOf(public).host, socketio.ManagerOf(public).p == m.p
    _ := socketio.PumpManager(m, 1000)
    socketio.Disconnect(admin)
    socketio.CloseManager(m)
end
```

### `Packet`

```salam
struct Packet
```

One Socket.IO packet.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int = -1` | The kind. |
| `nsp` | `str = "/"` | The namespace. |
| `id` | `int = -1` | The acknowledgement number; -1 means no acknowledgement. |
| `data` | `str = ""` | The data as JSON. |
| `attachments` | `int = 0` | The number of binary parts. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The packet was read correctly. |

net-socketio-Packet.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut p := socketio.Packet {}
    p.kind = socketio.PKT_EVENT
    p.nsp = "/chat"
    p.id = 7
    p.data = `["hi",1]`
    text := socketio.EncodePacket(p)
    println text
    d := socketio.DecodePacket(text)
    println d.ok, d.kind, d.nsp, d.id, d.data
    bad := socketio.DecodePacket("x")
    println bad.ok

    payload := socketio.EncodeEngine(socketio.EIO_MESSAGE, text)
    println payload
    println socketio.EngineKind(payload) == socketio.EIO_MESSAGE
    println socketio.EngineBody(payload)

    mut items := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    items.push("2")
    items.push(payload)
    body := socketio.JoinPayloads(items)
    parts := socketio.SplitPayloads(body)
    println parts.len(), parts.get(0), parts.get(1)

    arr := socketio.SplitJSONArray(`["a", {"b":[1,2]}, 3]`)
    println arr.len(), arr.get(1)

    ph := socketio.Placeholder(0)
    println ph
    println socketio.PlaceholderNum(ph), socketio.PlaceholderNum("12")
end
```

Output:

```text
2/chat,7["hi",1]
true 2 /chat 7 ["hi",1]
false
42/chat,7["hi",1]
true
2/chat,7["hi",1]
2 2 42/chat,7["hi",1]
3 {"b":[1,2]}
{"_placeholder":true,"num":0}
0 -1
```

```salam
import net.socketio
import encoding.value

func main:
    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "hello \"world\"")
    socketio.AddInt(a, 42)
    socketio.AddFloat(a, 2.5)
    socketio.AddBool(a, true)
    socketio.AddNull(a)
    socketio.AddJSON(a, `{"x":1}`)

    text := socketio.ArgsJSON(a, "message")

    println socketio.ItemStr(text, 1)
    println socketio.ItemInt(text, 2)

    println value.IsNumber(v), value.AsInt(v)
    mut a2 := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddValue(a2, v)

    println socketio.ArgsJSON(a2, "")
    socketio.ArgsFree(a2)
```

### Event kinds `EV_…`

The value of the `kind` field in the event that `Next` returns. A message event is one of the server's messages; the rest report on the connection itself: connecting and disconnecting, errors, reconnection attempts, pings, timeouts and the upgrade to WebSocket. Listeners are called with the English names of these events, such as `connect` and `disconnect`.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `EV_NONE` | `0` |
| `EV_EVENT` | `1` |
| `EV_CONNECT` | `2` |
| `EV_DISCONNECT` | `3` |
| `EV_CONNECT_ERROR` | `4` |
| `EV_ERROR` | `5` |
| `EV_RECONNECT` | `6` |
| `EV_RECONNECT_ATTEMPT` | `7` |
| `EV_RECONNECT_ERROR` | `8` |
| `EV_RECONNECT_FAILED` | `9` |
| `EV_PING` | `10` |
| `EV_TIMEOUT` | `11` |
| `EV_UPGRADE` | `12` |

net-socketio-Ack.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import encoding.value

func main:
    c := socketio.Dial("http://localhost:3000")
    if not socketio.IsConnected(c):
        println socketio.LastError(c)
        ret
    end
    socketio.OnAny(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "received:", e.name, socketio.ArgCount(e)
    end)
    socketio.Once(c, "welcome", (e: socketio.Event):
        println socketio.Arg(e, 0)
    end)
    socketio.OnAnyOutgoing(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "sent:", e.name
    end)

    socketio.PrependAny(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "first of all:", e.name
    end)
    socketio.PrependAnyOutgoing(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "sending:", e.name
    end)
    println socketio.AnyListenerCount(c)

    _ := socketio.Emit(c, "ping")
    _ := socketio.EmitInt(c, "score", 12)
    _ := socketio.EmitFloat(c, "temp", 21.5)
    _ := socketio.EmitBool(c, "ready", true)
    _ := socketio.EmitJSON(c, "user", `{"name":"Ali"}`)
    _ := socketio.EmitBytes(c, "file", "abc" as void*, 3)
    _ := socketio.Send(c, "a plain message")

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "room-1")
    _ := socketio.EmitArgs(c, "join", a)
    _ := socketio.EmitVolatile(c, "cursor", a)
    _ := socketio.EmitWithAck(c, "join", a, 2000, (k: socketio.Ack):
        println k.ok, socketio.AckCount(k), socketio.AckStr(k, 0)
        println socketio.AckArg(k, 1), socketio.AckFloat(k, 1), socketio.AckBool(k, 2)
        if socketio.AckIsBinary(k, 3):
            println socketio.AckBytes(k, 3).len
        end
        mut v := socketio.AckValue(k, 0)
        value.ValueFree(v)
    end)
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)

    mut e := socketio.Next(c, 5000)
    if e.kind == socketio.EV_EVENT:
        println socketio.ArgInt(e, 0), socketio.ArgFloat(e, 1), socketio.ArgBool(e, 2)
        if socketio.ArgIsBinary(e, 3):
            b := socketio.ArgBytes(e, 3)
            println b.len
        end
        if e.ack_id >= 0:
            _ := socketio.ReplyJSON(e, `{"ok":true}`)
        end
    else e.kind == socketio.EV_DISCONNECT:
        println "disconnected:", e.message
    end
    socketio.EventFree(e)

    mut e2 := socketio.NextEvent(c, 5000)
    mut v2 := socketio.ArgValue(e2, 0)
    println value.IsNumber(v2)
    value.ValueFree(v2)
    socketio.EventFree(e2)

    _ := socketio.Pump(c, 100)
    socketio.Off(c, "welcome")
    socketio.OffAny(c)
    socketio.OffAnyOutgoing(c)
    socketio.OffAll(c)
    socketio.Run(c)
end
```

### Disconnect reasons `REASON_…`

The text in the `message` field of a disconnect event, telling why the connection ended: the server or the program itself closed it, a ping did not arrive in time, the transport closed or failed, or a packet could not be read.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `REASON_SERVER_DISCONNECT` | `"io server disconnect"` |
| `REASON_CLIENT_DISCONNECT` | `"io client disconnect"` |
| `REASON_PING_TIMEOUT` | `"ping timeout"` |
| `REASON_TRANSPORT_CLOSE` | `"transport close"` |
| `REASON_TRANSPORT_ERROR` | `"transport error"` |
| `REASON_PARSE_ERROR` | `"parse error"` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Options.salam

### Pump results `PUMP_…`

The result of `Pump` and `PumpManager`: something arrived and was handled, the timeout ran out, or the connection is closed.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `PUMP_OK` | `0` |
| `PUMP_TIMEOUT` | `1` |
| `PUMP_CLOSED` | `2` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Options.salam

### Engine packet kinds `EIO_…`

Socket.IO runs on a layer called Engine.IO. Every message on that layer starts with a digit that gives its kind: open, close, ping, pong, message, upgrade and noop. Socket.IO packets travel inside messages of the "message" kind.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `EIO_OPEN` | `0` |
| `EIO_CLOSE` | `1` |
| `EIO_PING` | `2` |
| `EIO_PONG` | `3` |
| `EIO_MESSAGE` | `4` |
| `EIO_UPGRADE` | `5` |
| `EIO_NOOP` | `6` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Packet.salam

### Socket.IO packet kinds `PKT_…`

The kinds of Socket.IO packet: connecting to a namespace, disconnecting, an event, an acknowledgement, a connect error, and the binary event and binary acknowledgement whose bytes follow the packet separately.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `PKT_CONNECT` | `0` |
| `PKT_DISCONNECT` | `1` |
| `PKT_EVENT` | `2` |
| `PKT_ACK` | `3` |
| `PKT_CONNECT_ERROR` | `4` |
| `PKT_BINARY_EVENT` | `5` |
| `PKT_BINARY_ACK` | `6` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Packet.salam

### `NewBytes`

# dom

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/dom/

Working with a web page in the browser: elements, events, timers and JavaScript objects.

A program that uses this package runs in the browser. Translate it to JavaScript with `salam js app.salam --output=app.js` and put it in a page with a `<script src="app.js">` tag; `main` runs once the page is ready, and `println` writes to the browser console. That is why the examples on this page are not run, only checked.

Elements and JavaScript objects are held as one `i64` number. Events and timers take an anonymous function, such as `(): ... end`; keep a function you will want to drop later with `OffEvent` in a variable.

## Functions

### `Query`

```salam
func Query(sel: str): i64
```

The first element that matches the CSS selector; zero when there is none.

dom-Elements.salam

```salam
import dom

func main:
    list := dom.Create("ul")
    dom.SetAttr(list, "id", "books")
    dom.Append(dom.Body(), list)
    repeat 3 in i:
        item := dom.Create("li")
        dom.SetText(item, "book " + (i + 1))
        dom.AddClass(item, "book")
        dom.Append(list, item)
    end
    println dom.Exists("books"), dom.Exists("nothing")

    all := dom.QueryAll("li.book")
    println dom.CountOf(all)
    second := dom.ItemAt(all, 1)
    println dom.GetText(second)
    dom.ToggleClass(second, "selected")
    println dom.GetAttr(second, "class")
    dom.RemoveClass(second, "book")
    println dom.GetAttr(second, "class")

    dom.SetStyle(second, "color", "red")
    println dom.GetStyle(second, "color")
    first := dom.Query("li")
    dom.Remove(first)
    println dom.CountOf(dom.QueryAll("li"))

    box := dom.ById("books")
    dom.SetHtml(box, "<li>new</li>")
end
```

```salam
import dom

func main:
    d := dom.Document()
    println dom.GetStr(d, "title")
    dom.SetStr(d, "title", "my page")
    println dom.GetStr(d, "title")
    w := dom.Window()
    println dom.GetNum(w, "innerWidth") == dom.WinWidth()
    println dom.DocWidth() > 0, dom.DocHeight() > 0

    box := dom.Create("input")
    dom.SetBool(box, "disabled", true)
    println dom.GetBool(box, "disabled")
    dom.SetNum(box, "tabIndex", 3)
    println dom.GetNum(box, "tabIndex")
    dom.SetProp(box, "parentRef", dom.Body())
    println dom.GetProp(box, "parentRef") == dom.Body()

    math := dom.Global("Math")
    println dom.Call1(math, "abs", -5), dom.Call2(math, "max", 2, 9)
    println dom.Call3(math, "max", 1, 2, 3), dom.Call4(math, "min", 4, 3, 2, 1)
    _ := dom.Call0(box, "focus")
    _ := dom.CallS1(box, "removeAttribute", "placeholder")
    _ := dom.CallS2(box, "setAttribute", "name", "q")
    println dom.GetAttr(box, "name")

    canvas := dom.Create("canvas")
    ctx := dom.GetContext(canvas, "2d")
    println ctx != 0

    dom.StoreSetInt("best", 42)
    dom.StoreSetStr("name", "Maryam")
    println dom.StoreGetInt("best"), dom.StoreGetStr("name")

    r := dom.Random()
    println r >= 0.0 and r < 1.0, dom.RandomInt(6) < 6
    println dom.Now() >= 0.0

    button := dom.Create("button")
    greet := ():
        println "hello"
    end
    dom.OnEvent(button, "click", greet)
    dom.OffEvent(button, "click", greet)

    image := dom.LoadImage("logo.png")
    println dom.ImageReady(image)
    dom.Tone(440, 200)
    if dom.Confirm("shall we go on?"):
        name := dom.Prompt("what is your name?")
        dom.Alert("hello " + name)
    end
end
```

### `Window`

```salam
func Window(): i64
```

The `window` object.

dom-Events.salam

```salam
import dom

mut count := 0

func main:
    button := dom.Create("button")
    dom.SetText(button, "click me")
    dom.SetAttr(button, "data-autofire", "click")
    dom.Append(dom.Body(), button)
    dom.OnEvent(button, "click", ():
        count += 1
        println "click", count
    end)

    box := dom.Create("input")
    dom.SetAttr(box, "data-autofire", "keydown")
    dom.Append(dom.Body(), box)
    dom.SetValue(box, "hello")
    println dom.GetValue(box)
    dom.OnEventE(box, "keydown", (e: i64):
        if dom.EventKey(e) == "Enter":
            dom.PreventDefault(e)
        end
        dom.StopPropagation(e)
        println "target:", dom.GetValue(dom.EventTarget(e))
    end)

    dom.OnWindowE("mousemove", (e: i64):
        println dom.EventX(e), dom.EventY(e)
    end)
    dom.OnWindowE("touchstart", (e: i64):
        println dom.TouchX(e), dom.TouchY(e)
    end)
    dom.OnWindow("scroll", ():
        println dom.ScrollX(), dom.ScrollY()
    end)
    dom.OnReady(():
        println "the page is ready"
    end)
    dom.OnResize(():
        println dom.WinWidth(), dom.WinHeight()
    end)
end
```


dom-Timers.salam

```salam
import dom

mut tick := 0
mut every := 0 as i64

func main:
    dom.SetTitle("timers")
    start := dom.Now()
    _ := dom.SetTimeout(():
        println "one second has passed"
    end, 1000)
    cancelled := dom.SetTimeout(():
        println "this never runs"
    end, 5000)
    dom.ClearTimeout(cancelled)
    every = dom.SetInterval(():
        tick += 1
        if tick == 3:
            dom.ClearInterval(every)
        end
    end, 200)
    dom.RequestFrame((now: f64):
        println "frame after", now - start
    end)
    dom.EveryFrame((now: f64):
        _ := now
    end)
end
```

# web/canvas

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/web-canvas/

Drawing shapes, text and images on a browser canvas element.

This package gives plain functions for two dimensional drawing on a `canvas` element. As with dom, the program is translated for the browser with `salam js`. Get the drawing context with `Get` and pass it to every function. The coordinates start at the top left corner and the vertical axis points down.

## Functions

### `Get`

```salam
func Get(id: str): i64
```

The two dimensional drawing context of the canvas element with this id.

web-canvas-Draw.salam

```salam
import dom
import web.canvas

func main:
    el := dom.Create("canvas")
    dom.SetAttr(el, "id", "board")
    dom.SetAttr(el, "width", "320")
    dom.SetAttr(el, "height", "200")
    dom.Append(dom.Body(), el)
    c := canvas.Get("board")
    println canvas.Width(c), canvas.Height(c)

    canvas.FillStyle(c, "#f5f0e6")
    canvas.FillRect(c, 0, 0, canvas.Width(c), canvas.Height(c))
    canvas.FillStyle(c, "#2a7")
    canvas.RoundRect(c, 20, 20, 120, 60, 12)
    canvas.Fill(c)
    canvas.StrokeStyle(c, "#333")
    canvas.LineWidth(c, 2)
    canvas.StrokeRect(c, 160, 20, 120, 60)
    canvas.ClearRect(c, 170, 30, 20, 20)

    canvas.BeginPath(c)
    canvas.MoveTo(c, 20, 180)
    canvas.LineTo(c, 100, 100)
    canvas.LineTo(c, 180, 180)
    canvas.ClosePath(c)
    canvas.Stroke(c)
    canvas.BeginPath(c)
    canvas.Arc(c, 250, 140, 30, 0, 6.2832)
    canvas.Alpha(c, 0.5)
    canvas.Fill(c)
    canvas.Alpha(c, 1)

    canvas.Save(c)
    canvas.Translate(c, 160, 100)
    canvas.Rotate(c, 0.2)
    canvas.Scale(c, 1.5, 1.5)
    canvas.Font(c, "16px Inter")
    canvas.TextAlign(c, "center")
    canvas.FillStyle(c, "#000")
    canvas.FillText(c, "hello", 0, 0)
    canvas.Restore(c)

    image := dom.LoadImage("logo.png")
    if dom.ImageReady(image):
        canvas.DrawImage(c, image, 260, 10, 50, 50)
    end
    second := canvas.Of(dom.Create("canvas"))
    println second != 0
end
```

### `RoundRect`


# web/keys

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/web-keys/

Keyboard state for browser games.

In a game you usually ask once per frame which keys are down, rather than taking an event for every press. This package listens to the keyboard events for you and keeps the state. Call `Init` once, then ask for the state inside the `EveryFrame` function from dom.

## Functions

### `Track`

```salam
func Track(k: str)
```

Adds a key to the list of tracked keys; the key name is the browser `key` value, such as `a`. Up to 32 keys.

web-keys-Game.salam

```salam
import dom
import web.canvas
import web.keys

mut x := 160.0
mut score := 0

func main:
    el := dom.Create("canvas")
    dom.SetAttr(el, "id", "game")
    dom.Append(dom.Body(), el)
    c := canvas.Get("game")
    keys.Init()
    keys.Track("a")
    keys.Track("d")
    dom.EveryFrame((now: f64):
        if keys.Down("ArrowLeft") or keys.Down("a"):
            x -= 4
        end
        if keys.Down("ArrowRight") or keys.Down("d"):
            x += 4
        end
        if keys.Pressed(" "):
            score += 1
        end
        canvas.ClearRect(c, 0, 0, canvas.Width(c), canvas.Height(c))
        canvas.FillRect(c, x - 10, 100, 20, 20)
        canvas.FillText(c, "score: " + score, 10, 20)
    end)
end
```

### `Init`

```salam
func Init()
```

Starts tracking and adds the arrow keys, Enter and the space bar. Those keys no longer scroll the page.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: web-keys-Game.salam

### `Down`

```salam
func Down(k: str): bool
```

The key is being held right now; for continuous movement.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: web-keys-Game.salam

### `Pressed`

```salam
func Pressed(k: str): bool
```

The key has been pressed since the last time you asked; every press returns true exactly once. For jumping or shooting.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: web-keys-Game.salam

# webpush

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/webpush/

Sending notifications to browsers from a server, with VAPID keys and the standard encryption.

A web push notification is a message a server sends to a user's browser even when the site is not open. The flow: make a key pair once with `GenerateKeys`, use the public key in the page JavaScript to subscribe, store the subscription the browser makes on your server, and send messages with `Send`.

The message is encrypted under RFC 8291 before it is sent, so the browser push service never sees its contents. When the result says `gone`, the user has cancelled the subscription.

## Types

### `Keys`

```salam
struct Keys
```

The VAPID keys of the server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public_key` | `str = ""` | The public key as url safe base64; this is what you give to `applicationServerKey` in the page JavaScript. |
| `private_key` | `str = ""` | The private key; keep it secret. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The keys are valid. |

webpush-Keys.salam

```salam
import webpush
import str

func main:
    fresh := webpush.GenerateKeys()
    println fresh.ok, fresh.public_key.len(), fresh.private_key.len()

    k := webpush.KeysFrom("BLmOwafYGSjiuCX_1RSCO_n0YmacxYMDqitMydKE4A1Wp2qmUuMXg2IM_hzcrmZLun4jEu_lKfVdtnAp0LMK4NE", "Nhh4m4Va4yhL-53i302044iqeAeMtnOEYlIT2KWRJmg")
    println k.ok, webpush.KeysFrom("", "").ok
    at := webpush.VapidHeaderAt(k, "https://fcm.googleapis.com", "mailto:ali@example.com", 1700000000)
    println at
    now := webpush.VapidHeader(k, "https://fcm.googleapis.com", "mailto:ali@example.com")
    println str.StartsWith(now, "vapid t="), str.Contains(now, ", k=" + k.public_key)

    mut o := webpush.NewOptions("mailto:ali@example.com")
    println o.subject, o.ttl == webpush.DEFAULT_TTL, o.ttl / 86400
    o.urgency = "high"
    o.topic = "news"
    o.ttl = 3600
    println o.urgency, o.topic, o.ttl
end
```

Output:

```text
true 87 43
true false
vapid t=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJhdWQiOiJodHRwczovL2ZjbS5nb29nbGVhcGlzLmNvbSIsImV4cCI6MTcwMDA0MzIwMCwic3ViIjoibWFpbHRvOmFsaUBleGFtcGxlLmNvbSJ9.8Sx-V8MK5NDw923EAMtv8NSCJzQMdhQx8E_ItZUuaMU_VVCv0NzyPG0vZ6JfRsu-S6h99PJJFB6_vgd3NGT_Lw, k=BLmOwafYGSjiuCX_1RSCO_n0YmacxYMDqitMydKE4A1Wp2qmUuMXg2IM_hzcrmZLun4jEu_lKfVdtnAp0LMK4NE
true true
mailto:ali@example.com true 28
high news 3600
```

### `Subscription`

```salam
struct Subscription
```

The subscription the browser makes with `pushManager.subscribe` and sends to your server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | `str = ""` | The address of the browser push service. |
| `p256dh` | `str = ""` | The public key of the browser, from the `keys` part of the subscription. |
| `auth` | `str = ""` | The authentication secret, from the same part. |

webpush-Encrypt.salam

```salam
import webpush

func main:
    sub := webpush.Subscription {
        endpoint = "https://push.example.net/x",
        p256dh = "BCVxsr7N_eNgVRqvHtD0zTZsEc6-VV-JvLexhqUzORcxaOzi6-AYWXvTBHm4bjyPjs7Vd8pZGH6SRpkNtoIAiw4",
        auth = "BTBZMqHH6r4Tts7J_aSIgg"
    }
    mut good := false
    body := webpush.EncryptWith(sub, "When I grow up, I want to be a watermelon", "yfWPiYE-n46HLnH0KqZOF1fJJU3MYrct3AELtAQ-oRw", "DGv6ra1nlYgDCS1FRnbzlw", good)
    println good
    println body

    one := webpush.Encrypt(sub, "hello", good)
    two := webpush.Encrypt(sub, "hello", good)
    println good, one != two, one.len() == two.len()
end
```

Output:

```text
true
DGv6ra1nlYgDCS1FRnbzlwAAEABBBP4z9KsN6nGRTbVYI_c7VJSPQTBtkgcy27mlmlMoZIIgDll6e3vCYLocInmYWAmS6TlzAC8wEqKK6PBru3jl7A_yl95bQpu6cVPTpK4Mqgkf1CXztLVBSt2Ks3oZwbuwXPXLWyouBWLVWGNWQexSgSxsj_Qulcy4a-fN
true true true
```

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

The send options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `str = ""` | Your contact address, as a `mailto:` or a web address; the services require it. |
| `ttl` | `int = 2419200` | How many seconds the service should hold the message for a browser that is off. |
| `urgency` | `str = ""` | The urgency: `very-low`, `low`, `normal` or `high`. |
| `topic` | `str = ""` | The topic; a new message with the same topic replaces an earlier undelivered one. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Keys.salam

### `Result`

```salam
struct Result
```

The result of the send.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The service accepted the message. |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status code of the service. |
| `gone` | `bool = false` | The subscription is no longer valid (404 or 410); delete it from your database. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The error message. |

webpush-Send.salam

```salam
import webpush

func main:
    k := webpush.KeysFrom("BLmOwafYGSjiuCX_1RSCO_n0YmacxYMDqitMydKE4A1Wp2qmUuMXg2IM_hzcrmZLun4jEu_lKfVdtnAp0LMK4NE", "Nhh4m4Va4yhL-53i302044iqeAeMtnOEYlIT2KWRJmg")
    sub := webpush.Subscription {
        endpoint = "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/abc",
        p256dh = "BCVxsr7N_eNgVRqvHtD0zTZsEc6-VV-JvLexhqUzORcxaOzi6-AYWXvTBHm4bjyPjs7Vd8pZGH6SRpkNtoIAiw4",
        auth = "BTBZMqHH6r4Tts7J_aSIgg"
    }
    o := webpush.NewOptions("mailto:ali@example.com")
    r := webpush.Send(k, sub, `{"title":"hello","body":"you have a new message"}`, o)
    if r.ok:
        println "sent", r.status
    else r.gone:
        println "the subscription has expired; delete it"
    else:
        println "error:", r.status, r.error
    end
end
```

## Constants and variables

### `DEFAULT_TTL`

```salam

```

How long the push service keeps a message by default: 28 days, in seconds.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Keys.salam

Makes a fresh VAPID key pair; make it once and keep it, because the subscriptions are tied to the public key.


The `Authorization` header for the service at the given address, at the given time in Unix seconds. The signature is deterministic, so the same input gives the same output.

The same, at the current time.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Keys.salam

### `EncryptWith`

```salam
func EncryptWith(sub: Subscription, payload: str, as_private: str, salt: str, ok &: bool): str
```

Encrypts the message with the given key and salt under RFC 8291; for testing against the standard vectors. In real work use `Encrypt`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Encrypt.salam

### `Encrypt`

```salam
func Encrypt(sub: Subscription, payload: str, ok &: bool): str
```

Encrypts the message for this subscription; with a fresh key and salt every time, so two outputs are never the same.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Encrypt.salam

### `Send`

```salam
func Send(keys: Keys, sub: Subscription, payload: str, opts: Options): Result
```

Encrypts the message and sends it to the browser push service with the VAPID header. An empty message is a notification with no body.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Send.salam

The default options with a contact address.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Keys.salam

```salam

```

Returns stored keys; `ok` is false when either one is empty.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: webpush-Keys.salam

# crypto

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/crypto/

SHA and MD5 digests, HMAC signatures, secure random numbers and password hashing.

This package gives the basic cryptography tools, all of them written in Salam. For the digest of a piece of text the `...Hex` functions are the simplest way; the `...Bytes` functions write the digest into memory you pass in yourself.

Never store a user password raw or under a plain digest; use `HashPassword` and `VerifyPassword`. To compare tokens, use `SecretEquals` rather than `==`. To encrypt data, see the tls package.

## Types

### `Sha256`

```salam
struct Sha256
```

The SHA-256 state for data that arrives in pieces, such as a large file.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `h` | `u32[]` | The internal state. |
| `blk` | `u8[]` | The partial block. |
| `blen` | `int = 0` | The length of the partial block. |
| `total` | `u64 = 0` | The total number of bytes. |

crypto-Hash.salam

```salam
import crypto
import encoding
import mem

func main:
    println crypto.Sha256Hex("abc")
    println crypto.Sha512Hex("abc").len()
    println crypto.Sha1Hex("abc")
    println crypto.Sha1Base64("abc")
    println crypto.Md5Hex("abc")

    text := "abc"
    out := mem.Allocate(64 as u64)
    crypto.Sha256Bytes(text as void*, 3, out)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 32)
    crypto.Sha384Bytes(text as void*, 3, out)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 48)
    crypto.Sha512Bytes(text as void*, 3, out)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 16).len()
    crypto.Sha1Bytes(text as void*, 3, out)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 20)
    crypto.Md5Bytes(text as void*, 3, out)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 16)

    mut h := crypto.Sha256New()
    crypto.Sha256Update(h, "a" as void*, 1)
    crypto.Sha256Update(h, "bc" as void*, 2)
    crypto.Sha256Final(h, out)
    println encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 32)
    mut b := crypto.Sha512New()
    crypto.Sha512Update(b, text as void*, 3)
    crypto.Sha512Final(b, out)
    println b.outlen
    mut s := crypto.Sha384New()
    crypto.Sha512Update(s, text as void*, 3)
    crypto.Sha512Final(s, out)
    println s.outlen, encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 48)
    mem.Free(out)

    println crypto.HashStr("hello") == crypto.HashStr("hello"), crypto.HashStr("a") != crypto.HashStr("b")
    println crypto.HashBytes(text as void*, 3 as u64) == crypto.HashStr("abc")
    println crypto.HashInt(42 as u64) != crypto.HashInt(43 as u64)
end
```

Output:

```text
ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
128
a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d
qZk+NkcGgWq6PiVxeFDCbJzQ2J0=
900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72
ungWv48Bz+pBQUDeXa4iI7ADYaOWF3qctBD/YfIAFa0=
ywB1P0WjXou1oD1pmsZQBycsMqsO3tFjGotgWkP/W+2AhgcroefMI1i67KE0yCWn
24
qZk+NkcGgWq6PiVxeFDCbJzQ2J0=
kAFQmDzST7DWlj99KOF/cg==
ungWv48Bz+pBQUDeXa4iI7ADYaOWF3qctBD/YfIAFa0=
64
48 ywB1P0WjXou1oD1pmsZQBycsMqsO3tFjGotgWkP/W+2AhgcroefMI1i67KE0yCWn
true true
true
true
```

### `Sha512`

```salam
struct Sha512
```

The SHA-512 or SHA-384 state for data in pieces.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `h` | `u64[]` | The internal state. |
| `blk` | `u8[]` | The partial block. |
| `blen` | `int = 0` | The length of the partial block. |
| `total` | `u64 = 0` | The total number of bytes. |
| `outlen` | `int = 64` | The digest length: 64 for SHA-512 and 48 for SHA-384. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: crypto-Hash.salam

## Functions

### `Sha256Hex`

```salam

```

The SHA-256 digest as hex, 64 characters.

### `Pbkdf2HmacSha256Hex`

```salam
func Pbkdf2HmacSha256Hex(password: str, salt: str, iterations: int, keylen: int): str
```

Derives a key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from a password and a salt, at the given iteration count.

crypto-Password.salam

```salam
import crypto
import str
import mem

func main:
    stored := crypto.HashPassword("s3cret-password")
    println str.StartsWith(stored, "pbkdf2-sha256$")
    println crypto.VerifyPassword("s3cret-password", stored), crypto.VerifyPassword("wrong", stored)
    println stored != crypto.HashPassword("s3cret-password")

    println crypto.Pbkdf2HmacSha256Hex("password", "salt", 1, 32)
    println crypto.SecretEquals("abc", "abc"), crypto.SecretEquals("abc", "xyz")

    println crypto.RandomHex(16).len(), crypto.RandomToken(32).len() > 0
    b := mem.Allocate(8 as u64)
    crypto.RandomBytes(b, 8)
    mem.Free(b)
end
```

### `HashPassword`

### `SecretEquals`


Compares two secrets in constant time, so the answer time gives nothing away about them; for tokens and signatures.

### `HmacSha256Hex`

```salam
func HmacSha256Hex(key: str, msg: str): str
```

The HMAC-SHA256 signature of a message under a key, as hex; for checking that the message is untouched and comes from whoever holds the key.

crypto-Hmac.salam

```salam
import crypto
import encoding
import mem

func main:
    key := "key"
    message := "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
    println crypto.HmacSha256Hex(key, message)
    println crypto.HmacSha1Hex(key, message)
    println crypto.HmacSha1Base64(key, message)
    println crypto.HmacSha384Hex(key, message).len(), crypto.HmacSha512Hex(key, message).len()

    out := mem.Allocate(64 as u64)
    crypto.HmacSha256Bytes(key, message, out)
    a := encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 32)
    crypto.HmacSha256Raw(key as void*, 3, message as void*, message.len(), out)
    println a == encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 32)
    crypto.HmacSha1Bytes(key, message, out)
    b := encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 20)
    crypto.HmacSha1Raw(key as void*, 3, message as void*, message.len(), out)
    println b == encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 20), b == crypto.HmacSha1Base64(key, message)
    crypto.HmacSha384Bytes(key, message, out)
    c := encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 48)
    crypto.HmacSha384Raw(key as void*, 3, message as void*, message.len(), out)
    println c == encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 48)
    crypto.HmacSha512Bytes(key, message, out)
    d := encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 64)
    crypto.HmacSha512Raw(key as void*, 3, message as void*, message.len(), out)
    println d == encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 64)
    mem.Free(out)
end
```

Output:

```text
f7bc83f430538424b13298e6aa6fb143ef4d59a14946175997479dbc2d1a3cd8
de7c9b85b8b78aa6bc8a7a36f70a90701c9db4d9
3nybhbi3iqa8ino29wqQcBydtNk=
96 128
true
true true
true
true
```

# jwt

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/jwt/

Making and checking JWT tokens, and guarding API routes.

A JWT is a token the server signs after a user logs in and the client sends with every request; by checking the signature the server knows who the user is without going to the database. This package supports the HMAC algorithms, HS256, HS384 and HS512, and never accepts a token with the `none` algorithm.

For an API, make a `Guard` and call `Require` or one of its siblings in every handler; when the token is wrong the error response is sent for you. The secret has to be long and random, for instance from `RandomToken` in crypto.

## Types

### `Token`

```salam
struct Token
```

A decoded token.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alg` | `str = ""` | The signing algorithm, such as `HS256`. |
| `typ` | `str = ""` | The type, usually `JWT`. |
| `kid` | `str = ""` | The key id, when the header carries one. |
| `claims` | `Claims` | The standard claims. |
| `header_json` | `str = ""` | The JSON text of the header. |
| `payload_json` | `str = ""` | The JSON text of the body. |
| `signing_input` | `str = ""` | The part that was signed: the header and the body with a dot between them. |
| `signature` | `str = ""` | The signature as url safe base64. |
| `valid` | `bool = false` | The signature and the times were checked and were right. |

jwt-Sign.salam

```salam
import jwt

func main:
    mut c := jwt.NewClaims()
    c.iss = "salamlang.ir"
    c.sub = "42"
    c.aud = "api"
    c.iat = 1700000000
    c.exp = 1700003600
    jwt.SetStr(c, "name", "Maryam")
    jwt.SetInt(c, "level", 3)
    jwt.SetBool(c, "admin", false)
    jwt.SetRaw(c, "scope", `"read write"`)
    jwt.SetRaw(c, "roles", `["editor","viewer"]`)
    println jwt.ClaimsJSON(c)

    mut err := 0
    token := jwt.SignHS256(c, "a-long-random-secret", err)
    println err == jwt.JWT_OK
    println token

    mut o := jwt.DefaultOptions()
    o.now = 1700001000
    o.issuer = "salamlang.ir"
    o.audience = "api"
    t := jwt.Verify(token, "a-long-random-secret", o, err)
    println t.valid, t.alg, t.typ, t.claims.sub
    println jwt.Str(t, "name"), jwt.Int(t, "level"), jwt.Bool(t, "admin"), jwt.Has(t, "email")
    println jwt.Raw(t, "level"), jwt.HasScope(t, "write"), jwt.HasAudience(t, "api"), jwt.ListHas(t, "roles", "editor")

    _ := jwt.Verify(token, "another-secret", o, err)
    println err == jwt.JWT_ERR_SIGNATURE, jwt.ErrorText(err)
    o.now = 1800000000
    _ := jwt.Verify(token, "a-long-random-secret", o, err)
    println err == jwt.JWT_ERR_EXPIRED, jwt.ErrorText(err)
    o.now = 1700001000
    o.issuer = "example.com"
    println jwt.IsValid(token, "a-long-random-secret", o)
    _ := jwt.Decode("abc", err)
    println err == jwt.JWT_ERR_MALFORMED
end
```

Output:


### `Claims`

```salam
struct Claims
```

The claims of a token.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iss` | `str = ""` | The issuer. |
| `sub` | `str = ""` | The subject, usually the user id. |
| `aud` | `str = ""` | The audience. |
| `aud_raw` | `str = ""` | The audience as JSON, when it is an array. |
| `exp` | `i64 = 0` | The expiry time in Unix seconds. |
| `nbf` | `i64 = 0` | The time before which it is not valid. |
| `iat` | `i64 = 0` | The issue time. |
| `jti` | `str = ""` | The unique id of the token. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | The other claims, as JSON. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: jwt-Sign.salam

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

The check options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alg` | `str = "HS256"` | The algorithm expected; a token with another one is rejected. |
| `issuer` | `str = ""` | The required issuer; empty means do not check it. |
| `audience` | `str = ""` | The required audience. |
| `subject` | `str = ""` | The required subject. |
| `leeway` | `i64 = 0` | How many seconds of clock difference to accept. |
| `now` | `i64 = 0` | The time to check against; zero means now. For testing. |
| `require_exp` | `bool = false` | Reject a token with no `exp`. |
| `require_nbf` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `nbf`. |
| `require_iat` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `iat`. |
| `require_sub` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `sub`. |
| `require_jti` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `jti`. |
| `check_typ` | `bool = true` | Check that the type is `JWT`. |

jwt-Algorithms.salam

```salam
import jwt

func main:
    println jwt.JWT_HS256, jwt.JWT_HS384, jwt.JWT_HS512
    println jwt.IsSupportedAlg("HS512"), jwt.IsSupportedAlg("none"), jwt.DigestSize("HS384")

    mut c := jwt.NewClaims()
    c.sub = "7"
    c.jti = "t-1"
    jwt.ExpiresIn(c, 3600)
    jwt.NotBeforeIn(c, 0)
    mut err := 0
    one := jwt.SignHS384(c, "k", err)
    two := jwt.SignHS512(c, "k", err)
    three := jwt.Sign(c, jwt.JWT_HS256, "k", err)
    four := jwt.SignWithKid(c, "HS256", "key-2026", "k", err)
    println jwt.Decode(one, err).alg, jwt.Decode(two, err).alg, jwt.Decode(four, err).kid

    t := jwt.VerifyHS256(three, "k", err)
    println t.valid, jwt.SecondsRemaining(t) > 3500
    b := jwt.Verify(one, "k", jwt.OptionsFor("HS384"), err)
    println b.valid
    _ := jwt.Verify(one, "k", jwt.DefaultOptions(), err)
    println jwt.ErrorText(err)

    raw := jwt.SignJSON(`{"sub":"1"}`, "HS256", "", "k", err)
    println raw
    d := jwt.Decode(raw, err)
    println d.header_json, d.payload_json
    println jwt.SignatureOf(d.signing_input, "HS256", "k") == d.signature

    encoded := jwt.B64UrlEncode("hello?")
    println encoded.len()
    mut ok := false
    println jwt.B64UrlDecode(encoded, ok), ok
    println jwt.B64UrlEncodeBytes("hi?" as void*, 3)
    _ := jwt.SignHS256(c, "", err)
    println err == jwt.JWT_ERR_EMPTY_SECRET, jwt.ErrorText(err)
    println jwt.JWT_ERR_BAD_BASE64, jwt.JWT_ERR_BAD_JSON, jwt.JWT_ERR_ALG_UNSUPPORTED, jwt.JWT_ERR_ALG_MISMATCH
    println jwt.JWT_ERR_NOT_YET_VALID, jwt.JWT_ERR_ISSUED_IN_FUTURE, jwt.JWT_ERR_ISSUER, jwt.JWT_ERR_AUDIENCE
    println jwt.ErrorText(jwt.JWT_ERR_SUBJECT), "/", jwt.ErrorText(jwt.JWT_ERR_MISSING_CLAIM), "/", jwt.ErrorText(jwt.JWT_ERR_TYPE)
end
```

Output:

```text

true true
true
algorithm mismatch

{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"} {"sub":"1"}

true empty secret

```

### `Guard`

```salam
struct Guard
```

An HTTP route guard: the secret, the check options and the cookie name.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | `str = ""` | The signing secret. |
| `opts` | `Options` | The check options. |
| `cookie` | `str = ""` | The name of a cookie the token is also read from; empty means the Authorization header only. |
| `realm` | `str = "api"` | The name that goes in the `WWW-Authenticate` header. |

jwt-Guard.salam

```salam
import jwt
import net.http
import net.router

mut guard := jwt.NewGuard("a-server-secret-only-the-server-knows")

func login(ctx: i64):
    mut err := 0
    mut c := jwt.NewClaims()
    c.sub = "42"
    jwt.SetStr(c, "scope", "read")
    jwt.SetRaw(c, "roles", `["editor"]`)
    token := jwt.Issue(guard, c, 3600, err)
    jwt.SetSessionCookieInsecure(ctx, guard, token, 3600)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, token)
end

func me(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.Require(ctx, guard, t):
        http.Ctx_text(ctx, "hello user " + t.claims.sub)
    end
end

func admin(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.RequireScope(ctx, guard, "admin", t):
        http.Ctx_text(ctx, "admin panel")
    end
end

func edit(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.RequireClaim(ctx, guard, "roles", "editor", t):
        http.Ctx_text(ctx, "editor")
    end
end

func profile(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.RequireSubject(ctx, guard, http.Ctx_param(ctx, "id"), t):
        http.Ctx_text(ctx, "your own profile")
    end
end

func manual(ctx: i64):
    mut err := 0
    t := jwt.Check(ctx, guard, err)
    if jwt.BearerToken(ctx).len() == 0 and jwt.TokenFrom(ctx, guard).len() == 0:
        jwt.MissingCredential(ctx, guard)
    else err != jwt.JWT_OK:
        jwt.Unauthorized(ctx, guard, jwt.ErrorText(err))
    else t.claims.sub == "0":
        jwt.Forbidden(ctx, "the user is blocked")
    else:
        http.Ctx_text(ctx, "valid")
    end
end

func logout(ctx: i64):
    jwt.ClearSessionCookie(ctx, guard)
    http.Ctx_text(ctx, "you are logged out")
end

func main:
    guard.cookie = "session"
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/login", login)
    router.Get(r, "/me", me)
    router.Get(r, "/admin", admin)
    router.Get(r, "/edit", edit)
    router.Get(r, "/users/:id", profile)
    router.Get(r, "/check", manual)
    router.Post(r, "/logout", logout)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19630)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19630"

    login_response := http.Post(base + "/login", "")
    token := http.Body(login_response)
    println http.CookieMap(login_response).get("session") == token
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
    println jwt.ParseBearer("Bearer " + token) == token
    ask(base, "/me", headers)
    ask(base, "/admin", headers)
    ask(base, "/edit", headers)
    ask(base, "/users/42", headers)
    ask(base, "/users/7", headers)
    ask(base, "/check", headers)
    ask(base, "/me", http.NewHeaders())
    mut bad := http.NewHeaders()
    bad.insert("Authorization", "Bearer x.y.z")
    ask(base, "/check", bad)
    mut cookie := http.NewHeaders()
    cookie.insert("Cookie", "session=" + token)
    ask(base, "/me", cookie)

    mut access := ""
    mut refresh := ""
    mut err := 0
    println jwt.IssuePair(guard, "42", 900, 86400, access, refresh, err), access != refresh
    one := jwt.IssueFor(guard, "42", 60, err)
    println jwt.Verify(one, guard.secret, guard.opts, err).claims.sub, guard.realm
end

func ask(base: str, path: str, headers: HashMap<str, str>):
    response := http.GetWith(base + path, headers)
    println path, http.Status(response), http.Body(response)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true
/me 200 hello user 42
/admin 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"missing scope: admin"}
/edit 200 editor
/users/42 200 your own profile
/users/7 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"not your resource"}
/check 200 valid
/me 401 {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"missing bearer token"}
/check 401 {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"invalid base64url segment"}
/me 200 hello user 42
true true
42 api
```

# tls

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/tls/

Secure TLS 1.3 and 1.2 connections and public key cryptography tools, with no OpenSSL needed.

The tls package is a complete implementation of TLS written in Salam and needs no outside library. A client connects with `Dial` and checks the server certificate against the system roots; a server reads its certificate and key with `NewServerConfig` and secures each connection with `WrapServer`.

The cryptography tools here are also useful for building protocols of your own: the two sides make a shared secret with ECDH, derive a key from it with HKDF, and encrypt and seal the message with AES-GCM. Keys and data are passed around as base64.

## Types

### `Config`

```salam
struct Config
```

The client configuration.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server_name` | `str = ""` | The hostname for SNI and for certificate verification. |
| `ca_file` | `str = ""` | The file of root certificates; empty means the system roots. |
| `insecure_skip_verify` | `bool = false` | Do not verify the certificate; for testing only, since it leaves the connection open to eavesdropping. |
| `alpn` | `str = ""` | The protocol for ALPN, such as `h2`. |
| `aes_only` | `bool = false` | Offer AES ciphers only. |

tls-Client.salam

```salam
import tls

func main:
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("example.com")
    cfg.alpn = "http/1.1"
    mut conn := tls.Dial("example.com", 443, cfg)
    if not tls.ConnOk(conn):
        println "error:", tls.ConnError(conn)
        ret
    end
    println tls.Version(conn), tls.CipherName(conn), tls.PeerCertCount(conn)
    _ := tls.Write(conn, "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
    mut body := ""
    until tls.ConnOk(conn):
        chunk := tls.Read(conn, 4096)
        if chunk.len() == 0:
            break
        end
        body += chunk
    end
    println body.len() > 0
    tls.Close(conn)
end
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One TLS connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `h` | `Handshake` | The handshake state. |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `open` | `bool = false` | The connection is open. |
| `insecure` | `bool = false` | Without certificate verification. |
| `pending` | `Buf` | Data that has been read but not taken yet. |
| `err` | `str = ""` | The error message. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: tls-Client.salam

### `ServerConfig`

```salam
struct ServerConfig
```

The server configuration: the certificate chain and the private key.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chain` | `Roots` | The certificate chain. |
| `key` | `PrivateKey` | The private key. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Both were read. |

tls-Server.salam

```salam
import tls
import net.tcp
import mem

func main:
    cfg := tls.NewServerConfig("cert.pem", "key.pem")
    if not cfg.ok:
        println "the certificate or key could not be read"
        ret
    end
    server := tcp.Bind(8443)
    until true:
        sock := tcp.Accept(server)
        mut conn := tls.WrapServer(sock.fd, cfg)
        if tls.ConnOk(conn):
            if tls.Readable(conn) or tls.Pending(conn) > 0:
                println tls.Read(conn, 1024)
            end
            buffer := mem.Allocate(256 as u64)
            n := tls.ReadBytes(conn, buffer, 256)
            _ := tls.WriteBytes(conn, buffer, n)
            _ := tls.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello")
            mem.Free(buffer)
            println tls.Fd(conn) >= 0
        end
        tls.Close(conn)
    end
end
```

## Constants and variables

### `TLS10`

```salam
const TLS10: i32 = 769
```

The version number of TLS 1.0; not supported.

tls-Certs.salam

```salam
import tls
import net.tcp
import encoding
import io

func main:
    roots := tls.LoadRoots("/etc/ssl/cert.pem")
    println tls.RootCount(roots)

    chain := tls.LoadCertChainFile("cert.pem")
    println tls.RootCount(chain)
    mut key := tls.LoadPrivateKeyFile("key.pem")
    mut key2 := tls.ParsePrivateKeyPEM("-----BEGIN ...")
    tls.FreePrivateKey(key2)

    cert := tls.HexDecodeBuf("3082...")
    println tls.CertIsValid(cert), tls.CertSubjectCN(cert)
    code := tls.VerifyCert(cert, roots, "example.com")
    println code, tls.VerifyError(code)

    digest := tls.HashDigest(false, "message")
    sig := tls.NewBuf(512)
    println tls.SignRSAPKCS1(key, false, digest, sig)
    println tls.SignRSAPSS(key, false, digest, sig)
    println tls.VerifyRSAPSSWithKey(key, false, digest, sig)
    r := tls.NewBuf(32)
    s := tls.NewBuf(32)
    if tls.SignECDSA(key, digest, r, s):
        der := tls.ECDSADerEncode(r, s, 32)
        println tls.VerifyECDSADERWithKey(key, digest, der)
    end

    pem := io.ReadFile("rsa-key.pem")
    mut good := false
    println tls.RsaKeyBits(pem)
    println tls.RsaSignPkcs1Sha256(pem, encoding.Base64Encode("..."), good)

    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("internal.example")
    cfg.ca_file = "company-ca.pem"
    cfg.aes_only = true
    mut conn := tls.Dial("internal.example", 443, cfg)
    println tls.ConnOk(conn)
    tls.Close(conn)
    sock := tcp.Dial("example.com", 443)
    mut conn2 := tls.WrapClient(sock.fd, tls.NewConfig("example.com"))
    println tls.Version(conn2) == "TLS1.3"
    tls.Close(conn2)
    println tls.TLS10, tls.TLS11, tls.TLS12, tls.TLS13
    println tls.SelfTest()
    tls.FreeRoots(roots)
    tls.FreePrivateKey(key)
end
```

### `EcdhP256Generate`

```salam
func EcdhP256Generate(priv &: str, pub_spki &: str): bool
```

An ECDH key pair on the P-256 curve: the private key as base64 and the SPKI public key as base64.

tls-Crypto.salam

```salam
import tls
import encoding

func main:
    mut priv1 := ""
    mut pub1 := ""
    mut priv2 := ""
    mut pub2 := ""
    println tls.EcdhP256Generate(priv1, pub1), tls.EcdhP256Generate(priv2, pub2)
    mut good := false
    secret1 := tls.EcdhP256Shared(priv1, pub2, good)
    secret2 := tls.EcdhP256Shared(priv2, pub1, good)
    println good, secret1 == secret2

    point1 := tls.EcdhP256PublicPoint(priv1)
    point2 := tls.EcdhP256PublicPoint(priv2)
    println tls.EcdhP256SharedPoint(priv1, point2, good) == tls.EcdhP256SharedPoint(priv2, point1, good)

    salt := tls.RandomSalt(16)
    key := tls.HkdfSha256(secret1, salt, "chat v1", 32, good)
    println good, key == tls.HkdfSha256(secret2, salt, "chat v1", 32, good)
    println tls.HkdfSha256Raw(secret1, salt, encoding.Base64Encode("chat v1"), 32, good) == key

    nonce := tls.GcmNonce(0)
    sealed := tls.AesGcmSeal(key, nonce, "hello, this message is encrypted", good)
    println good
    println tls.AesGcmOpen(key, nonce, sealed, good), good
    _ := tls.AesGcmOpen(key, tls.GcmNonce(1), sealed, good)
    println good
    binary := tls.AesGcmSealBytes(key, nonce, encoding.Base64Encode("abc"), good)
    println encoding.Base64Decode(tls.AesGcmOpenBytes(key, nonce, binary, good))

    digest := encoding.Base64Encode("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
    sig := tls.P256Sign(priv1, digest, good)
    println good, tls.P256Verify(point1, digest, sig), tls.P256Verify(point2, digest, sig)

    b := tls.HashDigest(false, "abc")
    println tls.BufLen(b), tls.HexEncodeBuf(b)
    mut hex := tls.HexDecodeBuf("cafe")
    tls.BufAppendStr(hex, "!")
    println tls.BufLen(hex), tls.HexEncodeBuf(hex)
    mut zeros := tls.NewZeroBuf(4)
    println tls.HexEncodeBuf(zeros)
    mut empty := tls.NewBuf(64)
    println tls.BufLen(empty)
    tls.WipeBuf(hex)
    tls.FreeBuf(hex)
    tls.FreeBuf(zeros)
    tls.FreeBuf(empty)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true true
true
true true
true
true
hello, this message is encrypted true
false
abc
true true false
32 ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
3 cafe21
00000000
0
```
