# ssl

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ssl/

A familiar OpenSSL style interface for secure connections, on top of Salam's own TLS.

This package gives the same OpenSSL style context and connection interface, but underneath it is Salam's own tls and it needs no outside library. For new code tls is simpler; this package is for code already written in this style. Set the hostname before `Connect` when certificates are verified.

The flow: make a context, hand the TCP connection to it with `Wrap`, for a client set the hostname and call `Connect`, then read and write.

## Types

### `Context`

```salam
struct Context
```

A TLS context, shared between connections.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The pointer to the context state. |

ssl-Client.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp

func main:
    ctx := ssl.NewClientContext()
    if not ssl.CtxOk(ctx):
        println ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret
    end
    _ := ssl.SetMinVersion(ctx, ssl.TLS1_3)
    _ := ssl.SetDefaultVerifyPaths(ctx)
    sock := tcp.Dial("example.com", 443)
    conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
    _ := ssl.SetHostname(conn, "example.com")
    if not ssl.ConnOk(conn) or not ssl.Connect(conn):
        println "the handshake failed:", ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret
    end
    println ssl.PeerVerified(conn), ssl.VerifyResult(conn) == ssl.CERT_OK
    n := ssl.Write(conn, "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
    if n <= 0:
        println "error code:", ssl.ErrorCode(conn, n)
    end
    println ssl.Read(conn, 4096).len() > 0
    ssl.Shutdown(conn)
    ssl.Close(conn)
    ssl.CloseContext(ctx)
    tcp.Close(sock)
end
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One TLS connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The pointer to the connection state. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ssl-Client.salam

## Constants and variables

### `VERIFY_NONE`

```salam
const VERIFY_NONE: i32 = 0
```

Verification mode: no verification.

ssl-Server.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp

func main:
    ctx := ssl.NewServerContext("cert.pem", "key.pem")
    if not ssl.CtxOk(ctx):
        println ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret
    end
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_NONE)
    _ := ssl.LoadVerifyLocationsFile(ctx, "clients-ca.pem")
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_PEER)
    println ssl.FILETYPE_PEM, ssl.TLS1_2
    server := tcp.Bind(8443)
    until true:
        sock := tcp.Accept(server)
        conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
        if ssl.Accept(conn):
            request := ssl.Read(conn, 4096)
            _ := ssl.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: " + request.len() + "\r\n\r\n" + request)
        end
        ssl.Close(conn)
    end
end
```

### `VERIFY_PEER`


Verification mode: verify the certificate of the other side.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ssl-Server.salam

# ssh

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ssh/

SSH connections, running a command on a server, and working with files over SFTP.

This package is an SSH client written in Salam and needs neither OpenSSH nor any other library. Make a `Config` with the host and the user, pick the login method, and connect with `Connect`; then send a command with `Exec`, or move files with `SftpOpen`. It suits automating deployments and backups.

The host key is checked against the known_hosts file, the way `ssh` itself does. The buffer and reader functions build and read the data format of the SSH protocol; an ordinary program does not need them.

## Types

### `Config`

```salam
struct Config
```

The configuration of an SSH connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 22` | The port; 22 by default. |
| `user` | `str = ""` | The user name. |
| `password` | `str = ""` | The password. |
| `use_password` | `bool = false` | Log in with a password. |
| `key_pem` | `str = ""` | The private key as text. |
| `use_key` | `bool = false` | Log in with a key. |
| `hostkey_mode` | `int = 1` | The host key check mode. |
| `known_hosts_path` | `str = ""` | The path of the known_hosts file. |

ssh-Config.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("example.com", ssh.DefaultPort, "deploy")
    println cfg.host, cfg.port, cfg.user, cfg.hostkey_mode == ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_ACCEPT_NEW
    ssh.WithPassword(cfg, "s3cret")
    println cfg.use_password, cfg.use_key
    ssh.WithKeyPEM(cfg, "-----BEGIN OPENSSH KEY-----")
    println cfg.use_key, cfg.key_pem.len() > 0
    println ssh.WithKeyFile(cfg, "/nonexistent/id_rsa")
    ssh.WithHostKeyMode(cfg, ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT)
    ssh.WithKnownHostsPath(cfg, "/home/deploy/.ssh/known_hosts")
    println cfg.hostkey_mode, cfg.known_hosts_path
    println ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_INSECURE, ssh.ClientVersion
end
```

Output:

```text
example.com 22 deploy true
true false
true true
false
2 /home/deploy/.ssh/known_hosts
0 SSH-2.0-Salam_1.0
```

### `Session`

```salam
struct Session
```

One session over the connection: one command or one shell.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ch` | `Channel` | The SSH channel. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The session opened. |

ssh-Exec.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("server.example.com", 22, "deploy")
    _ := ssh.WithKeyFile(cfg, "/home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa")
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    if not ssh.Ok(client):
        println "error:", ssh.Error(client)
        ret
    end
    println "host key:", ssh.HostKeyFingerprint(client)

    r := ssh.Exec(client, "uname -a")
    println r.ok, r.exit_code, r.stdout, r.stderr
    r2 := ssh.RunCommand(client, "df -h /")
    println r2.stdout

    mut tail := ssh.NewSession(client)
    _ := ssh.RequestPty(tail, client, "xterm", 120, 40)
    if ssh.Start(tail, client, "tail -f /var/log/app.log"):
        repeat 10:
            _ := ssh.ReadStep(tail, client)
            print ssh.DrainOutput(tail)
            print ssh.DrainStderrOutput(tail)
        end
    end
    ssh.CloseSession(tail, client)

    mut shell := ssh.NewSession(client)
    if ssh.Shell(shell, client):
        _ := ssh.WriteInput(shell, client, "echo hello\nexit\n")
        ssh.CloseInput(shell, client)
        code := ssh.Wait(shell, client)
        println code, ssh.ExitCode(shell), ssh.SessionClosed(shell)
        println ssh.Output(shell), ssh.StderrOutput(shell)
    end
    ssh.CloseSession(shell, client)

    probe := ssh.Dial(cfg)
    println ssh.Ok(probe)
    println ssh.Reconnect(client)
    println ssh.SelfTest()
    ssh.Close(client)
end
```

### `ExecResult`

```salam
struct ExecResult
```

The result of running one command.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stdout` | `str = ""` | The output. |
| `stderr` | `str = ""` | The error output. |
| `exit_code` | `int = -1` | The exit code. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The command ran. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ssh-Exec.salam

### `Sftp`

```salam
struct Sftp
```

An SFTP session for working with the files on the server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ch` | `Channel` | The channel. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It opened. |
| `next_id` | `u32 = 1` | The number of the next request. |

ssh-Sftp.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("files.example.com", 22, "ali")
    ssh.WithPassword(cfg, "s3cret")
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    mut sftp := ssh.SftpOpen(client)
    if not sftp.ok:
        println ssh.Error(client)
        ret
    end
    println ssh.MkdirAll(client, sftp, "/backup/2026/09")
    println ssh.Upload(client, sftp, "report.pdf", "/backup/2026/09/report.pdf")
    println ssh.UploadDir(client, sftp, "site", "/var/www/site")
    if ssh.Exists(client, sftp, "/backup/2026/09/report.pdf"):
        info := ssh.Stat(client, sftp, "/backup/2026/09/report.pdf")
        println info.name, info.size, info.is_dir, info.permissions
    end
    each info in ssh.ListDir(client, sftp, "/backup"):
        println info.name, info.is_dir
    end
    println ssh.IsLink(client, sftp, "/current"), ssh.Lstat(client, sftp, "/current").name
    _ := ssh.Download(client, sftp, "/etc/hostname", "hostname.txt")
    _ := ssh.DownloadDir(client, sftp, "/var/log/app", "logs")
    _ := ssh.Rename(client, sftp, "/tmp/a", "/tmp/b")
    _ := ssh.Remove(client, sftp, "/tmp/b")
    _ := ssh.Mkdir(client, sftp, "/tmp/x")
    _ := ssh.Rmdir(client, sftp, "/tmp/x")
    _ := ssh.RemoveAll(client, sftp, "/tmp/old")
    ssh.SftpClose(client, sftp)
    ssh.Close(client)
end
```

### `HOSTKEY_MODE_INSECURE`

```salam
const HOSTKEY_MODE_INSECURE: i32 = 0
```

Host key mode: do not check it; the connection is then open to a man in the middle attack.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ssh-Config.salam

### `HOSTKEY_MODE_ACCEPT_NEW`

```salam
const HOSTKEY_MODE_ACCEPT_NEW: i32 = 1
```

Host key mode: accept a new host and record it in known_hosts, but reject a changed key; the default.

### `NewBuf`

```salam
func NewBuf(cap0: int): Buf
```

An empty buffer for building SSH protocol messages.

ssh-Wire.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut b := ssh.NewBuf(64)
    ssh.BufPutByte(b, 20)
    ssh.BufPutUint32(b, 7 as u32)
    ssh.BufPutUint64(b, 9 as u64)
    ssh.BufPutBool(b, true)
    ssh.BufPutStringStr(b, "ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-256")
    ssh.BufPutString(b, "abc" as void*, 3)
    ssh.BufPutBytes(b, "xy" as void*, 2)
    ssh.BufPutZeros(b, 2)
    ssh.BufPutMpintBytes(b, "\x80" as void*, 1)
    println b.len

    mut r := ssh.ReaderFromBuf(b)
    println ssh.RGetByte(r), ssh.RGetUint32(r), ssh.RGetUint64(r), ssh.RGetBool(r)
    names := ssh.RGetNameList(r)
    println names, ssh.NameListContains(names, "rsa-sha2-256")
    println ssh.RGetStringAsStr(r)
    ssh.RSkip(r, 4)
    println ssh.RRemaining(r)
    n := ssh.RGetMpintView(r)
    println n.len, ssh.RRemaining(r)

    println ssh.NegotiateFirstMatch("aes256-ctr,aes128-ctr", "aes128-ctr,aes256-ctr")
    println ssh.ConstantTimeEqual("abcd" as void*, "abcd" as void*, 4), ssh.ConstantTimeEqual("abcd" as void*, "abce" as void*, 4)

    mut b2 := ssh.NewBuf(16)
    ssh.BufPutStringBuf(b2, b)
    ssh.BufPutMpintBuf(b2, b)
    ssh.BufPutBuf(b2, b)
    mut r2 := ssh.NewReader(b2.p, b2.len)
    view := ssh.RGetStringView(r2)
    println view.len == b.len
    mut copied := ssh.RGetStringCopy(ssh.ReaderFromBuf(b2))
    mut number := ssh.RGetMpintCopy(r2)
    println copied.len, number.len, ssh.RRemaining(r2)
    ssh.WipeBuf(b)
    ssh.FreeBuf(b)
    ssh.FreeBuf(b2)
    ssh.FreeBuf(copied)
    ssh.FreeBuf(number)
end
```

Output:

```text
59
20 7 9 true
ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-256 true
abc
6
1 0
aes256-ctr
true false
true
59 59 59
```

# ftp

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ftp/

An FTP and FTPS client: listing a directory, uploading and downloading files.

This package connects to FTP servers, for uploading a site to shared hosting or pulling files off old equipment. Plain FTP sends the password and the data unencrypted; wherever the server supports it, use `DialTLS`, which encrypts both the commands and the data with AUTH TLS.

Transfers go in passive mode (PASV or EPSV), which works from behind a firewall. The parsing functions, such as `ParseListLine`, are available for writing tools of your own too.

## Types

### `FileInfo`

```salam
struct FileInfo
```

The information about one file from the server listing.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `size` | `i64 = 0` | The size. |
| `is_dir` | `bool = false` | It is a directory. |
| `is_link` | `bool = false` | It is a link. |
| `mode` | `str = ""` | The permissions, such as `rw-r--r--`. |
| `raw_date` | `str = ""` | The date exactly as the server wrote it. |

ftp-Parse.salam

```salam
import ftp

func main:
    println ftp.ReplyCode("230 Login successful."), ftp.ReplyCode("broken")
    println ftp.IsFinalLine("211-Features:"), ftp.IsFinalLine("211 End")
    println ftp.ParsePasv("227 Entering Passive Mode (192,168,1,10,19,137)")
    println ftp.ParseEpsv("229 Entering Extended Passive Mode (|||50000|)")
    file := ftp.ParseListLine("-rw-r--r--    1 ftp      ftp          1024 Sep 30 12:00 notes.txt")
    println file.name, file.size, file.is_dir, file.is_link, file.mode, file.raw_date
    folder := ftp.ParseListLine("drwxr-xr-x    2 ftp      ftp          4096 Jan 01  2026 backup")
    println folder.name, folder.is_dir
    link := ftp.ParseListLine("lrwxrwxrwx    1 ftp      ftp             7 Mar 03 09:15 current -> backup")
    println link.name, link.is_link
end
```

Output:

```text
230 0
false true
192.168.1.10:5001
50000
notes.txt 1024 false false rw-r--r-- Sep 30 12:00
backup true
current true
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

One FTP connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conn` | `tcp.Conn` | The TCP connection of the commands. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The connection is healthy. |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 21` | The port. |
| `rxbuf` | `str = ""` | The data that was read. |
| `last_reply` | `str = ""` | The last reply of the server. |
| `last_code` | `int = 0` | The code of the last reply. |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | The command channel is encrypted. |
| `tls_idx` | `int = -1` | The index of the TLS connection. |
| `prot_p` | `bool = false` | The data channel is encrypted too. |
| `tls_cfg` | `tls.Config` | The TLS configuration. |

ftp-Client.salam

```salam
import ftp
import tls

func main:
    mut c := ftp.DialTLS("ftp.example.com", 21)
    if not ftp.Ok(c) or not ftp.Login(c, "ali", "s3cret"):
        println ftp.LastCode(c), ftp.LastReply(c)
        ret
    end
    println ftp.Secure(c), ftp.SecureData(c)
    println ftp.System(c)
    println ftp.Features(c)
    _ := ftp.Binary(c)
    println ftp.Pwd(c)
    _ := ftp.MkdirAll(c, "/site/assets")
    _ := ftp.Cwd(c, "/site")
    _ := ftp.Write(c, "index.html", "<h1>hello</h1>")
    _ := ftp.Append(c, "log.txt", "one more line\n")
    println ftp.Read(c, "index.html")
    println ftp.Upload(c, "logo.png", "assets/logo.png")
    println ftp.Download(c, "log.txt", "log-copy.txt")
    each entry in ftp.List(c, "."):
        println entry.name, entry.size, entry.is_dir
    end
    each name in ftp.NameList(c, "assets"):
        println name
    end
    println ftp.ListRaw(c, ".").len() > 0
    println ftp.Size(c, "index.html"), ftp.ModTime(c, "index.html")
    println ftp.IsDir(c, "assets"), ftp.IsLink(c, "current"), ftp.Exists(c, "old.html")
    _ := ftp.Rename(c, "log.txt", "log-1.txt")
    _ := ftp.Move(c, "log-1.txt", "archive/log-1.txt")
    _ := ftp.Delete(c, "archive/log-1.txt")
    _ := ftp.CdUp(c)
    _ := ftp.Mkdir(c, "tmp")
    _ := ftp.Rmdir(c, "tmp")
    _ := ftp.RemoveAll(c, "/site/old")
    _ := ftp.UploadDir(c, "public", "/site")
    _ := ftp.DownloadDir(c, "/site", "backup")
    println ftp.Command(c, "SITE CHMOD 644 index.html")
    println ftp.Noop(c)
    _ := ftp.Ascii(c)
    ftp.Quit(c)
    ftp.Close(c)

    mut plain := ftp.Dial("ftp.example.com", 21)
    println ftp.AuthTLS(plain)
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("ftp.example.com")
    cfg.ca_file = "company-ca.pem"
    mut configured := ftp.DialTLSWith("ftp.example.com", 21, cfg)
    mut upgraded := ftp.Dial("ftp.example.com", 21)
    println ftp.AuthTLSWith(upgraded, cfg)
    ftp.Close(plain)
    ftp.Close(configured)
    ftp.Close(upgraded)
end
```

# rpc

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/rpc/

JSON-RPC 2.0 and MessagePack-RPC: a server, a client and registering methods.

With a remote procedure call one program calls another program's methods as if they were its own routines. On the server side you tie each method to a routine with `Register`; that routine takes the call's number, reads the parameters with `CallParamInt` and the like, and answers with `Reply...` or `Fail`.

The messages are exchanged with the JSON codec (JSON-RPC 2.0) or MessagePack, and over TCP they are separated by one of three framings, line, header (like LSP) or length prefixed; the client and the server must have the same framing. `HandleText` does the same thing without a network, so you can put RPC behind an net/http route.

## Types

### `Server`

```salam
struct Server
```

An RPC server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port; zero means a free port. |
| `codec` | `int = 0` | The codec. |
| `framing` | `int = 0` | The framing. |
| `listen_fd` | `i64 = -1` | The listening socket. |
| `running` | `bool = false` | It is running. |
| `served` | `int = 0` | The number of connections answered. |

rpc-Serve.salam

```salam
import rpc
import net.tcp
import compress

func echo(c: i64):
    rpc.Reply(c, rpc.CallParams(c))
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("echo", echo)
    if rpc.HandleText("").len() == 0:
        _ := rpc.ServeStdio(rpc.RPC_FRAME_HEADER)
        ret
    end

    mut s := rpc.NewServer(4000, rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK)
    rpc.SetFraming(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH)
    if rpc.Listen(s):
        println "on port", rpc.Port(s), s.running
        rpc.Serve(s)
    end

    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 4001)
    _ := rpc.ServeConn(conn.fd, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)

    c := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 4002)
    mut client := rpc.ClientFromFd(c.fd, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
    println rpc.ResultStr(rpc.CallNoParams(client, "version"))

    mut stream := rpc.NewStream(c.fd)
    _ := rpc.WriteFrameStr(c.fd, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"echo","params":[1],"id":1}`)
    _ := rpc.WriteFrame(c.fd, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, compress.BufFromStr(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"echo","id":2}`))
    mut ok := false
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(stream, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok)
    answer := rpc.HandlePayload(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, compress.BufFromStr(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"echo","params":[3],"id":3}`))
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(answer)
    rpc.FreeStream(stream)
    rpc.StopServer(s)
end
```

### `Stream`

```salam
struct Stream
```

The input stream that separates the frames from a socket or from memory.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket. |
| `data` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The data read. |
| `pos` | `int = 0` | The read position. |
| `closed` | `bool = false` | The input is finished. |
| `has_fd` | `bool = false` | It is over a socket. |

rpc-Frames.salam

```salam
import rpc
import compress

func main:
    line := rpc.FrameEncodeStr(rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, `{"a":1}`)
    headed := rpc.FrameEncodeStr(rpc.RPC_FRAME_HEADER, `{"b":2}`)
    sized := rpc.FrameEncode(rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH, compress.BufFromStr(`{"c":3}`))
    println line.len, headed.len, sized.len
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(headed).len() > 0

    mut s := rpc.NewMemStream()
    rpc.FeedStr(s, `{"x":1}` + "\n" + `{"x":2}` + "\n")
    mut ok := false
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok), ok
    println rpc.StreamPending(s)
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok)
    _ := rpc.ReadFrameStr(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok)
    println ok, rpc.StreamClosed(s)

    mut s2 := rpc.NewMemStream()
    rpc.FeedBuf(s2, headed)
    rpc.FeedBuf(s2, sized)
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(s2, rpc.RPC_FRAME_HEADER, ok)
    b := rpc.ReadFrame(s2, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH, ok)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(b), ok
    println rpc.RPC_READ_CHUNK, rpc.RPC_MAX_FRAME
    rpc.FreeStream(s)
    rpc.FreeStream(s2)
end
```

Output:

```text
8 28 11
true
{"x":1} true
8
{"x":2}
false false
{"b":2}
{"c":3} true
4096 33554432
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

An RPC client over a TCP connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conn` | `tcp.Conn` | The connection. |
| `stream` | `Stream` | The reading stream. |
| `codec` | `int = 0` | The codec. |
| `framing` | `int = 0` | The framing. |
| `next_id` | `i64 = 1` | The next request id. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It is healthy. |
| `last_error` | `str = ""` | The last error. |

rpc-Client.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value
import net.http
import net.router
import sync

mut server := rpc.NewServer(0, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func add(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, rpc.CallParamInt(c, "a", 0) + rpc.CallParamInt(c, "b", 1))
end

func clock(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyStr(c, "12:00")
end

func note(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyNull(c)
end

func run_server():
    _ := rpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := rpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func endpoint(ctx: i64):
    http.Ctx_json(ctx, rpc.HandleText(http.Ctx_body(ctx)))
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("add", add)
    rpc.Register("time", clock)
    rpc.Register("note", note)
    rpc.SetFraming(server, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)
    println rpc.Port(server) > 0

    mut client := rpc.DialClient("127.0.0.1", rpc.Port(server), rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
    rpc.ClientSetFraming(client, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)
    println rpc.ClientOk(client)
    mut params := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueInt(2))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueInt(40))
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.Call(client, "add", params))
    println rpc.ResultStr(rpc.CallNoParams(client, "time"))
    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<value.Value>
    args.push(value.ValueInt(1))
    args.push(value.ValueInt(2))
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.CallArgs(client, "add", args))
    println rpc.Notify(client, "note", value.NewValueArray())
    mut batch := Vector {} as Vector<rpc.Request>
    batch.push(rpc.NewRequest("add", params, 10))
    batch.push(rpc.NewRequest("missing", value.NewValueArray(), 11))
    answers := rpc.CallBatch(client, batch)
    println answers.items.len(), rpc.ResultInt(answers.items[0])
    println rpc.IsErrorResponse(answers.items[1]), rpc.ErrorCode(answers.items[1]), rpc.ErrorMessage(answers.items[1])
    rpc.CloseClient(client)
    println rpc.ClientOk(client), rpc.ClientError(client).len() >= 0
    join(t)
    rpc.StopServer(server)

    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/rpc", endpoint)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19631)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    answer := rpc.CallHTTP("http://127.0.0.1:19631/rpc", "add", params, 7)
    println rpc.ResultInt(answer)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true
42
12:00
3
true
2 42
true -32601 Method not found
false true
42
```

### `Error`

```salam
struct Error
```

A JSON-RPC error.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `int = 0` | The code. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message. |
| `data` | `value.Value` | The extra data. |
| `has_data` | `bool = false` | It has data. |

rpc-Messages.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value
import compress

func main:
    mut params := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueInt(2))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueString("hello"))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueFloat(1.5))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueBool(true))
    req := rpc.NewRequest("calc", params, 1)
    println rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(req)
    println rpc.ParamCount(req), rpc.ParamInt(req, "a", 0), rpc.ParamStr(req, "b", 1)
    println rpc.ParamFloat(req, "c", 2), rpc.ParamBool(req, "d", 3), rpc.HasParam(req, "e", 4)
    println value.AsInt(rpc.ParamAt(req, 0)), value.AsInt(rpc.Param(req, "a", 0))
    mut obj := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(obj, "name", value.ValueString("Ali"))
    req2 := rpc.NewRequestStrId("greet", obj, "req-1")
    println rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(req2)
    println value.AsString(rpc.ParamNamed(req2, "name"))
    note := rpc.NewNotification("tick", value.NewValueArray())
    println rpc.IsNotification(note), rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(note)

    mut ok := false
    read := rpc.JsonDecodeRequest(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":{"a":1,"b":2},"id":9}`, ok)
    println ok, read.method, read.msgid, rpc.ParamInt(read, "b", 1)

    answer := rpc.NewResponse(value.ValueInt(1), value.ValueString("ok"))
    println rpc.JsonEncodeResponse(answer)
    err := rpc.StdError(rpc.RPC_METHOD_NOT_FOUND)
    println err.code, err.message
    println rpc.JsonEncodeResponse(rpc.NewErrorResponse(value.ValueInt(2), rpc.NewError(-32000, "the server is busy")))
    with_data := rpc.ErrorWithData(rpc.RPC_INVALID_PARAMS, "bad", value.ValueString("x"))
    println with_data.has_data, rpc.JsonTopLevelError(rpc.StdError(rpc.RPC_PARSE_ERROR))

    one := rpc.JsonDecodeResponse(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":3.5,"id":1}`, ok)
    println ok, rpc.ResultFloat(one), rpc.IsErrorResponse(one)
    two := rpc.JsonDecodeResponse(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32601,"message":"nope"},"id":2}`, ok)
    println rpc.IsErrorResponse(two), rpc.ErrorCode(two), rpc.ErrorMessage(two)
    all := rpc.JsonDecodeResponses(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":true,"id":1},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":"x","id":2}]`, ok)
    println all.is_batch, all.items.len(), rpc.ResultBool(all.items[0]), rpc.ResultStr(all.items[1])
    println rpc.JsonEncodeResponses(all)

    println rpc.CodecName(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON), rpc.CodecName(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK)
    println rpc.CodecDefaultFraming(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON) == rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, rpc.CodecDefaultFraming(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK) == rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH
    packed := rpc.EncodeRequest(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK, req)
    println packed.len, compress.BufGet(packed, 0)
    batch := rpc.DecodeBatch(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK, packed)
    println batch.ok, batch.items[0].method, batch.items[0].msgid
    println rpc.MsgpackDecodeBatch(rpc.MsgpackEncodeRequest(req)).items[0].method
    mp := rpc.MsgpackEncodeResponse(rpc.NewResponse(value.ValueInt(1), value.ValueInt(42)))
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.MsgpackDecodeResponse(mp, ok)), ok
    js := rpc.EncodeRequest(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, req)
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.DecodeResponse(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK, mp, ok)), js.len > 0
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(rpc.EncodeResponses(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, all)).len() > 0
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(rpc.EncodeTopLevelError(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, err))
    println rpc.RPC_MP_REQUEST, rpc.RPC_MP_RESPONSE, rpc.RPC_MP_NOTIFY
    println rpc.RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, rpc.RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR, rpc.RPC_SERVER_ERROR
    println rpc.RPC_KIND_REQUEST, rpc.RPC_KIND_NOTIFICATION, rpc.RPC_KIND_RESPONSE
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(compress.BufFromStr(rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(req))).len() > 0
end
```

Output:

```text
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "calc", "params": [2, "hello", 1.5, true]}
4 2 hello
```

### `Request`

```salam
struct Request
```

One request.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `str = ""` | The method name. |
| `params` | `value.Value` | The parameters: an array or an object. |
| `has_params` | `bool = false` | It has parameters. |
| `id` | `value.Value` | The id; a number or a string. |
| `has_id` | `bool = false` | It has an id; without one it is a notification. |
| `msgid` | `i64 = 0` | The numeric id. |
| `err_code` | `int = 0` | If the request could not be read, the error code. |
| `err_message` | `str = ""` | That error's message. |

rpc-Methods.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value

func add(c: i64):
    a := rpc.CallParamInt(c, "a", 0)
    b := rpc.CallParamInt(c, "b", 1)
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, a + b)
end

func divide(c: i64):
    divisor := rpc.CallParamFloat(c, "b", 1)
    if divisor == 0.0:
        rpc.FailInvalidParams(c, "division by zero")
        ret
    end
    rpc.ReplyFloat(c, rpc.CallParamFloat(c, "a", 0) / divisor)
end

func hello(c: i64):
    name := rpc.CallParamStr(c, "name", 0)
    if name.len() == 0:
        rpc.Fail(c, -32001, "a name is needed")
        ret
    end
    rpc.ReplyStr(c, "hello " + name)
end

func status(c: i64):
    mut info := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(info, value.ValueString(rpc.CallMethodName(c)))
    value.ArrayPush(info, value.ValueInt(rpc.CallParamCount(c)))
    value.ArrayPush(info, value.ValueBool(rpc.CallParamBool(c, "verbose", 0)))
    rpc.Reply(c, info)
end

func log_event(c: i64):
    println "event:", value.AsString(rpc.CallParam(c, "event", 0)), rpc.CallIsNotification(c)
    _ := rpc.CallParams(c)
    _ := rpc.CallRequest(c)
    rpc.ReplyNull(c)
end

func forbidden(c: i64):
    rpc.FailWithData(c, -32003, "you are not allowed", value.ValueString("admin"))
end

func always(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyBool(c, true)
end

func main:
    rpc.RegisterDoc("add", add, "adds two numbers")
    rpc.Register("divide", divide)
    rpc.Register("hello", hello)
    rpc.Register("status", status)
    rpc.Register("log", log_event)
    rpc.Register("admin", forbidden)
    rpc.Register("ping", always)
    println rpc.MethodCount(), rpc.HasMethod("add"), rpc.MethodDoc("add")
    println rpc.ListMethods().len()

    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":[2,40],"id":1}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":{"a":5,"b":6},"id":2}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"divide","params":[1,0],"id":3}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hello","params":["Maryam"],"id":"x"}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hello","params":[],"id":4}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"status","params":{"verbose":true},"id":5}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"admin","id":6}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"nope","id":7}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"log","params":{"event":"start"}}`).len()
    println rpc.HandleText(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"ping","id":8},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":[1,1],"id":9}]`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":`)

    mut ok := false
    req := rpc.JsonDecodeRequest(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":[20,22],"id":10}`, ok)
    answer := rpc.Invoke(req)
    println rpc.ResultInt(answer)
    batch := rpc.JsonDecodeBatch(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"ping","id":1}]`)
    println rpc.InvokeBatch(batch).items.len()

    println rpc.Unregister("ping"), rpc.HasMethod("ping")
    rpc.ResetRegistry()
    println rpc.MethodCount()
end
```

Output:

```text
7 true adds two numbers
7
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": 42}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": 11}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "division by zero", "code": -32602}, "id": 3}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "x", "result": "hello Maryam"}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "a name is needed", "code": -32001}, "id": 4}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "result": ["status", 1, true]}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "you are not allowed", "code": -32003, "data": "admin"}, "id": 6}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "Method not found", "code": -32601}, "id": 7}
event: start true
0
[{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 8, "result": true}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 9, "result": 2}]
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "Parse error", "code": -32700}, "id": null}
42
1
true false
0
```

### `Response`

```salam
struct Response
```

One response.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `value.Value` | The request's id. |
| `has_id` | `bool = false` | It has an id. |
| `result` | `value.Value` | The result. |
| `is_error` | `bool = false` | It is an error. |
| `err` | `Error` | The error. |
| `msgid` | `i64 = 0` | The numeric id. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Methods.salam

### `Batch`

```salam
struct Batch
```

A batch of requests.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The requests. |
| `is_batch` | `bool = false` | It came in as an array. |
| `ok` | `bool = true` | It was read correctly. |
| `err` | `Error` | If it was not, the error. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Methods.salam

### `Responses`

```salam
struct Responses
```

The responses of a batch.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The responses. |
| `is_batch` | `bool = false` | Send it as an array. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Messages.salam

### `Method`

```salam
struct Method
```

One registered method.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `fn` | `i64 = 0` | The routine. |
| `doc` | `str = ""` | The description. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Methods.salam

### `MethodTable`

```salam
struct MethodTable
```

The table of methods.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The methods. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Methods.salam

### `CallSlot`

```salam
struct CallSlot
```

The state of a call that is running.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `req` | `Request` | The request. |
| `result` | `value.Value` | The result. |
| `err` | `Error` | The error. |
| `is_error` | `bool = false` | It is an error. |
| `replied` | `bool = false` | It has been answered. |
| `busy` | `bool = false` | It is in use. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Methods.salam

### `SlotTable`

```salam
struct SlotTable
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The calls. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: rpc-Methods.salam

# grpc

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/grpc/

A gRPC server and client over HTTP/2: unary and streaming calls, metadata and status codes.

gRPC is a way of calling a remote procedure that runs over HTTP/2, and it is common in microservices. On the server side you register each method under its path, like `/demo.Greeter/SayHello`; the method routine reads the client's message with `Recv`, answers with `Send` and ends it with `SetStatus` or `Fail`.

On the client side, `UnaryCall` is a plain request, and for streams you use `StartCall`, `SendMessage`, `RecvMessage` and `FinishCall`. Messages are bytes; you usually build them with protobuf.

## Types

### `Status`

```salam
struct Status
```

The final status of a call.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `int = 0` | The code. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message. |

grpc-Calls.salam

```salam
import grpc
import compress
import sync

mut server := grpc.NewServer(0)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func hello(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    name := grpc.RecvStr(c, ok)
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, "hello " + name)
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func countdown(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    _ := grpc.Recv(c, ok)
    repeat 3 in i:
        _ := grpc.Send(c, compress.BufFromStr("" + (3 - i)))
    end
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func trace(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    _ := grpc.RecvStr(c, ok)
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, grpc.MDGet(grpc.CallMetadata(c), "x-trace") + " " + grpc.CallPath(c))
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func forbidden(c: i64):
    grpc.Fail(c, grpc.GRPC_PERMISSION_DENIED, "the token expired")
end

func run_server():
    _ := grpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := grpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func main:
    hello_path := grpc.MethodPath("demo.Greeter", "SayHello")
    println hello_path
    grpc.RegisterMethod(hello_path, hello)
    grpc.RegisterStreamMethod("/demo.Greeter/Countdown", countdown, false, true)
    grpc.RegisterMethod("/demo.Greeter/Trace", trace)
    grpc.RegisterMethod("/demo.Greeter/Admin", forbidden)
    println grpc.MethodCount(), grpc.HasMethod(hello_path)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)

    mut ch := grpc.Dial("127.0.0.1", grpc.Port(server))
    grpc.SetTimeout(ch, 5000)
    println grpc.ChannelOk(ch)
    mut result := grpc.Status {}
    println grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, hello_path, "Maryam", result), grpc.StatusOk(result)

    call := grpc.StartCall(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Countdown", grpc.NewMetadata())
    _ := grpc.SendMessage(ch, call, compress.BufFromStr("go"), true)
    mut more := true
    until more:
        mut ok := false
        msg := grpc.RecvMessage(ch, call, ok)
        if not ok:
            more = false
        else:
            println "message:", compress.BufToStrUnsafe(msg)
        end
    end
    println grpc.MDCount(grpc.CallHeaders(ch, call))
    println grpc.StatusString(grpc.FinishCall(ch, call))

    mut md := grpc.NewMetadata()
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "x-trace", "t-42")
    mut result2 := grpc.Status {}
    answer := grpc.UnaryCall(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Trace", compress.BufFromStr("x"), md, result2)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(answer)

    call2 := grpc.StartCall(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Trace", md)
    _ := grpc.SendMessage(ch, call2, compress.BufFromStr("y"), false)
    _ := grpc.CloseSend(ch, call2)
    mut ok2 := false
    _ := grpc.RecvMessage(ch, call2, ok2)
    _ := grpc.FinishCall(ch, call2)
    println ok2, grpc.CallTrailers(ch, call2).items.len() >= 0

    mut result3 := grpc.Status {}
    _ := grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Admin", "", result3)
    println result3.code, result3.message, grpc.StatusName(result3.code)
    mut result4 := grpc.Status {}
    _ := grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Nope", "", result4)
    println grpc.StatusString(result4)
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)
    join(t)
    grpc.StopServer(server)
    grpc.ResetMethods()
    println grpc.MethodCount()
end
```

Output:

```text
/demo.Greeter/SayHello
4 true
true
hello Maryam true
message: 3
message: 2
message: 1
0
OK
t-42 /demo.Greeter/Trace
true true
7 the token expired PERMISSION_DENIED
UNIMPLEMENTED: unknown method /demo.Greeter/Nope
0
```

### `MDEntry`

```salam
struct MDEntry
```

One metadata entry.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The key. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |
| `binary` | `bool = false` | It is binary. |

grpc-Wire.salam

```salam
import grpc
import compress
import net.http2

func main:
    one := grpc.FrameMessageStr("hello")
    println one.len, compress.BufGet(one, 0), compress.BufGet(one, 4)
    mut all := compress.NewByteBuf()
    compress.BufPushBuf(all, one)
    compress.BufPushBuf(all, grpc.FrameMessage(compress.BufFromStr("two"), false))
    compress.BufPushBuf(all, grpc.FrameMessageGzip(compress.BufFromStr("three three three"), true))
    println grpc.MessageCount(all), grpc.HasMessage(all, 0)
    mut pos := 0
    mut ok := false
    until grpc.HasMessage(all, pos):
        msg := grpc.NextMessage(all, pos, ok)
        println ok, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(msg)
    end

    mut md := grpc.NewMetadata()
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "authorization", "Bearer abc")
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "x-tag", "a")
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "x-tag", "b")
    _ := grpc.MDAddBinary(md, "trace-bin", "\x01\x02")
    println grpc.MDCount(md), grpc.MDHas(md, "x-tag"), grpc.MDGet(md, "authorization")
    println grpc.MDGetAll(md, "x-tag").len()
    println grpc.MDKeyAt(md, 3), grpc.MDValueAt(md, 3).len()
    mut headers := http2.HeaderList {}
    grpc.MDToHeaders(md, headers)
    println http2.HeadersCount(headers), http2.HeadersGet(headers, "trace-bin")
    println grpc.MDCount(grpc.MDFromHeaders(headers))

    bad := grpc.NewStatus(grpc.GRPC_NOT_FOUND, "there is no user 42")
    println grpc.StatusOk(bad), grpc.StatusString(bad)
    message := grpc.EncodeStatusMessage("100% done")
    println message, grpc.DecodeStatusMessage(message)
    println grpc.FormatStatusCode(14), grpc.ParseStatusCode("14"), grpc.ParseStatusCode("x")
    println grpc.StatusName(grpc.GRPC_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), grpc.StatusName(grpc.GRPC_UNAUTHENTICATED)
    println grpc.GRPC_CANCELLED, grpc.GRPC_UNKNOWN, grpc.GRPC_INVALID_ARGUMENT, grpc.GRPC_ALREADY_EXISTS
    println grpc.GRPC_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, grpc.GRPC_FAILED_PRECONDITION, grpc.GRPC_ABORTED, grpc.GRPC_OUT_OF_RANGE
    println grpc.GRPC_UNIMPLEMENTED, grpc.GRPC_INTERNAL, grpc.GRPC_UNAVAILABLE, grpc.GRPC_DATA_LOSS
    println grpc.GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE, grpc.GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE_PROTO, grpc.GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE_JSON
    println grpc.GRPC_COMP_NONE, grpc.GRPC_COMP_GZIP, grpc.GRPC_MAX_FRAMES, grpc.GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE
end
```

Output:

```text
10 0 5
3 true
true hello
true two
true three three three
4 true Bearer abc
2
trace-bin 2
4 AQI=
4
false NOT_FOUND: there is no user 42
100%25 done 100% done
14 14 2
DEADLINE_EXCEEDED UNAUTHENTICATED
1 2 3 6
8 9 10 11
12 13 14 15
application/grpc application/grpc+proto application/grpc+json
0 1 100000 4194304
```

### `Channel`

```salam
struct Channel
```

A channel to a gRPC server over HTTP/2.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conn` | `http2.Conn` | The HTTP/2 connection. |
| `authority` | `str = ""` | The host and port. |
| `scheme` | `str = "http"` | The scheme: http or https. |
| `user_agent` | `str = "salam-grpc/1.0"` | The client identifier. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int = 0` | The timeout of each call. |
| `use_gzip` | `bool = false` | Send the messages compressed. |
| `cursors` | `CursorTable` | The read position of each stream. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It is healthy. |
| `last_error` | `str = ""` | The last error. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: grpc-Calls.salam

```salam

```

A secure channel with TLS and ALPN h2.

grpc-TLS.salam

```salam
import grpc
import net.tcp

func echo(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, grpc.RecvStr(c, ok))
end

func main:
    mut ch := grpc.DialTLS("api.example.com", 443)
    if not grpc.ChannelOk(ch):
        println grpc.ChannelError(ch)
        ret
    end
    grpc.SetGzip(ch, true)
    mut result := grpc.Status {}
    println grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, "/demo.Echo/Say", "hello", result)
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)

    grpc.RegisterMethod("/demo.Echo/Say", echo)
    mut s := grpc.NewServer(50051)
    if grpc.Listen(s):
        grpc.Serve(s)
    end
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 50052)
    _ := grpc.ServeConn(conn.fd)
end
```

# db

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db/

One interface shared by the database engines, schema migrations and a connection pool.

Every database engine has its own package: db/sqlite, db/mysql, db/postgres, for key and value db/redis, and for search db/typesense, db/meilisearch, db/elasticsearch and, for search and analytics, db/opensearch; the last two also answer SQL queries through `Connection`. This package gives the `Connection` interface that the three SQL engines implement; write your code against it and changing engine is one line.

Migrations move the database schema along with the code: every change has a number and `MigrateUp` applies only the ones not applied yet. Never paste a value a user typed straight into SQL; send it through `QuoteLiteral` or as a prepared parameter.

## Types

### `Pool`

```salam
struct Pool
```

A pool of connections, for programs that need several at once.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conns` | `Vector` | The connections. |
| `taken` | `Vector` | Which connections are taken. |
| `limit` | `int = 0` | The greatest number of connections. |

db-Pool.salam

```salam
import db
import db.sqlite

func main:
    mut pool := db.NewPool(2)
    repeat 3:
        println db.Add(pool, sqlite.Conn(sqlite.Open(":memory:")))
    end
    println db.Size(pool), db.Idle(pool), db.InUse(pool)

    one := db.Acquire(pool)
    two := db.Acquire(pool)
    three := db.Acquire(pool)
    println db.Leased(one), db.Leased(three), three == db.NO_LEASE
    println db.Idle(pool), db.InUse(pool)

    c := db.Conn(pool, one)
    println db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT 6 * 7")
    db.Release(pool, one)
    db.Release(pool, two)
    println db.Idle(pool), db.DropDead(pool)
    db.CloseAll(pool)
    db.Free(pool)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true
false
2 2 0
true false true
0 2
42
2 0
```

### `Rows`

```salam
interface Rows
```

The interface of the rows of a query; its methods are `next`, `text`, `int`, `close` and the like.

db-Connection.salam

```salam
import db
import db.sqlite

func report(c: dyn db.Connection):
    println c.Kind(), c.Ok(), c.Ping()
    _ := c.Exec("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, score REAL)")
    _ := c.Exec("INSERT INTO users (name, score) VALUES (" + c.Quote("O'Brien") + ", 7.5)")
    _ := c.Exec("INSERT INTO users (name, score) VALUES ('Maryam', 9)")
    println c.LastInsertId(), c.Changes()

    rows := c.Query("SELECT id, name, score FROM users ORDER BY id")
    println rows.Ok(), rows.ColumnCount(), rows.ColumnName(1)
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Int(0), rows.Text(1), rows.Float(2), rows.Int64(0), rows.IsNull(2), rows.ColumnType(1)
    end
    _ := rows.Close()

    tx := c.Begin()
    println tx.Ok()
    _ := tx.Exec("UPDATE users SET score = 0")
    txrows := tx.Query("SELECT SUM(score) FROM users")
    _ := txrows.Next()
    println txrows.Float(0)
    _ := txrows.Close()
    _ := tx.Rollback()
    tx2 := c.Begin()
    _ := tx2.Exec("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 1")
    _ := tx2.Commit()

    println db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users"), db.QueryInt64(c, "SELECT MAX(id) FROM users")
    println db.QueryFloat(c, "SELECT score FROM users"), db.QueryText(c, "SELECT name FROM users")
    println db.CountRows(c, "SELECT * FROM users")
    println db.Run(c, "INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('Ali')"), db.Run(c, "INSERT INTO nowhere VALUES (1)")
    println c.Error()
    mut stmts := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    stmts.push("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('Sara')")
    stmts.push("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('Reza')")
    println db.RunAll(c, stmts)
    stmts.push("INSERT INTO nowhere VALUES (1)")
    println db.InTx(c, stmts), db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users")
    println db.QuoteLiteral("it's")
    _ := c.Close()
end

func main:
    report(sqlite.Conn(sqlite.Open(":memory:")))
    println db.SQLITE, db.MYSQL, db.POSTGRES
    println db.TYPE_NULL, db.TYPE_INT, db.TYPE_FLOAT, db.TYPE_TEXT, db.TYPE_BLOB
end
```

Output:

```text
sqlite true true
2 1
true 3 name
1 O'Brien 7.5 1 false 3
2 Maryam 9 2 false 3
true
0
1 2
9 Maryam
1
true false
no such table: nowhere
2
false 4
'it''s'
sqlite mysql postgres
0 1 2 3 4
```

### `Tx`

```salam

```

The transaction interface; its methods are `exec`, `query`, `commit` and `rollback`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-Connection.salam

### `Connection`

```salam
interface Connection
```

The interface shared by every engine. Code written against it runs unchanged on SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL; get one from the `Connect` of whichever engine.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-Connection.salam

### `Migration`

```salam
struct Migration
```

One migration: one numbered change to the database schema.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `int = 0` | The version number; migrations are applied in that order. |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `up` | `str = ""` | The SQL that applies it; separate several statements with `;`. |
| `down` | `str = ""` | The SQL that undoes it. |

db-Migrate.salam

```salam
import db
import db.sqlite

func main:
    c := sqlite.Conn(sqlite.Open(":memory:"))
    mut m := db.NewMigrator()
    db.AddMigration(m, 1, "users", "CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL)", "DROP TABLE users")
    db.AddMigration(m, 2, "posts", "CREATE TABLE posts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT); INSERT INTO posts (title) VALUES ('hello')", "DROP TABLE posts")
    db.AddMigration(m, 3, "tags", "ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN tag TEXT", "ALTER TABLE posts DROP COLUMN tag")
    println db.MigrationCount(m), db.SchemaVersion(m, c), db.PendingCount(m, c)

    println db.MigrateTo(m, c, 2)
    println db.SchemaVersion(m, c), db.IsApplied(m, c, 2), db.IsApplied(m, c, 3)
    println db.MigrateUp(m, c), db.SchemaVersion(m, c)
    println db.MigrateUp(m, c)
    println db.Rollback(m, c), db.SchemaVersion(m, c)
    println db.MigrateTo(m, c, 0), db.SchemaVersion(m, c)
    println db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM " + db.MIGRATION_TABLE)
    db.FreeMigrator(m)

    mut m2 := db.NewMigratorIn("app_versions")
    db.AddMigration(m2, 1, "t", "CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER)", "DROP TABLE t")
    println db.EnsureTable(m2, c), db.MigrateUp(m2, c), m2.table
    db.FreeMigrator(m2)

    parts := db.SplitStatements("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1); SELECT ';' ; ")
    println parts.len(), parts.get(1)
end
```

Output:

```text
3 0 3
2
2 true false
1 3
0
true 2
2 0
0
0 1 app_versions
2 SELECT ';'
```

# db/sqlite

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-sqlite/

An SQLite database in one file or in memory.

SQLite is a database that fits in one file and needs no server; for desktop programs, tools and a great many websites it is enough. The sqlite3 library has to be on the system to run it.

There are two ways to work: the functions of this package, such as `Query` and `Next`, which reach everything SQLite offers; or the database and row methods and `Conn`, which is the shared interface of db. Send user values through `Prepare` and the `Bind...` functions, not by pasting them into the SQL text.

## Types

### `Database`

```salam
struct Database
```

One open SQLite database.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The SQLite pointer. |

db-sqlite-Methods.salam

```salam
import db
import db.sqlite

func main:
    d := sqlite.Open(":memory:")
    println d.Kind(), d.Ok(), d.Ping()
    _ := d.Exec("CREATE TABLE notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT, stars REAL)")
    _ := d.Exec("INSERT INTO notes (body, stars) VALUES (" + d.Quote("the 'first' note") + ", 4.5)")
    println d.LastInsertId(), d.Changes()

    tx := d.Begin()
    _ := tx.Exec("INSERT INTO notes (body) VALUES ('second')")
    txrows := tx.Query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes")
    _ := txrows.Next()
    println txrows.Int(0)
    _ := txrows.Close()
    println tx.Ok(), tx.Commit()

    rows := d.Query("SELECT id, body, stars FROM notes ORDER BY id")
    println rows.Ok(), rows.ColumnCount(), rows.ColumnName(2)
    until rows.Next():
        mut stars := "-"
        if not rows.IsNull(2):
            stars = "" + rows.Float(2)
        end
        println rows.Int64(0), rows.Text(1), stars, rows.ColumnType(2)
    end
    _ := rows.Close()

    tx2 := d.Begin()
    _ := tx2.Exec("DELETE FROM notes")
    _ := tx2.Rollback()
    c := sqlite.Conn(d)
    println db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes")
    println d.Exec("DROP TABLE nope") != 0, d.Error()
    println d.Close()
end
```

Output:

```text
sqlite true true
1 1
2
true 0
true 3 stars
1 the 'first' note 4.5 2
2 second - 0
2
true no such table: nope
0
```

db-sqlite-Basics.salam

```salam
import db.sqlite

func main:
    println sqlite.Available(), sqlite.Version().len() > 0
    d := sqlite.Open(":memory:")
    println sqlite.Ok(d)
    _ := sqlite.Exec(d, "CREATE TABLE books (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, pages INTEGER, price REAL, note TEXT)")
    _ := sqlite.Exec(d, "INSERT INTO books (title, pages, price) VALUES ('The Little Prince', 96, 4.5)")
    println sqlite.LastInsertId(d), sqlite.Changes(d)

    stmt := sqlite.Prepare(d, "INSERT INTO books (title, pages, price, note) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)")
    println sqlite.StmtOk(stmt)
    _ := sqlite.BindText(stmt, 1, "The Blind Owl")
    _ := sqlite.BindInt(stmt, 2, 120)
    _ := sqlite.BindFloat(stmt, 3, 6.25)
    _ := sqlite.BindNull(stmt, 4)
    _ := sqlite.Next(stmt)
    _ := sqlite.Reset(stmt)
    _ := sqlite.BindText(stmt, 1, "Savushun")
    _ := sqlite.BindInt(stmt, 2, 304)
    _ := sqlite.BindFloat(stmt, 3, 9)
    _ := sqlite.BindText(stmt, 4, "classic")
    _ := sqlite.Next(stmt)
    _ := sqlite.Finish(stmt)
    println sqlite.TotalChanges(d)

    rows := sqlite.Query(d, "SELECT id, title, pages, price, note FROM books ORDER BY id")
    println sqlite.ColumnCount(rows), sqlite.ColumnName(rows, 1)
    until sqlite.Next(rows):
        mut note := "-"
        if not sqlite.IsNull(rows, 4):
            note = sqlite.Text(rows, 4)
        end
        println sqlite.Int(rows, 0), sqlite.Text(rows, 1), sqlite.Int64(rows, 2), sqlite.Float(rows, 3), note
    end
    _ := sqlite.Finish(rows)

    kinds := sqlite.Query(d, "SELECT pages, title, price, note FROM books WHERE id = 2")
    _ := sqlite.Next(kinds)
    println sqlite.ColumnType(kinds, 0), sqlite.ColumnType(kinds, 1), sqlite.ColumnType(kinds, 2), sqlite.ColumnType(kinds, 3)
    _ := sqlite.Finish(kinds)

    println sqlite.QueryInt(d, "SELECT SUM(pages) FROM books"), sqlite.QueryText(d, "SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1")

    _ := sqlite.Begin(d)
    _ := sqlite.Exec(d, "DELETE FROM books")
    _ := sqlite.Rollback(d)
    _ := sqlite.Begin(d)
    _ := sqlite.Exec(d, "UPDATE books SET price = price * 2")
    _ := sqlite.Commit(d)
    println sqlite.QueryInt(d, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books"), sqlite.QueryText(d, "SELECT price FROM books WHERE id = 1")

    println sqlite.Exec(d, "SELECT * FROM missing") != 0
    println sqlite.Error(d)
    _ := sqlite.Close(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true
1 1
true
3
5 title
1 The Little Prince 96 4.5 -
2 The Blind Owl 120 6.25 -
3 Savushun 304 9 classic
1 3 2 5
520 Savushun
3 9.0
true
no such table: missing
```

# db/mysql

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-mysql/

Connecting to MySQL and MariaDB.

This package implements the MySQL and MariaDB protocol directly and needs no outside library; when the server offers TLS the connection is encrypted. The example needs a running server, so it is checked and not run. For text outside ASCII, call `SetCharset` with `utf8mb4` once you are connected.

## Types

### `Database`

```salam
struct Database
```

One MySQL connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The pointer to the connection state. |

db-mysql-Client.salam

```salam
import db
import db.mysql

func main:
    if not mysql.Available():
        println "the MySQL client is not available"
        ret
    end
    _ := mysql.LibraryInit()
    _ := mysql.ThreadInit()
    println mysql.ClientVersion()
    d := mysql.Open("127.0.0.1", "app", "s3cret", "shop", 3306)
    if not mysql.Ok(d):
        println mysql.Errno(d), mysql.Error(d)
        ret
    end
    println mysql.ServerVersion(d), mysql.Ping(d)
    _ := mysql.SetCharset(d, "utf8mb4")
    _ := mysql.SelectDB(d, "shop")
    name := mysql.Escape(d, "O'Brien")
    _ := mysql.Exec(d, "INSERT INTO customers (name) VALUES ('" + name + "')")
    println mysql.LastInsertId(d), mysql.AffectedRows(d), mysql.Changes(d)

    _ := mysql.Autocommit(d, false)
    _ := mysql.Begin(d)
    _ := mysql.Exec(d, "UPDATE products SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE id = 7")
    if mysql.QueryInt(d, "SELECT stock FROM products WHERE id = 7") < 0:
        _ := mysql.Rollback(d)
    else:
        _ := mysql.Commit(d)
    end

    mut result := mysql.Query(d, "SELECT id, name, price, note FROM products")
    if mysql.QueryOk(result):
        println mysql.ColumnCount(result), mysql.RowCount(result), mysql.ColumnName(result, 1)
        until mysql.Next(result):
            println mysql.Int(result, 0), mysql.Text(result, 1), mysql.Float(result, 2), mysql.Int64(result, 0), mysql.IsNull(result, 3)
        end
        mysql.Finish(result)
    end
    println mysql.QueryText(d, "SELECT VERSION()")

    c := mysql.Conn(d)
    println c.Kind(), db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products")
    println d.Kind(), d.Ping(), d.Quote("x'y")
    rows := d.Query("SELECT name FROM customers")
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Text(0)
    end
    _ := rows.Close()
    mysql.Close(d)
    mysql.ThreadEnd()
    mysql.LibraryEnd()
    _ := mysql.OpenFull("localhost", "app", "s3cret", "shop", 0, "/tmp/mysql.sock", 0 as u64)
end
```

# db/postgres

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-postgres/

Connecting to PostgreSQL.

This package implements the Postgres protocol directly and needs no outside library; the example needs a running Postgres server, so it is checked and not run. Every row of a result is fetched from the server at once, so `RowCount` is known before you read any of them.

## Types

### `Database`

```salam
struct Database
```

One PostgreSQL connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The library pointer. |
| `affected` | `i64 = 0` | The number of rows changed by the last statement. |

db-postgres-Client.salam

```salam
import db
import db.postgres

func main:
    if not postgres.Available():
        println "the Postgres client is not available"
        ret
    end
    println postgres.ClientVersion()
    d := postgres.Open("host=127.0.0.1 port=5432 dbname=shop user=app password=s3cret")
    if not postgres.Ok(d):
        println postgres.Error(d)
        ret
    end
    println postgres.ServerVersion(d), postgres.DatabaseName(d), postgres.UserName(d), postgres.HostName(d), postgres.Port(d)
    println postgres.Ping(d)
    _ := postgres.Exec(d, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price NUMERIC)")
    _ := postgres.Exec(d, "INSERT INTO items (name, price) VALUES (" + postgres.Quote(d, "tea") + ", 12.5)")
    println postgres.ExecCount(d, "UPDATE items SET price = price * 1.1")

    rows := postgres.Query(d, "SELECT id, name, price FROM items ORDER BY id")
    println rows.Ok(), rows.ColumnCount(), rows.RowCount(), rows.ColumnName(1)
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Int(0), rows.Text(1), rows.Float(2), rows.Int64(0), rows.IsNull(2), rows.ColumnType(1)
    end
    _ := rows.Close()
    println postgres.QueryInt(d, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM items"), postgres.QueryText(d, "SELECT version()")

    c := postgres.Conn(d)
    tx := c.Begin()
    _ := tx.Exec("DELETE FROM items")
    _ := tx.Rollback()
    println db.QueryInt(c, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM items"), d.Kind()
    postgres.Reset(d)
    _ := postgres.Close(d)
    _ := postgres.OpenFull("db.example.com", 5432, "app", "s3cret", "shop")
end
```

# db/redis

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-redis/

A Redis client: keys and values, hashes, lists, sets and publishing.

Redis is an in memory database for caches, sessions, counters and queues. This package implements the Redis protocol directly and with no outside library; the example needs a running Redis server, so it is only checked. For a command with no function of its own, call `Command` with the command name and its arguments.

## Types

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

A connection to Redis.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The connection pointer. |

db-redis-Client.salam

```salam
import db.redis

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    if not redis.Ok(c):
        println redis.Error(c)
        ret
    end
    _ := redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")
    _ := redis.Select(c, 1)
    println redis.Ping(c)

    _ := redis.Set(c, "greeting", "hello")
    _ := redis.SetEx(c, "session:42", "token", 3600)
    println redis.Get(c, "greeting"), redis.Exists(c, "greeting"), redis.TTL(c, "session:42")
    println redis.Incr(c, "visits"), redis.IncrBy(c, "visits", 10), redis.Decr(c, "visits")
    println redis.Append(c, "greeting", "!"), redis.StrLen(c, "greeting"), redis.Type(c, "greeting")
    _ := redis.Expire(c, "greeting", 60)
    println redis.Keys(c, "session:*").len()
    _ := redis.Del(c, "greeting")

    _ := redis.HSet(c, "user:1", "name", "Maryam")
    _ := redis.HSet(c, "user:1", "city", "Tehran")
    println redis.HGet(c, "user:1", "name"), redis.HExists(c, "user:1", "age"), redis.HLen(c, "user:1")
    all := redis.HGetAll(c, "user:1")
    println all.size()
    _ := redis.HDel(c, "user:1", "city")

    _ := redis.RPush(c, "jobs", "a")
    _ := redis.LPush(c, "jobs", "b")
    println redis.LLen(c, "jobs"), redis.LRange(c, "jobs", 0, -1).len()
    println redis.LPop(c, "jobs"), redis.RPop(c, "jobs")

    _ := redis.SAdd(c, "tags", "go")
    _ := redis.SAdd(c, "tags", "salam")
    println redis.SIsMember(c, "tags", "salam"), redis.SCard(c, "tags"), redis.SMembers(c, "tags").len()
    _ := redis.SRem(c, "tags", "go")
    println redis.Publish(c, "news", "fresh news")

    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    args.push("GET")
    args.push("visits")
    r := redis.Command(c, args)
    if redis.ReplyOk(r) and not redis.ReplyIsError(r) and not redis.ReplyIsNil(r):
        println redis.ReplyType(r) == redis.REPLY_STRING, redis.ReplyStr(r)
    end
    redis.FreeReply(r)
    mut args2 := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    args2.push("LRANGE")
    args2.push("jobs")
    args2.push("0")
    args2.push("-1")
    r2 := redis.Command(c, args2)
    if redis.ReplyType(r2) == redis.REPLY_ARRAY:
        repeat redis.ReplyArrayLen(r2) in i:
            println redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(r2, i))
        end
    end
    println redis.ReplyInt(r2), redis.REPLY_INTEGER, redis.REPLY_NIL, redis.REPLY_STATUS, redis.REPLY_ERROR, redis.REPLY_DOUBLE
    redis.FreeReply(r2)
    _ := redis.FlushDB(c)
    redis.Close(c)
end
```

### `Reply`

```salam
struct Reply
```

# db/typesense

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-typesense/

A Typesense client: collections, documents, typo tolerant, faceted, grouped, vector and union search, synonyms, curation, API keys, analytics and clusters.

Typesense is an open source search engine with typo tolerance, filters, facets, grouping, vector and hybrid search. This package speaks its HTTP API directly with `net.httpx` and covers all of it: collections and their fields, documents one at a time or in bulk JSONL imports and exports, every search parameter, multi search and union search, synonym sets and curation sets, presets, stopwords, stemming dictionaries, API keys and scoped search keys signed with no request, analytics rules and events, conversation (RAG) models, natural language search models and the cluster operations. The examples need a running server, so they are only checked.

Every call takes an `Error` as its last argument and fills it when something fails; check it with `Ok`, or with `IsNotFound` and `IsConflict` for the two answers code usually handles. A client can hold several nodes: a node that does not answer, or answers with a 5xx, is skipped for `healthcheck_ms` and the request moves to the next one, the same way the official clients behave. Documents and hits come back as raw JSON text; read them into your own structs with `GetDocumentAs` and `HitsAs`, and send your structs with `ImportOf` and `CreateDocumentOf`. Typesense 30 replaced per collection synonyms and overrides with synonym sets and curation sets; both kinds are here, so the package works with 29 and 30 servers alike. For a route with no function of its own, use `Request`.

New to Typesense? The Search with Typesense lesson builds a small catalog step by step, with the output of every example.

## Types

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

A connection to a Typesense server or cluster. Build it with `New` or `NewCluster` and release it with `Free`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `Vector` | The node URLs, such as `http://localhost:8108`; a path after the host is kept as a prefix. |
| `nearest` | `str = ""` | A node to try before the others, such as the one in the same region; empty for none. |
| `api_key` | `str = ""` | The key sent in the `X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY` header. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int = 10000` | How long one request may take, in milliseconds; 0 waits forever. |
| `retries` | `int = 3` | How many more times to try after a node fails. |
| `retry_interval_ms` | `int = 100` | The pause between two tries, in milliseconds. |
| `healthcheck_ms` | `int = 60000` | How long a node that failed is skipped, in milliseconds. |
| `headers` | `Vector` | Extra header lines added with `AddHeader`. |
| `state` | `Vector` | Internal: the round robin position and when each node may be tried again. |

db-typesense-Client.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    mut nodes := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    nodes.push("http://ts-1:8108")
    nodes.push("http://ts-2:8108")
    nodes.push("http://ts-3:8108")
    mut c := typesense.NewCluster(nodes, "admin-key")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    typesense.SetNearestNode(c, "http://ts-local:8108")
    typesense.AddNode(c, "http://ts-4:8108")
    typesense.AddHeader(c, "X-Request-Source", "salam")
    c.timeout_ms = 5000
    c.retries = 2
    c.retry_interval_ms = 200
    c.healthcheck_ms = 30000

    mut err := typesense.Error {}
    if not typesense.Health(c, err):
        println "not ready: " + typesense.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println typesense.IsHealthy(c), typesense.NodeHealthy(c, 0), typesense.NodeHealthy(c, -1)
    println "server", typesense.ServerVersion(c, err), typesense.Debug(c, err)
    st := typesense.Status(c, err)
    println st.state, st.committed_index, st.queued_writes
    println typesense.Stats(c, err)
    println typesense.Metrics(c, err)
    println typesense.CreateSnapshot(c, "/data/snapshots/today", err)
    println typesense.Vote(c, err), typesense.ClearCache(c, err), typesense.CompactDB(c, err), typesense.ResetPeers(c, err)
    println typesense.SchemaChanges(c, err).len()
    println typesense.SetSlowRequestLog(c, 1000, err), typesense.UpdateConfig(c, `{"healthy-read-lag": 1000}`, err)

    body := typesense.Request(c, "GET", "/collections?limit=1", "", err)
    if not typesense.Ok(err):
        println err.status, err.kind, err.message
        println err.kind == typesense.KIND_HTTP, err.kind == typesense.KIND_NETWORK, err.kind == typesense.KIND_INVALID, err.kind == typesense.KIND_DECODE
        println typesense.IsNotFound(err), typesense.IsConflict(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println body
    println typesense.RequestAs(c, "POST", "/stemming/dictionaries/import?id=plurals", "text/plain", `{"word":"mice","root":"mouse"}`, err)
    println typesense.VERSION, c.nodes.len(), c.nearest, c.api_key.len(), c.headers.len(), c.state.len()
    single := typesense.New("localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    println single.nodes.get(0)
end
```

### `Error`

```salam
struct Error
```

What went wrong in the last call. Empty when the call worked.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status, or 0 when there was no answer. |
| `kind` | `str = ""` | One of the `KIND_` constants, or empty when the call worked. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message from the server, or a description of the failure. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-Client.salam

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-Client.salam

### `AnalyticsRule`

```salam
struct AnalyticsRule
```

An analytics rule, in the Typesense 30 form.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | Its name. |
| `kind` | `str = ""` | One of the `RULE_` constants. |
| `collection` | `str = ""` | The collection whose events it collects. |
| `event_type` | `str = ""` | One of the `EVENT_` constants. |
| `rule_tag` | `str = ""` | A tag to list rules by. |
| `params` | `str = ""` | The rule parameters, as JSON, such as `{"destination_collection":"pq","limit":100}`. |
| `raw` | `str = ""` | The whole rule, as JSON; the only place a Typesense 29 rule keeps its source and destination. |

db-typesense-CreateAnalyticsRule.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    popular := typesense.AnalyticsRule {
        name = "popular-searches", kind = typesense.RULE_POPULAR_QUERIES, collection = "books", event_type = typesense.EVENT_SEARCH,
        params = `{"destination_collection": "popular_queries", "limit": 1000}`
    }
    println typesense.AnalyticsRuleJSON(popular)
    made := typesense.CreateAnalyticsRule(c, popular, err)
    println made.name, made.kind, made.collection, made.event_type, made.params

    clicks := typesense.AnalyticsRule {
        name = "book-clicks", kind = typesense.RULE_COUNTER, collection = "books", event_type = typesense.EVENT_CLICK,
        rule_tag = "homepage", params = `{"destination_collection": "books", "counter_field": "popularity", "weight": 1}`
    }
    println typesense.UpsertAnalyticsRule(c, clicks, err).rule_tag
    println typesense.CreateAnalyticsRuleJSON(c, `{"name": "no-results", "type": "nohits_queries", "collection": "books", "event_type": "search", "params": {"destination_collection": "nohits", "limit": 100}}`, err)
    println typesense.UpsertAnalyticsRuleJSON(c, "old-style", `{"type": "popular_queries", "params": {"source": {"collections": ["books"]}, "destination": {"collection": "pq"}}}`, err)
    println typesense.GetAnalyticsRule(c, "book-clicks", err).raw
    each r in typesense.ListAnalyticsRules(c, "homepage", err):
        println r.name, r.kind
    end

    println typesense.SendEvent(c, "book-clicks", typesense.EVENT_CLICK, `{"doc_id": "42", "user_id": "u-7"}`, err)
    println typesense.SendEventJSON(c, `{"name": "book-clicks", "event_type": "click", "data": {"doc_id": "43", "user_id": "u-7"}}`, err)
    each e in typesense.GetEvents(c, "u-7", "book-clicks", 20, err):
        println e
    end
    println typesense.FlushAnalytics(c, err), typesense.AnalyticsStatus(c, err)
    println typesense.DeleteAnalyticsRule(c, "no-results", err)
    println typesense.RULE_LOG, typesense.EVENT_CONVERSION, typesense.EVENT_VISIT, typesense.EVENT_CUSTOM

    m := typesense.ConversationModel {
        id = "books-assistant", model_name = "openai/gpt-4o-mini", api_key = "sk-...", history_collection = "conversations",
        system_prompt = "You recommend books from our catalog.", max_bytes = 16384, ttl = 86400, account_id = "", vllm_url = "", extra = ""
    }
    println typesense.ConversationModelJSON(m)
    println typesense.CreateConversationModel(c, m, err)
    println typesense.GetConversationModel(c, "books-assistant", err)
    println typesense.ListConversationModels(c, err).len()
    println typesense.UpdateConversationModel(c, "books-assistant", typesense.ConversationModel { system_prompt = "Answer in one sentence." }, err)
    println typesense.DeleteConversationModel(c, "books-assistant", err)

    println typesense.CreateNLSearchModel(c, `{"id": "gpt-4o-nl", "model_name": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", "api_key": "sk-...", "max_bytes": 16000}`, err)
    println typesense.GetNLSearchModel(c, "gpt-4o-nl", err)
    println typesense.ListNLSearchModels(c, err).len()
    println typesense.UpdateNLSearchModel(c, "gpt-4o-nl", `{"temperature": 0.0}`, err)
    println typesense.DeleteNLSearchModel(c, "gpt-4o-nl", err)
end
```

### `ConversationModel`

```salam
struct ConversationModel
```

A large language model for conversational search (RAG). Only the values you set are sent.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str = ""` | Its id. |
| `model_name` | `str = ""` | The model, such as `openai/gpt-4o`. |
| `api_key` | `str = ""` | The key for the model provider. |
| `history_collection` | `str = ""` | The collection that keeps conversation history. |
| `system_prompt` | `str = ""` | The instructions given to the model. |
| `max_bytes` | `int = 0` | How much context the model receives. |
| `ttl` | `int = 0` | How long a conversation is kept, in seconds. |
| `account_id` | `str = ""` | The account id, for Cloudflare models. |
| `vllm_url` | `str = ""` | The server URL, for vLLM models. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | More members as a JSON object. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-CreateAnalyticsRule.salam

### `SearchParams`

```salam
struct SearchParams
```

The parameters of one search. Zero values and empty strings are left out; anything else goes through `Set`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | `str = ""` | The text to search for; `*` matches every document. |
| `query_by` | `str = ""` | The fields to search, comma separated. |
| `query_by_weights` | `str = ""` | The weight of each field in `query_by`, such as `2,1`. |
| `text_match_type` | `str = ""` | How field scores combine: `max_score`, `max_weight` or `sum_score`. |
| `prefix` | `str = ""` | Whether the last word matches as a prefix, one value per field such as `true,false`. |
| `infix` | `str = ""` | Infix search per field: `off`, `always` or `fallback`. |
| `filter_by` | `str = ""` | A filter, such as `year:>2000 && genre:=[scifi]`. |
| `sort_by` | `str = ""` | The sort order, such as `year:desc,_text_match:desc`. |
| `facet_by` | `str = ""` | Fields to count values of. |
| `facet_query` | `str = ""` | Narrow the facet values, such as `genre:sci`. |
| `max_facet_values` | `int = 0` | How many values each facet returns. |
| `group_by` | `str = ""` | Group the results by these fields. |
| `group_limit` | `int = 0` | How many hits each group returns. |
| `include_fields` | `str = ""` | Return only these fields. |
| `exclude_fields` | `str = ""` | Leave these fields out of the results. |
| `highlight_fields` | `str = ""` | Highlight only these fields. |
| `highlight_full_fields` | `str = ""` | Highlight the whole value of these fields, not a snippet. |
| `highlight_start_tag` | `str = ""` | The tag before a match; `<mark>` by default. |
| `highlight_end_tag` | `str = ""` | The tag after a match. |
| `snippet_threshold` | `int = 0` | Fields shorter than this many words are highlighted whole. |
| `num_typos` | `str = ""` | How many typos a word may have, 0 to 2, one value per field. |
| `typo_tokens_threshold` | `int = 0` | Look for typo matches only when fewer results than this were found. |
| `drop_tokens_threshold` | `int = 0` | Drop words from the query only when fewer results than this were found. |
| `page` | `int = 0` | The page, from 1. |
| `per_page` | `int = 0` | Hits per page, up to 250. |
| `offset` | `int = 0` | Skip this many hits; an alternative to `page`. |
| `limit` | `int = 0` | Return this many hits; used with `offset`. |
| `pinned_hits` | `str = ""` | Pin documents to positions, such as `12:1,3:2`. |
| `hidden_hits` | `str = ""` | Ids of documents to hide. |
| `override_tags` | `str = ""` | Apply only the curation rules with these tags. |
| `preset` | `str = ""` | Use the parameters saved in this preset. |
| `vector_query` | `str = ""` | A nearest neighbour search, such as `embedding:([0.1, 0.2], k: 10)`. |
| `stopwords` | `str = ""` | A stopword set to apply. |
| `exhaustive_search` | `bool = false` | Consider every variation of the query, slower but complete. |
| `search_cutoff_ms` | `int = 0` | Stop searching after this many milliseconds and return what was found. |
| `use_cache` | `bool = false` | Cache the results on the server. |
| `cache_ttl` | `int = 0` | How long to cache them, in seconds. |
| `conversation` | `bool = false` | Answer the query with a conversation model (RAG). |
| `conversation_id` | `str = ""` | Continue this conversation. |
| `conversation_model_id` | `str = ""` | The conversation model to use. |
| `nl_query` | `bool = false` | Turn a natural language query into filters and sorting with an NL search model. |
| `nl_model_id` | `str = ""` | The NL search model to use. |
| `keys` | `Vector` | Parameter names added with `Set`. |
| `values` | `Vector` | Their values. |

db-typesense-Search.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import str
import db.typesense

struct Book:
    pub id: str = ""
    pub title: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
end

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "search-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut p := typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title,description")
    p.query_by_weights = "3,1"
    p.filter_by = "year:>1950 && genres:=[scifi]"
    p.sort_by = "_text_match:desc,year:desc"
    p.facet_by = "genres,year"
    p.max_facet_values = 10
    p.per_page = 20
    p.page = 1
    p.num_typos = "2,1"
    p.highlight_start_tag = "<b>"
    p.highlight_end_tag = "</b>"
    typesense.Set(p, "prioritize_exact_match", "false")
    println typesense.SearchQuery(p)
    println typesense.SearchParamsJSON(p)

    r := typesense.Search(c, "books", p, err)
    if not typesense.Ok(err):
        println typesense.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println r.found, r.out_of, r.page, r.search_time_ms, r.search_cutoff
    each h in r.hits:
        println h.document, h.text_match, h.curated, typesense.Highlight(h, "title")
        println h.highlight, h.highlights, h.text_match_info, h.vector_distance, h.geo_distance_meters, h.hybrid_search_info, h.raw.len()
    end
    each f in r.facets:
        print f.field_name, f.sampled, f.stats, ":"
        each fc in f.counts:
            print " " + fc.value + "=" + fc.count + " " + fc.highlighted
        end
        println ""
    end
    mut books := Vector {} as Vector<Book>
    if typesense.HitsAs(r, books, err):
        println books.len()
    end
    println r.request_params, r.raw.len()

    mut g := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    g.group_by = "genres"
    g.group_limit = 3
    g.include_fields = "id,title"
    rg := typesense.Search(c, "books", g, err)
    println rg.found, rg.found_docs
    each grp in rg.groups:
        println str.Join(grp.key, ","), grp.found, grp.hits.len()
    end

    mut v := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    v.vector_query = "embedding:([0.12, 0.45, 0.87], k: 10)"
    v.exclude_fields = "embedding"
    println typesense.SearchRaw(c, "books", v, err)

    mut rag := typesense.NewSearch("which books are about deserts?", "title_vector")
    rag.conversation = true
    rag.conversation_model_id = "books-assistant"
    rag.conversation_id = ""
    rag.prefix = "false"
    rag.exhaustive_search = true
    rag.search_cutoff_ms = 200
    rag.use_cache = true
    rag.cache_ttl = 60
    println typesense.Search(c, "books", rag, err).conversation

    mut nl := typesense.NewSearch("science fiction books after 1960 sorted by year", "title")
    nl.nl_query = true
    nl.nl_model_id = "gpt-4o-nl"
    println typesense.Search(c, "books", nl, err).parsed_nl_query

    mut reqs := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.SearchRequest>
    reqs.push(typesense.SearchRequest { collection = "books", params = typesense.NewSearch("dune", "") })
    reqs.push(typesense.SearchRequest { collection = "authors", params = typesense.NewSearch("herbert", "name"), api_key = "scoped-key" })
    common := typesense.NewSearch("", "title")
    each m in typesense.MultiSearch(c, reqs, common, err):
        println m.found, m.code, m.error
    end
    println typesense.MultiSearchRaw(c, reqs, common, err).len()
    u := typesense.UnionSearch(c, reqs, common, err)
    each h in u.hits:
        println h.collection, h.search_index, h.document
    end
    mut rr := typesense.ParseSearchResult(`{"found": 0, "hits": []}`)
    println rr.found, rr.code, rr.error, typesense.MAX_GET_QUERY
    typesense.FreeResult(rr)
end
```

### `KeySpec`

```salam

```

A new API key.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `str = ""` | What the key is for. |
