db-typesense-CreateKey.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut books := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    books.push("books")
    search := typesense.SearchOnlyKey(c, "website search", books, err)
    println search.id, search.value, search.actions.len(), search.collections.get(0)

    mut actions := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    actions.push("documents:*")
    actions.push("collections:get")
    mut orgs := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    orgs.push("org_.*")
    spec := typesense.KeySpec { description = "tenant writer", actions = actions, collections = orgs, expires_at = 1924992000, autodelete = true }
    println typesense.KeySpecJSON(spec)
    k := typesense.CreateKey(c, spec, err)
    println k.value, k.expires_at, k.autodelete

    mut all := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    all.push(typesense.KEY_ACTION_ALL)
    admin := typesense.CreateKey(c, typesense.KeySpec { description = "admin", actions = all, collections = all, value = "my-chosen-admin-key" }, err)
    println admin.id

    g := typesense.GetKey(c, k.id, err)
    println g.value_prefix, g.description
    each key in typesense.ListKeys(c, err):
        println key.id, key.value_prefix, key.description, key.actions.len(), key.collections.len(), key.expires_at
    end
    println typesense.DeleteKey(c, k.id, err)

    scope := typesense.SearchParams { filter_by = "company_id:=124", exclude_fields = "salary" }
    scoped := typesense.ScopedSearchKey(search.value, scope, 1924992000)
    println scoped
    println typesense.GenerateScopedSearchKey(search.value, `{"filter_by":"user_id:=42"}`)
    mut browser := typesense.New("https://search.example.com", scoped)
    defer typesense.Free(browser)
    println typesense.Search(browser, "books", typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title"), err).found
    println typesense.KEY_ACTION_SEARCH
end
```

### `Field`

```salam
struct Field
```

One field of a collection schema. Only the values you change are sent.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The field name, or a regular expression such as `.*_facet`. |
| `kind` | `str = ""` | Its type, one of the `TYPE_` constants. |
| `facet` | `bool = false` | Count its values for facets and allow exact filters. |
| `optional` | `bool = false` | Documents may leave it out. |
| `index` | `bool = true` | Index it for search and filters; false keeps it stored only. |
| `store` | `bool = true` | Keep it on disk; false indexes it without storing it. |
| `sort` | `int = 0` | 1 makes it sortable, -1 makes it not sortable, 0 keeps the default (numbers sort, text does not). |
| `infix` | `bool = false` | Allow matches in the middle of words. |
| `locale` | `str = ""` | The language of the text, such as `fa` or `en`. |
| `stem` | `bool = false` | Match words by their root. |
| `stem_dictionary` | `str = ""` | A custom stemming dictionary to use. |
| `range_index` | `bool = false` | Index it for fast range filters. |
| `reference` | `str = ""` | Join to another collection, as `collection.field`. |
| `async_reference` | `bool = false` | Accept a reference to a document that does not exist yet. |
| `num_dim` | `int = 0` | The size of the vector, for a `float[]` vector field. |
| `vec_dist` | `str = ""` | The vector distance, `cosine` or `ip`. |
| `embed` | `str = ""` | How to make the vector automatically, as JSON; see `EmbeddingField`. |
| `token_separators` | `Vector` | Extra characters that split words in this field. |
| `symbols_to_index` | `Vector` | Special characters to keep in this field. |
| `truncate_len` | `int = 0` | How many characters of a long string to index. |
| `drop` | `bool = false` | Removes the field in `UpdateCollection`; used by `DropFields`. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | More members as a JSON object, such as `{"hnsw_params":{"M":16}}`. |

db-typesense-CreateCollection.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut s := typesense.Schema { name = "books_v2", default_sorting_field = "year", enable_nested_fields = true }
    s.fields.push(typesense.NewField("title", typesense.TYPE_STRING))
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "title_fa", kind = typesense.TYPE_STRING, locale = "fa", stem = true, optional = true })
    s.fields.push(typesense.FacetField("year", typesense.TYPE_INT32))
    s.fields.push(typesense.FacetField("genres", typesense.TYPE_STRING_ARRAY))
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "price", kind = typesense.TYPE_FLOAT, range_index = true })
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "isbn", kind = typesense.TYPE_STRING, index = false, optional = true })
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "author_id", kind = typesense.TYPE_STRING, reference = "authors.id" })
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "location", kind = typesense.TYPE_GEOPOINT, optional = true })
    s.fields.push(typesense.VectorField("embedding", 384))
    mut from := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    from.push("title")
    s.fields.push(typesense.EmbeddingField("title_vector", from, "ts/all-MiniLM-L12-v2"))
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "meta.*", kind = typesense.TYPE_AUTO, optional = true })
    s.symbols_to_index.push("+")
    s.token_separators.push("-")
    s.metadata = `{"owner": "catalog"}`
    println typesense.SchemaJSON(s)

    col := typesense.CreateCollection(c, s, err)
    if typesense.IsConflict(err):
        println "books_v2 already exists"
    end
    println col.name, col.num_documents, col.created_at, col.fields.len()
    each f in col.fields:
        println f.name, f.kind, f.facet, f.optional, f.sort, f.index, f.store
    end

    if typesense.CollectionExists(c, "books_v2", err):
        println typesense.GetCollection(c, "books_v2", err).default_sorting_field
    end
    each x in typesense.ListCollections(c, err):
        println x.name, x.num_documents
    end
    mut skip := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    skip.push("fields")
    println typesense.ListCollectionsPage(c, 0, 20, skip, err).len()

    mut add := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.Field>
    add.push(typesense.FacetField("publisher", typesense.TYPE_STRING))
    println typesense.AddFields(c, "books_v2", add, err)
    mut drop := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    drop.push("isbn")
    println typesense.DropFields(c, "books_v2", drop, err)
    println typesense.SetCollectionMetadata(c, "books_v2", `{"owner": "search team"}`, err)
    println typesense.UpdateCollection(c, "books_v2", `{"synonym_sets": ["book-words"]}`, err)

    a := typesense.UpsertAlias(c, "books", "books_v2", err)
    println a.name, a.collection_name
    println typesense.GetAlias(c, "books", err).collection_name
    each al in typesense.ListAliases(c, err):
        println al.name, "->", al.collection_name
    end
    println typesense.CloneCollection(c, "books_v2", "books_v3", err).name
    println typesense.TruncateCollection(c, "books_v3", err)
    println typesense.DeleteCollection(c, "books_v3", err).name
    println typesense.DeleteAlias(c, "old_books", err).name
    println typesense.CreateCollectionJSON(c, `{"name": "authors", "fields": [{"name": "name", "type": "string"}]}`, err).name
    println typesense.FieldJSON(typesense.NewField("pages", typesense.TYPE_INT32))
    println typesense.TYPE_STRING_ANY, typesense.TYPE_INT32_ARRAY, typesense.TYPE_INT64, typesense.TYPE_INT64_ARRAY, typesense.TYPE_FLOAT_ARRAY
    println typesense.TYPE_BOOL, typesense.TYPE_BOOL_ARRAY, typesense.TYPE_GEOPOINT_ARRAY, typesense.TYPE_GEOPOLYGON
    println typesense.TYPE_OBJECT, typesense.TYPE_OBJECT_ARRAY, typesense.TYPE_IMAGE
end
```

### `Synonym`

```salam
struct Synonym
```

A synonym: words that should find each other.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str = ""` | Its id. |
| `synonyms` | `Vector` | The words. Without a root they all mean the same thing. |
| `root` | `str = ""` | When set, a search for the root also finds the other words, but not the other way round. |
| `locale` | `str = ""` | The language of the words, such as `fa`. |
| `symbols_to_index` | `Vector` | Special characters the words contain that should be kept. |

db-typesense-UpsertSynonymSet.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut words := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    words.push("book")
    words.push("novel")
    words.push("کتاب")
    mut items := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.Synonym>
    items.push(typesense.Synonym { id = "books", synonyms = words })
    set := typesense.UpsertSynonymSet(c, "book-words", items, err)
    println set.name, set.items.len()
    mut one := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    one.push("paperback")
    s := typesense.Synonym { id = "paper", root = "book", synonyms = one, locale = "en", symbols_to_index = Vector {} as Vector<str> }
    println typesense.SynonymJSON(s)
    println typesense.UpsertSynonymItem(c, "book-words", s, err).root
    println typesense.GetSynonymItem(c, "book-words", "paper", err).synonyms.len()
    println typesense.ListSynonymItems(c, "book-words", err).len(), typesense.GetSynonymSet(c, "book-words", err).items.len(), typesense.ListSynonymSets(c, err).len()
    println typesense.DeleteSynonymItem(c, "book-words", "paper", err)

    println typesense.UpsertSynonym(c, "books", s, err).id
    println typesense.GetSynonym(c, "books", "paper", err).root, typesense.ListSynonyms(c, "books", err).len()
    println typesense.DeleteSynonym(c, "books", "paper", err)

    mut pins := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.Pin>
    pins.push(typesense.Pin { id = "42", position = 1 })
    mut hide := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    hide.push("13")
    mut tags := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    tags.push("summer-sale")
    rule := typesense.CurationRule {
        id = "promote-dune", query = "dune", match_type = typesense.MATCH_EXACT, includes = pins, excludes = hide,
        filter_curated_hits = true, effective_from_ts = 1924992000, metadata = `{"campaign": "summer"}`
    }
    println typesense.CurationJSON(rule)
    mut rules := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.CurationRule>
    rules.push(rule)
    rules.push(typesense.CurationRule {
        id = "sale", tags = tags, rule_filter_by = "on_sale:=true", filter_by = "stock:>0", sort_by = "price:asc",
        match_type = typesense.MATCH_CONTAINS, replace_query = "", remove_matched_tokens = true, stop_processing = false,
        effective_to_ts = 1956528000, extra = ""
    })
    cs := typesense.UpsertCurationSet(c, "promotions", rules, err)
    println cs.name, cs.items.len()
    println typesense.UpsertCurationItem(c, "promotions", rule, err).id
    println typesense.GetCurationItem(c, "promotions", "sale", err).sort_by, typesense.ListCurationItems(c, "promotions", err).len()
    println typesense.GetCurationSet(c, "promotions", err).items.len(), typesense.ListCurationSets(c, err).len()
    println typesense.DeleteCurationItem(c, "promotions", "sale", err)
    println typesense.UpdateCollection(c, "books", `{"synonym_sets": ["book-words"], "curation_sets": ["promotions"]}`, err)

    println typesense.UpsertOverride(c, "books", rule, err).id
    println typesense.GetOverride(c, "books", "promote-dune", err).query, typesense.ListOverrides(c, "books", err).len()
    println typesense.DeleteOverride(c, "books", "promote-dune", err)

    mut listing := typesense.NewSearch("", "title,description")
    listing.per_page = 24
    listing.sort_by = "popularity:desc"
    pr := typesense.UpsertSearchPreset(c, "listing", listing, err)
    println pr.name, pr.value
    println typesense.UpsertPreset(c, "listing-raw", `{"query_by": "title"}`, err).value
    println typesense.GetPreset(c, "listing", err).value
    each x in typesense.ListPresets(c, err):
        println x.name
    end
    println typesense.DeletePreset(c, "listing-raw", err)

    mut sw := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    sw.push("the")
    sw.push("a")
    st := typesense.UpsertStopwords(c, "english", sw, "en", err)
    println st.id, st.locale, st.stopwords.len()
    println typesense.GetStopwords(c, "english", err).stopwords.len(), typesense.ListStopwords(c, err).len()
    println typesense.DeleteStopwords(c, "english", err)

    mut stem := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.StemWord>
    stem.push(typesense.StemWord { word = "mice", root = "mouse" })
    stem.push(typesense.StemWord { word = "geese", root = "goose" })
    println typesense.ImportStemmingDictionary(c, "irregular", stem, err)
    println typesense.ImportStemmingJSONL(c, "irregular", `{"word": "teeth", "root": "tooth"}`, err)
    d := typesense.GetStemmingDictionary(c, "irregular", err)
    println d.id, d.words.len()
    println typesense.ListStemmingDictionaries(c, err).len()
    println typesense.DeleteStemmingDictionary(c, "irregular", err)
    println typesense.DeleteCurationSet(c, "promotions", err), typesense.DeleteSynonymSet(c, "book-words", err)
end
```

struct SynonymSet

| `items` | `Vector` | The synonyms. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-UpsertSynonymSet.salam

struct Pin

A document pinned to a position in the results.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str = ""` | The document id. |
| `position` | `int = 0` | The position, from 1. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-UpsertSynonymSet.salam

### `CurationRule`

```salam
struct CurationRule
```

A curation rule (called an override before Typesense 30): when a query matches, pin, hide, filter or sort the results.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str = ""` | Its id. |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query text it matches. |
| `match_type` | `str = ""` | `MATCH_EXACT` or `MATCH_CONTAINS`. |
| `rule_filter_by` | `str = ""` | Apply the rule when the search uses this filter. |
| `tags` | `Vector` | Apply the rule when the search sends one of these tags in `override_tags`. |
| `includes` | `Vector` | Documents to pin. |
| `excludes` | `Vector` | Ids of documents to hide. |
| `filter_by` | `str = ""` | A filter to add to the search. |
| `sort_by` | `str = ""` | A sort order to use instead. |
| `replace_query` | `str = ""` | A query to search for instead. |
| `remove_matched_tokens` | `bool = false` | Remove the matched words from the query. |
| `filter_curated_hits` | `bool = false` | Apply the search filter to the pinned documents too. |
| `stop_processing` | `bool = true` | Stop at this rule when it matches; false lets later rules apply too. |
| `effective_from_ts` | `i64 = 0` | A Unix time before which the rule does nothing; 0 for always. |
| `effective_to_ts` | `i64 = 0` | A Unix time after which the rule does nothing; 0 for never. |
| `metadata` | `str = ""` | Any JSON object to return with the results when the rule applies. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | More members as a JSON object, merged into the rule as they are. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-UpsertSynonymSet.salam

### `WriteOptions`

```salam
struct WriteOptions
```

Options for writing documents. Empty fields are left out.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `str = ""` | One of the `ACTION_` constants; empty means create. |
| `dirty_values` | `str = ""` | One of the `DIRTY_` constants. |
| `batch_size` | `int = 0` | How many documents the server indexes at once during an import. |
| `return_id` | `bool = false` | Include the id of each document in the import result. |
| `return_doc` | `bool = false` | Include each document in the import result. |
| `remote_embedding_batch_size` | `int = 0` | How many documents to send to a remote embedding model at once. |

db-typesense-ImportDocuments.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

struct Book:
    pub id: str = ""
    pub title: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
end

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    println typesense.CreateDocument(c, "books", `{"id": "1", "title": "Dune", "year": 1965}`, err)
    println typesense.UpsertDocument(c, "books", `{"id": "1", "title": "Dune", "year": 1965}`, err)
    println typesense.EmplaceDocument(c, "books", `{"id": "2", "title": "Emma"}`, err)
    println typesense.UpdateDocument(c, "books", "2", `{"year": 1815}`, err)
    println typesense.UpdateDocumentWith(c, "books", "2", `{"year": "1815"}`, typesense.DIRTY_COERCE_OR_REJECT, err)
    println typesense.IndexDocument(c, "books", `{"id": "3", "title": "Ulysses", "year": "1922"}`, typesense.WriteOptions { action = typesense.ACTION_UPSERT, dirty_values = typesense.DIRTY_COERCE_OR_DROP }, err)
    println typesense.GetDocument(c, "books", "1", err)
    println typesense.DocumentExists(c, "books", "42", err)

    mut b := Book {}
    if typesense.GetDocumentAs(c, "books", "1", b, err):
        println b.title, b.year
    end
    println typesense.CreateDocumentOf(c, "books", Book { id = "4", title = "Beloved", year = 1987 }, err)
    println typesense.UpsertDocumentOf(c, "books", Book { id = "4", title = "Beloved", year = 1987 }, err)

    mut books := Vector {} as Vector<Book>
    books.push(Book { id = "5", title = "Hamlet", year = 1603 })
    books.push(Book { id = "6", title = "Middlemarch", year = 1871 })
    r := typesense.ImportOf(c, "books", books, typesense.WriteOptions { action = typesense.ACTION_UPSERT, batch_size = 100, return_id = true }, err)
    println r.success, r.failed, r.ids.len(), r.documents.len(), r.lines.len()
    each e in r.errors:
        println e.line, e.id, e.code, e.error, e.document
    end

    mut docs := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    docs.push(`{"id": "7", "title": "Persuasion", "year": 1817}`)
    docs.push(`{"id": "8", "title": "Walden", "year": "1854"}`)
    r2 := typesense.ImportDocuments(c, "books", docs, typesense.WriteOptions { action = typesense.ACTION_CREATE, dirty_values = typesense.DIRTY_REJECT, return_doc = true }, err)
    println r2.success, r2.failed
    r3 := typesense.ImportJSONL(c, "books", "{\"id\": \"9\", \"title\": \"Emma\"}\n", typesense.WriteOptions { action = typesense.ACTION_UPDATE, remote_embedding_batch_size = 50 }, err)
    println r3.success, typesense.ACTION_EMPLACE, typesense.DIRTY_DROP

    println typesense.UpdateByFilter(c, "books", "year:<1900", `{"classic": true}`, err)
    println typesense.DeleteByFilter(c, "books", "year:<1700", 500, err)
    println typesense.DeleteDocument(c, "books", "9", err)

    lines := typesense.ExportDocuments(c, "books", typesense.ExportOptions { filter_by = "year:>1800", include_fields = "id,title,year", exclude_fields = "" }, err)
    mut back := Vector {} as Vector<Book>
    if typesense.DecodeDocuments(lines, back, err):
        println back.len()
    end
    mut one := Book {}
    println typesense.DecodeDocument(`{"id": "1", "title": "Dune", "year": 1965}`, one, err), one.title
    println typesense.ExportJSONL(c, "books", typesense.ExportOptions {}, err).len()
end
```

### `ImportError`

```salam
struct ImportError
```

One line of an import that failed.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `line` | `int = 0` | Its position in the import, from 0. |
| `id` | `str = ""` | The document id, when `return_id` was set. |
| `code` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status for this line, such as 400 or 409. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The reason it failed. |
| `document` | `str = ""` | The document text, when `return_doc` was set. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-ImportDocuments.salam

### `ImportResult`

```salam
struct ImportResult
```

The result of an import. Typesense answers 200 even when some lines fail, so check `failed`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `success` | `int = 0` | How many documents were written. |
| `failed` | `int = 0` | How many were not. |
| `ids` | `Vector` | The ids of the written documents, with `return_id`. |
| `documents` | `Vector` | The written documents, with `return_doc`. |
| `errors` | `Vector` | The lines that failed. |
| `lines` | `Vector` | The raw result line of every document. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-ImportDocuments.salam

### `ExportOptions`

```salam
struct ExportOptions
```

Which documents to export and which fields.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filter_by` | `str = ""` | A filter, such as `year:>2000`; empty exports all. |
| `include_fields` | `str = ""` | Export only these fields, comma separated. |
| `exclude_fields` | `str = ""` | Leave these fields out, comma separated. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-ImportDocuments.salam

## Functions

### `New`

```salam
func New(url: str, api_key: str): Client
```

A client for one node. A URL with no scheme gets `http://`, and a trailing slash is dropped.

# db/elasticsearch

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-elasticsearch/

An Elasticsearch and OpenSearch client: documents, search, aggregations, bulk, SQL and index management.

Elasticsearch is a search engine and document store spoken to with JSON over HTTP. This package is written in Salam on top of `net.httpx` and `tls`, with no outside library. It works with Elasticsearch 7 and 8, Elastic Cloud (`ConnectCloud`) and OpenSearch; SQL and point in time calls switch to the OpenSearch endpoints by themselves. A client keeps one connection open per node and can list several nodes: it rotates over them, skips a node that refuses connections for `DEAD_NODE_MS`, and retries on 502, 503 and 504. Documents and query clauses are plain JSON text, so you can mix the builders here with JSON you write by hand, and `Perform` reaches every API that has no function of its own. After any call, `Error`, `ErrorType` and `Status` describe what the server said. The examples need a running cluster, so they are only checked.

New to Elasticsearch? Lesson 27, Search with Elasticsearch, walks through the package step by step with runnable examples.

## Types

### `AsyncSearch`

```salam
struct AsyncSearch
```

An async search: its id, whether it still runs, and the result so far.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Whether it succeeded. |
| `id` | `str = ""` | The id to fetch or delete the search with. |
| `running` | `bool = false` | Whether the search is still running. |
| `partial` | `bool = false` | Whether the result is partial. |
| `result` | `SearchResult` | The search result so far. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The error text, empty on success. |

db-elasticsearch-Admin.salam

```salam
import time
import encoding.json
import db.elasticsearch

func main:
    c := elasticsearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")

    elasticsearch.PutPipeline(c, "clean", `{"processors":[{"lowercase":{"field":"tag"}},{"set":{"field":"seen","value":true}}]}`)
    test := elasticsearch.SimulatePipeline(c, "clean", `{"docs":[{"_source":{"tag":"LOUD"}}]}`)
    println json.GetPath(test, "docs.0.doc._source.tag")
    elasticsearch.IndexWith(c, "books", "9", `{"tag":"Poetry"}`, elasticsearch.Options { pipeline = "clean" })

    elasticsearch.PutIndexTemplate(c, "app_logs", `{"index_patterns":["applog-*"],"data_stream":{},"priority":200}`)
    elasticsearch.CreateDataStream(c, "applog-web")
    elasticsearch.Create(c, "applog-web", "", `{"@timestamp":"2026-10-16T10:00:00Z","msg":"started"}`)
    elasticsearch.Rollover(c, "applog-web", "")
    println elasticsearch.GetDataStream(c, "applog-web")

    policy := `{"policy":{"phases":{"delete":{"min_age":"30d","actions":{"delete":{}}}}}}`
    if not elasticsearch.IsOpenSearch(c): elasticsearch.PutLifecyclePolicy(c, "month", policy) end

    elasticsearch.PutRepository(c, "backups", `{"type":"fs","settings":{"location":"/mnt/backups"}}`)
    elasticsearch.CreateSnapshot(c, "backups", "nightly", `{"indices":"books"}`)
    println elasticsearch.ListSnapshots(c, "backups")

    id := elasticsearch.StartUpdateByQuery(c, "books", elasticsearch.MatchAll(), elasticsearch.Script("ctx._source.year += 1", ""))
    mut task := elasticsearch.GetTask(c, id)
    until task.ok and not task.completed:
        time.Sleep(200)
        task = elasticsearch.GetTask(c, id)
    end
    println json.Get(task.response, "updated")

    elasticsearch.PutStoredScript(c, "by_tag", "mustache", `{"query":{"term":{"tag":"{{tag}}"}}}`)
    hits := elasticsearch.SearchTemplate(c, "books", "by_tag", `{"tag":"poetry"}`)
    println hits.total

    mut a := elasticsearch.SubmitAsyncSearch(c, "books", elasticsearch.SearchRequest { query = elasticsearch.MatchAll() }, "1s")
    until a.running:
        a = elasticsearch.GetAsyncSearch(c, a.id, "1s")
    end
    println a.result.total
    elasticsearch.DeleteAsyncSearch(c, a.id)

    println elasticsearch.ValidateQuery(c, "books", elasticsearch.Match("title", "shahnameh"))
    println elasticsearch.Explain(c, "books", "9", elasticsearch.Term("tag", "poetry"))
    println elasticsearch.PutClusterSettings(c, `{"persistent":{"indices.recovery.max_bytes_per_sec":"100mb"}}`)
end
```

### `Task`

```salam
struct Task
```

A server task started with one of the `Start*` calls.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Whether it succeeded. |
| `id` | `str = ""` | The task id, `node:number`. |
| `completed` | `bool = false` | Whether the task has finished. |
| `action` | `str = ""` | The task action, such as `indices:data/write/update/byquery`. |
| `response` | `str = ""` | The raw response of a finished task, such as counts of updated documents. |
| `raw` | `str = ""` | The raw JSON it was parsed from. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-elasticsearch-Admin.salam

### `Config`

```salam
struct Config
```

Everything a client needs: nodes, credentials, TLS, timeout, retries and extra headers.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `Vector` | Node URLs; each may list several separated by commas. |
| `cloud_id` | `str = ""` | An Elastic Cloud id, used before `nodes`. |
| `username` | `str = ""` | The user for basic authentication. |
| `password` | `str = ""` | The password for basic authentication. |
| `api_key` | `str = ""` | An API key, encoded or `id:key`; wins over basic authentication. |
| `bearer` | `str = ""` | A bearer token, such as a service account token. |
| `ca_file` | `str = ""` | A PEM file of the CA that signed the cluster certificate, for example `http_ca.crt`. |
| `insecure` | `bool = false` | Skip TLS certificate checks. Only for local testing. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int = 30000` | The connect and read timeout of one request in milliseconds; 0 waits forever. |
| `max_retries` | `int = 3` | How many more nodes to try after a connection failure or a 502, 503 or 504. |
| `keep_alive` | `bool = true` | Reuse one connection per node across requests (the default). Over HTTPS this skips a TLS handshake per call; a connection the server closed is reopened on its own. |
| `headers` | `HashMap` | Extra headers sent with every request. |

db-elasticsearch-Client.salam

```salam
import db.elasticsearch

func main:
    mut cfg := elasticsearch.DefaultConfig()
    cfg.username = "elastic"
    cfg.password = "s3cret"
    cfg.ca_file = "/etc/elasticsearch/certs/http_ca.crt"
    cfg.timeout_ms = 10000
    cfg.headers.put("X-Opaque-Id", "salam-docs")
    mut c := elasticsearch.NewClient(cfg)
    if not elasticsearch.Ping(c):
        println "cannot reach elasticsearch:", elasticsearch.Error(c)
        ret
    end
    info := elasticsearch.GetInfo(c)
    println info.distribution, info.version, elasticsearch.ClusterHealth(c).status

    mapping := `{"mappings":{"properties":{"title":{"type":"text"},"year":{"type":"integer"}}}}`
    if not elasticsearch.IndexExists(c, "books"):
        elasticsearch.CreateIndex(c, "books", mapping)
    end
    w := elasticsearch.IndexWith(c, "books", "1", `{"title":"Shahnameh","year":1010}`, elasticsearch.Options { refresh = elasticsearch.REFRESH_WAIT_FOR })
    println w.result, w.version

    d := elasticsearch.Get(c, "books", "1")
    if d.found: println d.source end
    u := elasticsearch.UpdateWith(c, "books", "1", `{"year":1011}`, elasticsearch.Options { if_seq_no = d.seq_no, if_primary_term = d.primary_term })
    if not u.ok: println "conflict:", elasticsearch.ErrorType(c) end
    elasticsearch.UpdateScript(c, "books", "1", "ctx._source.year += params.n", `{"n": 1}`)
    println elasticsearch.Exists(c, "books", "1"), elasticsearch.Count(c, "books", "")

    r := elasticsearch.Perform(c, "GET", "/_cat/health?format=json", "")
    println r.status, r.body
    elasticsearch.Delete(c, "books", "1")
    elasticsearch.Close(c)
end
```

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

Optional request parameters shared by the write calls: refresh, routing, pipeline, optimistic concurrency and more.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | `str = ""` | `true`, `wait_for` or `false`; see the `REFRESH_*` constants. |
| `routing` | `str = ""` | A custom routing value. |
| `pipeline` | `str = ""` | An ingest pipeline to run first. |
| `timeout` | `str = ""` | A server side timeout such as `30s`. |
| `wait_for_active_shards` | `str = ""` | How many shard copies must be active, or `all`. |
| `source` | `str = ""` | Source filtering: for `Options` a comma list of fields, for `SearchRequest` the fields to return; on results the raw `_source` JSON. |
| `conflicts` | `str = ""` | `proceed` to skip version conflicts in by query operations. |
| `if_seq_no` | `i64 = -1` | Only write when the document still has this sequence number; -1 turns it off. |
| `if_primary_term` | `i64 = -1` | The primary term that goes with `if_seq_no`. |
| `retry_on_conflict` | `int = -1` | How many times an update retries on a version conflict; -1 leaves the default. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-elasticsearch-Client.salam

db-elasticsearch-Search.salam

```salam
import db.elasticsearch

func main:
    c := elasticsearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut must := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    must.push(elasticsearch.Match("title", "persian poetry"))
    mut filters := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    filters.push(elasticsearch.Range("year", "900", "1500"))
    filters.push(elasticsearch.Not(elasticsearch.Term("status", "draft")))
    mut aggs := elasticsearch.AddAgg("", "by_author", elasticsearch.SubAggs(elasticsearch.TermsAgg("author", 5), elasticsearch.AddAgg("", "avg_year", elasticsearch.AvgAgg("year"))))
    aggs = elasticsearch.AddAgg(aggs, "newest", elasticsearch.MaxAgg("year"))
    mut sort := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    sort.push(elasticsearch.SortDesc("year"))
    mut fields := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    fields.push("title")
    req := elasticsearch.SearchRequest {
        query = elasticsearch.Filtered(elasticsearch.And(must), filters), size = 10, sort = sort, aggs = aggs, highlight = elasticsearch.Highlight(fields)
    }
    res := elasticsearch.Search(c, "books", req)
    if not res.ok:
        println elasticsearch.Error(c)
        ret
    end
    println res.total, res.total_relation, res.took
    each h in res.hits:
        println h.id, h.score, h.source, h.highlight
    end
    println elasticsearch.AggValue(res, "newest")
    each b in elasticsearch.AggBuckets(res, "by_author"):
        println b.key, b.doc_count, elasticsearch.AggValueIn(b.raw, "avg_year")
    end

    mut page := elasticsearch.SearchScroll(c, "books", elasticsearch.SearchRequest { query = elasticsearch.MatchAll(), size = 500 }, "1m")
    until page.hits.len() > 0:
        println "page of", page.hits.len()
        page = elasticsearch.Scroll(c, page.scroll_id, "1m")
    end
    elasticsearch.ClearScroll(c, page.scroll_id)

    pit := elasticsearch.OpenPit(c, "books", "1m")
    first := elasticsearch.Search(c, "", elasticsearch.SearchRequest { pit_id = pit, size = 100, sort = sort })
    if first.hits.len() > 0:
        last := first.hits.get(first.hits.len() - 1)
        next := elasticsearch.Search(c, "", elasticsearch.SearchRequest { pit_id = pit, size = 100, sort = sort, search_after = last.sort })
        println next.hits.len()
    end
    elasticsearch.ClosePit(c, pit)
    println elasticsearch.DeleteByQuery(c, "books", elasticsearch.Term("status", "draft"))
end
```

### `SearchResult`

```salam
struct SearchResult
```

A parsed search response: totals, hits, aggregations and paging ids.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Whether it succeeded. |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status, or the status reported for this item. |
| `took` | `i64 = 0` | Milliseconds the server spent. |
| `timed_out` | `bool = false` | Whether the server timed out. |
| `total` | `i64 = 0` | The number of matching documents. |
| `total_relation` | `str = ""` | `eq` when `total` is exact, `gte` when it is a lower bound. |
| `max_score` | `f64 = 0` | The best score. |
| `hits` | `Vector` | The hits of this page. |
| `aggregations` | `str = ""` | The raw aggregations JSON. |
| `suggest` | `str = ""` | Suggesters: the section on a request, the raw result on a response. |
| `scroll_id` | `str = ""` | The id for the next `Scroll`. |
| `pit_id` | `str = ""` | A point in time id: on a request to search it, on a result the refreshed id. |
| `raw` | `str = ""` | The raw JSON it was parsed from. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The error text, empty on success. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-elasticsearch-Search.salam

### `SearchRequest`

```salam
struct SearchRequest
```

A search request; `SearchBody` turns it into JSON. Empty fields are left out.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query clause JSON; empty matches everything. |
| `from` | `int = -1` | The offset of the first hit; -1 leaves it out. |
| `size` | `int = -1` | How many hits to return; -1 leaves it out. |
| `sort` | `Vector` | Sort clauses on a request; on a hit the raw sort values, to pass to `search_after`. |
| `source` | `Vector` | Source filtering: for `Options` a comma list of fields, for `SearchRequest` the fields to return; on results the raw `_source` JSON. |
| `source_excludes` | `Vector` | Fields to leave out of `_source`. |
| `no_source` | `bool = false` | Return no `_source` at all. |
| `fields` | `Vector` | Stored or runtime fields: raw JSON on results, a field list on `SearchRequest`. |
| `aggs` | `str = ""` | The aggregations object, built with `AddAgg`. |
| `highlight` | `str = ""` | Highlighting: the section on a request, the raw fragments on a hit. |
| `post_filter` | `str = ""` | A filter applied after aggregations. |
| `knn` | `str = ""` | A `Knn` clause for vector search. |
| `collapse` | `str = ""` | A field to collapse hits on, one hit per value. |
| `suggest` | `str = ""` | Suggesters: the section on a request, the raw result on a response. |
| `search_after` | `str = ""` | The raw sort values of the last hit of the previous page. |
| `pit_id` | `str = ""` | A point in time id: on a request to search it, on a result the refreshed id. |
| `pit_keep_alive` | `str = ""` | How long to keep the point in time alive, such as `1m`. |
| `track_total_hits` | `str = ""` | `true` for an exact total, or a number as the counting limit. |
| `min_score` | `str = ""` | Leave out hits scoring below this. |
| `timeout` | `str = ""` | A server side timeout such as `30s`. |
| `extra` | `Vector` | Raw members added to the body, such as `"explain": true`. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-elasticsearch-Search.salam

### `Bulk`

```salam
struct Bulk
```

A bulk request being built; add actions with the `Bulk*` functions.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `Vector` | The NDJSON lines so far. |
| `count` | `int = 0` | How many actions were added. |

db-elasticsearch-Bulk.salam

```salam
import str
import db.elasticsearch

func main:
    c := elasticsearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut b := elasticsearch.NewBulk()
    repeat 1000 in i:
        id := str.FromInt(i as i64)
        elasticsearch.BulkIndex(b, "logs", id, `{"line":` + id + `,"level":"info"}`)
    end
    elasticsearch.BulkUpdate(b, "logs", "7", `{"level":"warn"}`)
    elasticsearch.BulkUpsert(b, "logs", "new", `{"line":-1}`)
    elasticsearch.BulkDelete(b, "logs", "8")
    println elasticsearch.BulkLen(b)
    res := elasticsearch.RunBulkWith(c, "", b, elasticsearch.Options { refresh = elasticsearch.REFRESH_TRUE })
    println res.ok, res.succeeded, res.failed, res.took
    if res.errors:
        each it in res.items:
            if not it.ok: println it.action, it.id, it.status, it.error_type, it.error_reason end
        end
    end
    elasticsearch.BulkReset(b)
end
```

### `SqlRows`

```salam
struct SqlRows
```

SQL query results; implements `db.Rows` and fetches further pages with the cursor as you call `Next`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The internal state pointer. |

db-elasticsearch-Sql.salam

```salam
import db
import db.elasticsearch

func report(conn: dyn db.Connection):
    rows := conn.Query("SELECT level, COUNT(*) AS n FROM logs GROUP BY level")
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Text(0), rows.Int(1)
    end
    rows.Close()
end

func main:
    c := elasticsearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut params := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    params.push("100")
    mut rows := elasticsearch.SqlWith(c, "SELECT line, level FROM logs WHERE line < ? ORDER BY line", params, 50)
    println rows.ColumnCount(), rows.ColumnName(0), rows.ColumnTypeName(0), rows.ColumnType(0) == db.TYPE_INT
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Int64(0), rows.Text(1), rows.IsNull(1)
    end
    rows.Close()
    print elasticsearch.SqlText(c, "SELECT level FROM logs LIMIT 3")
    println elasticsearch.SqlTranslate(c, "SELECT line FROM logs WHERE level = 'warn'")
    report(elasticsearch.Conn(c))
end
```

---

# db/meilisearch

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-meilisearch/

A Meilisearch client: indexes, documents, full text, faceted, hybrid and federated search, settings, tasks and API keys.

Meilisearch is a fast search engine with typo tolerance, filters, facets and AI powered hybrid search. This package talks to its HTTP API directly with `net.httpx` and covers all of it: indexes, documents in JSON, NDJSON or CSV, every search parameter, multi-search and federated search, facet search, similar documents, every index setting, tasks and batches, API keys and tenant tokens, webhooks, dynamic search rules and chat workspaces. This page starts with a tutorial; the full reference of every function and type comes after it.

## Tutorial: a movie search in eleven steps

The steps below build one small movie catalogue and search it. Each step is a complete program, and the output under it is what it printed against a real Meilisearch 1.55. Run them in order, because each step uses the data the earlier ones left behind.

First start a server. With Docker that is one command; without it, download the `meilisearch` binary from the Meilisearch releases page and run it with the same key:

```salam
docker run -p 7700:7700 -e MEILI_MASTER_KEY=masterKey getmeili/meilisearch:v1.55.0
```

The programs assume `http://127.0.0.1:7700` and the master key `masterKey`. A real deployment uses a long random master key and gives applications smaller keys, as step 9 shows.

## 1. Connect

`New` makes a client: a plain value with the address and the key, which threads can share. `WithTimeout` returns a copy that stops waiting after the given milliseconds; without it a request waits as long as the server takes. Every call that can fail takes an `Error` as its last argument. `Ok` tells you whether the call worked and `ErrorString` turns the error into one line.

meili-connect.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.WithTimeout(meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey"), 5000)
    if not meilisearch.IsHealthy(c):
        println "Meilisearch is not running at " + c.host
        ret 1
    end
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}
    version := meilisearch.GetVersion(c, err)
    println "connected to Meilisearch " + version.pkg_version

    meilisearch.GetIndex(c, "no_such_index", err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
connected to Meilisearch 1.55.0
meilisearch 404 [index_not_found]: Index `no_such_index` not found.
```

The error carries everything Meilisearch sent: the HTTP `status`, the `code` to branch on (here `index_not_found`), the `message` and a `link` to its documentation. When the server cannot be reached at all, `code` is `communication_error`, or `timeout` when the time limit ran out.

## 2. Create an index and add documents

An index is a named collection of documents, each with a unique primary key. Documents can be Salam structs: `AddDocumentsOf` turns each one into JSON. `AddDocuments` takes JSON text instead, and `AddDocumentsNdjson` and `AddDocumentsCsv` take those formats.

meili-index.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

struct Movie:
    pub id: int = 0
    pub title: str = ""
    pub genre: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
    pub overview: str = ""
end

func movie(id: int, title: str, genre: str, year: int, overview: str): Movie:
    ret Movie { id = id, title = title, genre = genre, year = year, overview = overview }
end

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.CreateIndex(c, "movies", "id", err), err)

    mut movies := Vector {} as Vector<Movie>
    movies.push(movie(1, "Heat", "Crime", 1995, "A detective hunts a crew of professional thieves in Los Angeles."))
    movies.push(movie(2, "Moana", "Family", 2016, "A girl sails across the ocean to save her island."))
    movies.push(movie(3, "Alien", "Horror", 1979, "The crew of a space freighter meets a deadly creature."))
    movies.push(movie(4, "Up", "Family", 2009, "An old man flies his house away with thousands of balloons."))
    movies.push(movie(5, "Arrival", "Drama", 2016, "A linguist learns to talk with visitors from another world."))
    movies.push(movie(6, "Dune", "Adventure", 2021, "A young noble fights for a desert planet."))
    movies.push(movie(7, "Interstellar", "Drama", 2014, "Explorers travel through a wormhole to find a new home."))
    movies.push(movie(8, "Coco", "Family", 2017, "A boy enters the land of the dead to find his family."))

    task := meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.AddDocumentsOf(c, "movies", movies, "id", err), err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println "indexing: " + task.status
    stats := meilisearch.GetIndexStats(c, "movies", err)
    println "documents in movies: " + stats.number_of_documents
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
indexing: succeeded
documents in movies: 8
```

Meilisearch does not apply a change at once. A write returns a `TaskInfo`, a receipt with a task number, and the server applies the tasks in order in the background. `Wait` blocks until that task has finished, which is what you want when the next line depends on the change. A batch import does not need to wait after every call; wait once at the end, or not at all.

## 3. Search

`Query` searches for some words with every option at its default. The hits come back as JSON text, and `HitsAs` reads them into your own struct. A struct with fewer fields than the document is fine: the extra fields are ignored.

meili-search.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

struct Movie:
    pub id: int = 0
    pub title: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
end

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    res := meilisearch.Query(c, "movies", "spcae", err)
    println "hits for \"" + res.query + "\": " + res.estimated_total_hits
    mut movies := Vector {} as Vector<Movie>
    if meilisearch.HitsAs(res, movies, err):
        each m in movies:
            println "  " + m.title + " (" + m.year + ")"
        end
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
hits for "spcae": 1
  Alien (1979)
```

The query was misspelled on purpose: `spcae` still finds the movie whose overview says space, because Meilisearch tolerates typos out of the box.

## 4. Filter, sort and count facets

Filtering and sorting need to be switched on for the fields involved; that is a setting of the index, and `UpdateSettings` changes several settings in one task. A `SearchRequest` holds every search option and sends only the ones you set.

meili-filter.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    settings := `{"filterableAttributes": ["genre", "year"], "sortableAttributes": ["year"]}`
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateSettings(c, "movies", settings, err), err)

    mut req := meilisearch.SearchRequest { filter = "genre = Family AND year > 2010" }
    req.sort.push("year:desc")
    req.facets.push("genre")
    req.attributes_to_retrieve.push("title")
    req.attributes_to_retrieve.push("year")
    res := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", req, err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    each hit in res.hits:
        println hit
    end

    all := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", meilisearch.SearchRequest { facets = req.facets, limit = 0 }, err)
    println "genres: " + all.facet_distribution
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
{"title":"Coco","year":2017}
{"title":"Moana","year":2016}
genres: {"genre":{"Adventure":1,"Crime":1,"Drama":2,"Family":3,"Horror":1}}
```

`facets` asks how many hits have each value of a field, which is how a search page shows filter options with counts. `attributes_to_retrieve` keeps the hits small by returning only the fields you need.

## 5. Highlight, crop and page through results

For a results page you usually want the matched words marked and long text cut down around them. Meilisearch adds a `_formatted` copy of each hit with both done. `page` and `hits_per_page` give numbered pages with an exact total; `offset` and `limit` are the cheaper choice for endless scrolling.

meili-highlight.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch
import encoding.json

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    mut req := meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "crew", hits_per_page = 1, page = 1 }
    req.attributes_to_highlight.push("overview")
    req.highlight_pre_tag = "["
    req.highlight_post_tag = "]"
    req.attributes_to_crop.push("overview")
    req.crop_length = 6
    res := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", req, err)
    println "page " + res.page + " of " + res.total_pages + ", " + res.total_hits + " hits"
    each hit in res.hits:
        formatted := json.Get(hit, "_formatted")
        println json.Get(hit, "title") + ": " + json.Get(formatted, "overview")
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
page 1 of 2, 2 hits
Alien: The [crew] of a space freighter…
```

## 6. Tune relevancy

Every index setting has its own `Get`, `Update` and `Reset` function. Synonyms make different words find each other, stop words are ignored in queries, and the searchable attributes choose which fields are searched and how much each one counts.

meili-settings.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateSynonyms(c, "movies", `{"cartoon": ["family"], "space": ["planet", "wormhole"]}`, err), err)
    mut stop := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    stop.push("the")
    stop.push("a")
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateStopWords(c, "movies", stop, err), err)
    mut searchable := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    searchable.push("title")
    searchable.push("overview")
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateSearchableAttributes(c, "movies", searchable, err), err)

    res := meilisearch.Query(c, "movies", "cartoon", err)
    println "hits for \"cartoon\", a synonym of family: " + res.estimated_total_hits
    space := meilisearch.Query(c, "movies", "space", err)
    println "hits for \"space\": " + space.estimated_total_hits
    println "searchable: " + meilisearch.GetSetting(c, "movies", "searchable-attributes", err)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
hits for "cartoon", a synonym of family: 1
hits for "space": 3
searchable: ["title","overview"]
```

Other settings follow the same pattern: `UpdateRankingRules`, `UpdateTypoTolerance`, `UpdateDistinctAttribute`, `UpdatePagination`, `UpdateFaceting`, `UpdateDictionary` and the rest in the reference below. `GetSetting` and `UpdateSetting` reach any setting by its route name, including ones newer than this package.

## 7. Search several indexes at once

`MultiSearch` sends several searches in one request and returns one result each. `FederatedSearch` merges them into a single ranked list, which suits one search box over different kinds of content. `FacetSearch` searches the values of one facet, for a filter box that completes as you type.

meili-multi.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.AddDocuments(c, "books", `[{"id": 1, "title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert"}, {"id": 2, "title": "Coco and the Moon", "author": "A. Writer"}]`, "id", err), err)

    mut queries := Vector {} as Vector<meilisearch.MultiQuery>
    queries.push(meilisearch.MultiQuery { index_uid = "movies", request = meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "dune" } })
    queries.push(meilisearch.MultiQuery { index_uid = "books", request = meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "dune" } })
    each r in meilisearch.MultiSearch(c, queries, err):
        println r.index_uid + ": " + r.hits.len() + " hit"
    end

    merged := meilisearch.FederatedSearch(c, queries, meilisearch.Federation { limit = 5 }, err)
    println "federated: " + merged.hits.len() + " hits in one list"

    genres := meilisearch.FacetSearch(c, "movies", meilisearch.FacetSearchRequest { facet_name = "genre", facet_query = "fam" }, err)
    each g in genres.hits:
        println "genre " + g.value + ": " + g.count
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
movies: 1 hit
books: 1 hit
federated: 2 hits in one list
genre Family: 3
```

## 8. Vector and hybrid search

Meilisearch can also search by meaning. An embedder turns documents into vectors; it can call a model such as OpenAI or Hugging Face, or take vectors you computed yourself, which is what the `userProvided` source in this step does. A search with `hybrid_embedder` mixes keyword and vector results; a `hybrid_semantic_ratio` of 1 uses vectors only. `SimilarDocuments` finds the documents nearest to one you already have.

meili-vectors.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.CreateIndex(c, "movies_ai", "id", err), err)
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateEmbedders(c, "movies_ai", `{"manual": {"source": "userProvided", "dimensions": 3}}`, err), err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    docs := `[
        {"id": 2, "title": "Moana", "_vectors": {"manual": [0.9, 0.1, 0.0]}},
        {"id": 4, "title": "Up", "_vectors": {"manual": [0.8, 0.2, 0.1]}},
        {"id": 5, "title": "Arrival", "_vectors": {"manual": [0.1, 0.9, 0.3]}},
        {"id": 6, "title": "Dune", "_vectors": {"manual": [0.2, 0.8, 0.4]}},
        {"id": 7, "title": "Interstellar", "_vectors": {"manual": [0.1, 0.8, 0.5]}},
        {"id": 8, "title": "Coco", "_vectors": {"manual": [0.9, 0.0, 0.1]}}
    ]`
    task := meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.AddDocuments(c, "movies_ai", docs, "", err), err)
    println "vectors stored: " + task.status

    mut req := meilisearch.SearchRequest { hybrid_embedder = "manual", hybrid_semantic_ratio = 1.0, limit = 2 }
    req.vector.push(0.15)
    req.vector.push(0.85)
    req.vector.push(0.4)
    req.attributes_to_retrieve.push("title")
    res := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies_ai", req, err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    each hit in res.hits:
        println "close to the query: " + hit
    end

    mut like := meilisearch.SimilarRequest { id = "2", embedder = "manual", limit = 2 }
    like.attributes_to_retrieve.push("title")
    each hit in meilisearch.SimilarDocuments(c, "movies_ai", like, err).hits:
        println "like Moana: " + hit
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
vectors stored: succeeded
close to the query: {"title":"Dune"}
close to the query: {"title":"Arrival"}
like Moana: {"title":"Coco"}
like Moana: {"title":"Up"}
```

A `userProvided` embedder needs a vector in every document, so this step uses its own index. Add the embedder while the index is still empty and send the vectors in each document under `_vectors`.

## 9. API keys and tenant tokens

The master key can do everything, so applications should get smaller keys. `CreateKey` makes a key limited to some actions and indexes. A tenant token goes one step further: `TenantToken` signs, in your own program and without asking the server, a key that adds a filter to every search. Give each user their own token and they can search directly from the browser while seeing only their rows.

meili-keys.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch
import time

func main:
    admin := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    mut r := meilisearch.KeyRequest { name = "Shop front end", description = "Search the movies index only" }
    r.actions.push("search")
    r.indexes.push("movies")
    key := meilisearch.CreateKey(admin, r, err)
    println "new key " + key.name + " can: " + key.actions.get(0)

    rules := `{"movies": {"filter": "genre = Family"}}`
    token := meilisearch.TenantToken(key.uid, key.key, rules, time.Now() + 3600, err)
    kids := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", token)
    res := meilisearch.Query(kids, "movies", "", err)
    println "the token sees " + res.estimated_total_hits + " family movies"

    meilisearch.Query(kids, "books", "", err)
    println "books with the token: " + err.code

    println "key deleted: " + meilisearch.DeleteKey(admin, key.uid, err)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
new key Shop front end can: search
the token sees 3 family movies
books with the token: invalid_api_key
key deleted: true
```

## 10. Update and delete documents

`AddDocuments` replaces a whole document with the same id; `UpdateDocuments` changes only the fields you send. Documents can be deleted one by one, by a list of ids, by a filter, or all at once.

meili-update.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

struct Movie:
    pub id: int = 0
    pub title: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
end

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateDocuments(c, "movies", `[{"id": 6, "title": "Dune: Part One"}]`, "", err), err)
    mut dune := Movie {}
    if meilisearch.GetDocumentAs(c, "movies", "6", dune, err):
        println "renamed: " + dune.title + " (" + dune.year + ")"
    end

    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.DeleteDocument(c, "movies", "3", err), err)
    meilisearch.GetDocument(c, "movies", "3", Vector {} as Vector<str>, err)
    println "after delete: " + err.code

    removed := meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.DeleteDocumentsByFilter(c, "movies", "year < 2000", err), err)
    println "delete by filter: " + removed.status + " " + removed.details
    println "left: " + meilisearch.GetIndexStats(c, "movies", err).number_of_documents
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
renamed: Dune: Part One (2021)
after delete: document_not_found
delete by filter: succeeded {"providedIds":0,"deletedDocuments":1,"originalFilter":"\"year < 2000\""}
left: 6
```

## 11. Tasks and failures

A write that is accepted can still fail later, while the server applies it. The error then lives on the task, not on the call that queued it. `WaitForTask` copies it into your `Error`, so the usual check works. `GetTasks` lists past tasks with filters on index, type, status and dates.

meili-tasks.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    info := meilisearch.AddDocuments(c, "movies", `[{"title": "No id here"}]`, "", err)
    println "queued task " + info.task_uid + ": " + info.status
    task := meilisearch.WaitForTask(c, info.task_uid, 10000, 50, err)
    println "finished as " + task.status
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println "why: " + err.code
    end

    mut q := meilisearch.TaskQuery { limit = 3 }
    q.index_uids.push("movies")
    q.statuses.push(meilisearch.STATUS_SUCCEEDED)
    page := meilisearch.GetTasks(c, q, err)
    println "recent successful tasks on movies:"
    each t in page.results:
        println "  " + t.kind
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
queued task 13: enqueued
finished as failed
why: missing_document_id
recent successful tasks on movies:
  documentDeletion
  documentDeletion
  documentAdditionOrUpdate
```

## More

The rest of the API works the same way; the reference below covers each function. A few pointers:

- `CreateWebhook` registers a URL that Meilisearch calls when tasks finish, so you do not need to poll.

- `UpdateSearchRule` pins or boosts chosen documents for chosen queries, such as a sale banner for sale; it needs the `dynamicSearchRules` experimental feature.

- `UpdateChatSettings` and `ChatCompletion` answer questions in plain language from your indexes through an LLM; they need the `chatCompletions` feature.

- `WithMetadata` tags every document write with a label that comes back on the task, to follow one import through the task list.

- `CreateDump`, `CreateSnapshot`, `GetStats`, `GetMetrics` and `SetStderrLogs` are for running the server.

- For a route with no function of its own, `Request` sends any method, path and JSON body.

The Salam repository has one runnable example for each part of the API, in English under `tests/en/stdlib/meilisearch/examples` and in Persian under `tests/fa/stdlib/meilisearch/examples`.

struct ChatWorkspacePage

db-meilisearch-ChatCompletion.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}
    meilisearch.UpdateExperimentalFeatures(c, `{"chatCompletions": true}`, err)

    settings := `{"source": "openAi", "apiKey": "sk-your-key", "prompts": {"system": "You answer questions about our movie catalog."}}`
    println meilisearch.UpdateChatSettings(c, "support", settings, err)
    println meilisearch.GetChatSettings(c, "support", err)
    ws := meilisearch.ListChatWorkspaces(c, 0, 20, err)
    println ws.total, ws.offset, ws.limit
    each name in ws.results:
        println name, meilisearch.GetChatWorkspace(c, name, err)
    end

    request := `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "stream": true, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Which space movies do you have?"}]}`
    println meilisearch.ChatCompletion(c, "support", request, err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
    end
    println meilisearch.ResetChatSettings(c, "support", err)
    println meilisearch.DeleteChatWorkspace(c, "support", err)
end
```

### `SearchRequest`

```salam
struct SearchRequest
```

Everything a search can ask for. Only fields you set are sent: empty text and lists, -1 numbers and false flags are left out.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The words to search for; empty lists every document. |
| `offset` | `int = -1` | How many hits to skip. |
| `limit` | `int = -1` | How many hits to return; 20 by default. |
| `page` | `int = -1` | The page number, for numbered pages with an exact total. |
| `hits_per_page` | `int = -1` | The hits on each numbered page. |
| `filter` | `str = ""` | A filter expression such as `year > 2000 AND genre = Drama`, or a JSON array of them. |
| `facets` | `Vector` | Count the values of these fields among the hits. |
| `attributes_to_retrieve` | `Vector` | Return only these fields. |
| `attributes_to_crop` | `Vector` | Cut these fields around the matched words. |
| `crop_length` | `int = -1` | How many words a cropped field keeps. |
| `crop_marker` | `str = ""` | The text that marks a cut. |
| `attributes_to_highlight` | `Vector` | Wrap the matched words of these fields in tags. |
| `highlight_pre_tag` | `str = ""` | The tag before a match; `<em>` by default. |
| `highlight_post_tag` | `str = ""` | The tag after a match. |
| `show_matches_position` | `bool = false` | Return where every match is. |
| `sort` | `Vector` | Sort rules such as `year:desc`. |
| `matching_strategy` | `str = ""` | One of the `MATCH_` values. |
| `show_ranking_score` | `bool = false` | Return the relevancy score of each hit. |
| `show_ranking_score_details` | `bool = false` | Return how the score was built. |
| `ranking_score_threshold` | `f64 = -1` | Drop hits scoring below this, from 0 to 1. |
| `attributes_to_search_on` | `Vector` | Search only these fields. |
| `distinct` | `str = ""` | Return at most one hit for each value of this field. |
| `locales` | `Vector` | The languages of the query, such as `fas`. |
| `vector` | `Vector` | Search by this vector. |
| `hybrid_embedder` | `str = ""` | The embedder for AI powered search; setting it turns hybrid search on. |
| `hybrid_semantic_ratio` | `f64 = -1` | How much meaning outweighs keywords, from 0 to 1. |
| `retrieve_vectors` | `bool = false` | Also return the stored vectors. |
| `media` | `str = ""` | Raw JSON media for multimodal search, such as an image. |
| `show_performance_details` | `bool = false` | Return how long each step of the search took. |
| `use_network` | `bool = false` | Search every instance of a sharded network. |
| `personalize` | `str = ""` | Personalization options as raw JSON, such as `{"userContext": "..."}`. |
| `inline_rule` | `str = ""` | A dynamic search rule for this search only, as raw JSON. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | A raw JSON object whose fields are added to the request, for parameters this struct does not have yet. |

db-meilisearch-Search.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

struct Movie:
    pub id: int = 0
    pub title: str = ""
end

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "searchKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    quick := meilisearch.Query(c, "movies", "botman", err)
    println quick.query, quick.estimated_total_hits, quick.processing_time_ms

    mut r := meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "space", limit = 10, offset = 0, filter = "year > 2000 AND genre = Drama" }
    r.facets.push("genre")
    r.sort.push("year:desc")
    r.attributes_to_retrieve.push("id")
    r.attributes_to_retrieve.push("title")
    r.attributes_to_highlight.push("title")
    r.highlight_pre_tag = "<mark>"
    r.highlight_post_tag = "</mark>"
    r.attributes_to_crop.push("overview")
    r.crop_length = 20
    r.crop_marker = "..."
    r.matching_strategy = meilisearch.MATCH_ALL
    r.show_ranking_score = true
    r.show_ranking_score_details = false
    r.show_matches_position = false
    r.ranking_score_threshold = 0.2
    r.attributes_to_search_on.push("title")
    r.locales.push("eng")
    r.distinct = "studio"
    res := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", r, err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        ret
    end
    println res.index_uid, res.offset, res.limit, res.facet_distribution, res.facet_stats, res.raw.len()
    each hit in res.hits:
        println hit
    end
    mut movies := Vector {} as Vector<Movie>
    if meilisearch.HitsAs(res, movies, err):
        println movies.len()
    end

    pages := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "space", page = 2, hits_per_page = 20 }, err)
    println pages.page, pages.hits_per_page, pages.total_hits, pages.total_pages

    mut hybrid := meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "a sad robot", hybrid_embedder = "default", hybrid_semantic_ratio = 0.7, retrieve_vectors = false, matching_strategy = meilisearch.MATCH_LAST }
    hybrid.vector.push(0.1)
    hybrid.media = `{"image": "https://example.com/robot.png"}`
    hybrid.extra = `{"showPerformanceDetails": true}`
    println meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", hybrid, err).semantic_hit_count, meilisearch.MATCH_FREQUENCY

    mut queries := Vector {} as Vector<meilisearch.MultiQuery>
    queries.push(meilisearch.MultiQuery { index_uid = "movies", request = meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "moana" } })
    queries.push(meilisearch.MultiQuery { index_uid = "books", request = meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "moana" }, weight = 0.5, remote = "" })
    each one in meilisearch.MultiSearch(c, queries, err):
        println one.index_uid, one.hits.len()
    end
    fed := meilisearch.FederatedSearch(c, queries, meilisearch.Federation { offset = 0, limit = 20, page = -1, hits_per_page = -1, facets_by_index = `{"movies": ["genre"]}`, merge_facets = `{}` }, err)
    println fed.hits.len()

    mut fr := meilisearch.FacetSearchRequest { facet_name = "genre", facet_query = "dra", query = "space", filter = "year > 2000", matching_strategy = meilisearch.MATCH_ALL, exhaustive_facet_count = true }
    fr.attributes_to_search_on.push("title")
    fs := meilisearch.FacetSearch(c, "movies", fr, err)
    println fs.facet_query, fs.processing_time_ms
    each h in fs.hits:
        println h.value, h.count
    end

    mut sr := meilisearch.SimilarRequest { id = "143", embedder = "default", limit = 5, offset = 0, filter = "year > 2000", show_ranking_score = true, show_ranking_score_details = false, ranking_score_threshold = 0.5, retrieve_vectors = false }
    sr.attributes_to_retrieve.push("title")
    println meilisearch.SimilarDocuments(c, "movies", sr, err).hits.len()

    mut more := meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "space", show_performance_details = true, use_network = false, personalize = `{"userContext": "likes old films"}`, inline_rule = `{"actions": {"pin": [{"id": "1", "position": 0}]}}` }
    more.locales.push("eng")
    detailed := meilisearch.Search(c, "movies", more, err)
    println detailed.request_uid, detailed.performance_details, detailed.query_vector, detailed.remote_errors, detailed.metadata, detailed.facets_by_index
    mut fq := meilisearch.FacetSearchRequest { facet_name = "genre", ranking_score_threshold = 0.1, hybrid_embedder = "default", hybrid_semantic_ratio = 0.5, media = "", use_network = false }
    fq.locales.push("eng")
    fq.vector.push(0.2)
    println meilisearch.FacetSearch(c, "movies", fq, err).remote_errors
    mut posq := Vector {} as Vector<meilisearch.MultiQuery>
    posq.push(meilisearch.MultiQuery { index_uid = "movies", request = meilisearch.SearchRequest { query = "up" }, query_position = 0 })
    println meilisearch.FederatedSearch(c, posq, meilisearch.Federation { distinct = "studio", personalize = "", show_performance_details = true }, err).hits.len()
    println meilisearch.SimilarDocuments(c, "movies", meilisearch.SimilarRequest { id = "1", embedder = "default", show_performance_details = true }, err).hits.len()
end
```

### `SearchResult`

```salam
struct SearchResult
```

The answer to a search. Numbers the server did not send are -1.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index_uid` | `str = ""` | The index, in multi-search results. |
| `hits` | `Vector` | Each hit as its own JSON text; read them into structs with `HitsAs`. |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query that was run. |
| `processing_time_ms` | `i64 = 0` | How long the search took, in milliseconds. |
| `offset` | `i64 = -1` | How many hits were skipped. |
| `limit` | `i64 = -1` | The page size. |
| `estimated_total_hits` | `i64 = -1` | About how many documents match. |
| `page` | `i64 = -1` | The page number, with numbered pages. |
| `hits_per_page` | `i64 = -1` | The hits on each page. |
| `total_hits` | `i64 = -1` | Exactly how many documents match, with numbered pages. |
| `total_pages` | `i64 = -1` | How many pages there are. |
| `facet_distribution` | `str = ""` | The value counts of the requested facets, as raw JSON. |
| `facet_stats` | `str = ""` | The minimum and maximum of numeric facets, as raw JSON. |
| `semantic_hit_count` | `i64 = -1` | How many hits came from meaning rather than keywords. |
| `performance_details` | `str = ""` | How long each step took, as raw JSON. |
| `query_vector` | `str = ""` | The vector the query was turned into, as raw JSON. |
| `remote_errors` | `str = ""` | Errors from other instances of a sharded network, as raw JSON. |
| `request_uid` | `str = ""` | The id of this search request. |
| `metadata` | `str = ""` | Extra information about the query, as raw JSON. |
| `facets_by_index` | `str = ""` | The facets of each index, in a federated search. |
| `raw` | `str = ""` | The whole response body. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-meilisearch-Search.salam

### `Version`

```salam
struct Version
```

The server version.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkg_version` | `str = ""` | The version, such as `1.15.2`. |
| `commit_sha` | `str = ""` | The commit the server was built from. |
| `commit_date` | `str = ""` | The date of that commit. |

db-meilisearch-Client.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.WithAgent(meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey"), "my-app/1.0")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}
    if not meilisearch.IsHealthy(c):
        println "Meilisearch is not reachable at " + c.host
        ret
    end
    println meilisearch.Health(c, err), meilisearch.VERSION

    v := meilisearch.GetVersion(c, err)
    println v.pkg_version, v.commit_sha, v.commit_date
    st := meilisearch.GetStats(c, err)
    println st.database_size, st.used_database_size, st.last_update, st.indexes

    dump := meilisearch.CreateDump(c, err)
    println dump.task_uid, meilisearch.CreateSnapshot(c, err).status
    println meilisearch.GetExperimentalFeatures(c, err)
    println meilisearch.UpdateExperimentalFeatures(c, `{"metrics": true}`, err)
    println meilisearch.GetMetrics(c, err).len()
    println meilisearch.GetNetwork(c, err)
    println meilisearch.UpdateNetwork(c, `{"self": "ms-0"}`, err)
    println meilisearch.Export(c, `{"url": "http://backup:7700", "apiKey": "key"}`, err).kind

    body := meilisearch.Request(c, "GET", "/indexes?limit=1", "", err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        println err.status, err.code, err.kind, err.message, err.link
        ret
    end
    println body
    println meilisearch.RequestAs(c, "POST", "/indexes/movies/documents", "application/x-ndjson", "{\"id\": 1}\n", err)
    p := meilisearch.Page {}
    println p.results.len(), p.offset, p.limit, p.total, p.from, p.next, c.api_key.len() > 0, c.agent

    quick := meilisearch.WithTimeout(c, 2000)
    println quick.timeout_ms, meilisearch.IsHealthy(quick)
    tagged := meilisearch.WithMetadata(c, "nightly-import")
    println tagged.metadata
    println meilisearch.SetStderrLogs(c, "info", err)
    println meilisearch.RenderTemplate(c, `{"template": {"kind": "inlineDocumentTemplate", "inline": "{{doc.title}}"}, "input": {"kind": "inlineDocument", "inline": {"title": "Up"}}}`, err)
    println meilisearch.NetworkControl(c, `{"origin": {"remoteName": "ms-0", "taskUid": 1}, "message": {"type": "exportNoIndexForRemote", "remote": "ms-1"}}`, err)
end
```

### `Client`

### `SearchRule`

```salam
struct SearchRule
```

A dynamic search rule: when its conditions hold, its actions pin or boost documents.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uid` | `str = ""` | The rule name. |
| `last_updated_at` | `str = ""` | When it last changed. |
| `precedence` | `i64 = -1` | Which rule wins when several match; -1 when unset. |
| `active` | `bool = false` | It is on. |
| `conditions` | `str = ""` | When it applies, as raw JSON: a time range, query words or filter values. |
| `actions` | `str = ""` | What it does, as raw JSON: `pin` and `scale`. |
| `raw` | `str = ""` | The whole rule. |

db-meilisearch-UpdateSearchRule.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}
    meilisearch.UpdateExperimentalFeatures(c, `{"dynamicSearchRules": true}`, err)

    rule := `{"active": true, "precedence": 1, "conditions": {"query": {"words": "sale"}}, "actions": {"pin": [{"id": "42", "position": 0}]}}`
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.UpdateSearchRule(c, "black-friday", rule, err), err)
    r := meilisearch.GetSearchRule(c, "black-friday", err)
    println r.uid, r.active, r.precedence, r.last_updated_at, r.conditions, r.actions, r.raw.len()

    page := meilisearch.ListSearchRules(c, meilisearch.SearchRuleQuery { offset = 0, limit = 20, query = "sale", active = 1 }, err)
    println page.total, page.offset, page.limit
    each one in page.results:
        println one.uid
    end
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.DeleteSearchRule(c, "black-friday", err), err)
    meilisearch.Wait(c, meilisearch.DeleteAllSearchRules(c, err), err)
end
```

### `Webhook`

```salam
struct Webhook
```

A webhook: a URL Meilisearch calls each time a task finishes.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uuid` | `str = ""` | Its id. |
| `url` | `str = ""` | The URL called. |

db-meilisearch-CreateWebhook.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    hook := meilisearch.CreateWebhook(c, "https://example.com/meilisearch-hook", `{"Authorization": "Bearer hook-secret"}`, err)
    if not meilisearch.Ok(err):
        println meilisearch.ErrorString(err)
        ret
    end
    println hook.uuid, hook.url, hook.headers, hook.is_editable
    println meilisearch.GetWebhook(c, hook.uuid, err).url
    println meilisearch.UpdateWebhook(c, hook.uuid, "https://example.com/v2/hook", "", err).url
    each w in meilisearch.ListWebhooks(c, err):
        println w.uuid, w.url
    end
    println meilisearch.DeleteWebhook(c, hook.uuid, err)
end
```

### `TaskInfo`

```salam
struct TaskInfo
```

The receipt of a change. Meilisearch applies every write later, in order; wait for it with `Wait`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task_uid` | `i64 = -1` | The task number; -1 when the call failed. |
| `index_uid` | `str = ""` | The index it changes, if any. |
| `status` | `str = ""` | The status when it was queued. |
| `kind` | `str = ""` | The task type, such as `documentAdditionOrUpdate`. |
| `enqueued_at` | `str = ""` | When it was queued. |
| `custom_metadata` | `str = ""` | The metadata the write was tagged with. |

db-meilisearch-GetTasks.salam

```salam
import db.meilisearch

func main:
    c := meilisearch.New("http://127.0.0.1:7700", "masterKey")
    mut err := meilisearch.Error {}

    info := meilisearch.DeleteIndex(c, "old_movies", err)
    t := meilisearch.WaitForTask(c, info.task_uid, 30000, 100, err)
    println t.uid, t.batch_uid, t.index_uid, t.status, t.kind, t.canceled_by, t.details, t.duration
    println t.enqueued_at, t.started_at, t.finished_at
    if t.status == meilisearch.STATUS_FAILED:
        println t.error.code, t.error.message
    end
    println meilisearch.GetTask(c, info.task_uid, err).status

    mut q := meilisearch.TaskQuery { limit = 20, from = -1, reverse = true, after_enqueued_at = "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z" }
    q.statuses.push(meilisearch.STATUS_SUCCEEDED)
    q.statuses.push(meilisearch.STATUS_FAILED)
    q.index_uids.push("movies")
    q.types.push("documentAdditionOrUpdate")
    q.uids.push(1)
    q.batch_uids.push(1)
    q.canceled_by.push(2)
    q.before_enqueued_at = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    q.before_started_at = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    q.after_started_at = "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    q.before_finished_at = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    q.after_finished_at = "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    page := meilisearch.GetTasks(c, q, err)
    println page.total, page.limit, page.from, page.next
    each task in page.results:
        println task.uid, task.kind, task.status
    end

    mut pending := meilisearch.TaskQuery {}
    pending.statuses.push(meilisearch.STATUS_ENQUEUED)
    pending.statuses.push(meilisearch.STATUS_PROCESSING)
    println meilisearch.CancelTasks(c, pending, err).task_uid
    mut finished := meilisearch.TaskQuery {}
    finished.statuses.push(meilisearch.STATUS_CANCELED)
    println meilisearch.DeleteTasks(c, finished, err).task_uid

    batches := meilisearch.GetBatches(c, meilisearch.TaskQuery { limit = 5 }, err)
    println batches.total, batches.limit, batches.from, batches.next
    each b in batches.results:
        one := meilisearch.GetBatch(c, b.uid, err)
        println one.uid, one.batch_strategy, one.details, one.stats, one.progress, one.duration, one.started_at, one.finished_at
    end

    println t.custom_metadata, t.network, info.custom_metadata
    println meilisearch.GetTaskDocuments(c, info.task_uid, err)
    comp := meilisearch.CompactTasks(c, err)
    println comp.status, comp.pre_size, comp.post_size, comp.action_required, comp.error_message
end
```
